@import '@jini-ai/ui/admin-widgets.css';
/* Keep Tovu's link colour and text size when widgets are imported directly from Jini. */
@import './styles/see-more.css';
 
/* Installed Tovu admin themes. Compatibility tokens precede classic so its scoped values win. */
@import './styles/admin-theme-bridge.css';
@import './admin-themes/classic/admin.css';
@import './admin-themes/glass/admin.css';
 
:root {
  /* Tells the browser which palette to draw NATIVE controls in — checkbox/radio boxes, the select
     popup, scrollbars, date pickers. Without it they stay light-drawn under the dark tokens (white
     checkboxes on a near-black card). `accent-color` still paints the checked state on top. */
  color-scheme: light;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] { color-scheme: dark; }
 
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-ui); background: var(--jini-app-bg, var(--bg)); color: var(--fg); -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; }
a { color: var(--link); text-decoration: none; }
a:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; }
/* A control that looks like a link but is a real `<button>`, for actions that reveal something
   in place rather than navigate (Users' username opens that row's Manage panel). An `<a href="#">`
   would read as navigation to assistive tech and to anyone watching the status bar, so the
   element stays a button and only the appearance is borrowed — matching the `a` rules directly
   above, including the hover underline, so the two are indistinguishable on screen. Strips the
   UA button chrome that would otherwise draw a bordered box around the text; the global focus
   ring below still applies, since this is still a button.
 
   Used by Users' username and Members' email toggle — both sections, not editors, which is why
   this lives here and not in a screen-scoped partial. Two identical definitions of this class were
   written in parallel by different authors; this is the merged one, and it keeps the more complete
   property list of the two. */
.link-button {
  background: none; border: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; text-align: left;
  font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-weight: inherit; letter-spacing: normal;
  color: var(--link); cursor: pointer; text-decoration: none;
}
/* `opacity: 1` overrides the bare `button:hover` dim — this control signals hover by underlining,
   the way `a:hover` does, not by fading. */
.link-button:hover { opacity: 1; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; }
 
/* Skip link — off-screen (not `display: none`/`visibility: hidden`, both of which would also
   remove it from the tab order and defeat the point) until it receives keyboard focus, at which
   point it becomes the first visible thing on the page. `top: -100%` rather than `left: -9999px`
   so it cannot introduce horizontal scroll on the way in — an off-canvas element still
   participates in `scrollWidth` on some engines if it is offset in X, not Y. */
.skip-link {
  position: fixed; top: -100%; left: var(--space-3); z-index: 100;
  background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-ink);
  padding: 0.6rem 1rem; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 600;
  transition: top 0.15s ease;
}
.skip-link:focus {
  top: var(--space-3);
  outline: 2px solid var(--primary-ink); outline-offset: 2px;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .skip-link { transition: none; }
}
/* Bare `button` is the filled primary CTA — burnt orange, per the user's swatch (see the
   `--primary` token comment above for the measured-contrast reasoning). This is the app-wide
   default specifically so every section keeps a working, accessible primary action without
   individually opting in; it is why `.btn-secondary`/`.btn-ghost`/`.btn-danger` below exist as
   deliberate *opt-outs* for a screen's non-primary actions, rather than the other way around.
   One primary per screen is a per-section discipline the class names cannot enforce by
   themselves — Posts/Media apply it explicitly (see those files); `/admin/users` and
   `/admin/redirects` were spot-checked after this change and still read correctly since neither
   screen has more than one bare button competing for attention. */
/* `.btn-*` classes are listed here too (not just below) so an element carrying one of them gets
   this SHAPE — radius/padding/font/cursor/transition — regardless of whether it's a real
   `<button>` or something else (an `<a>` styled to look like a button, e.g. Dashboard's
   "View site ↗"). Safe to add: the variant rules further down only set `background`/`color`/
   `border-color`, all at the same (0,1,0) specificity as their entry in this selector list, and
   they sit later in the file — same-specificity ties resolve by source order, so they still win
   for color regardless of this rule also matching. See the `a.btn-*` block below this one for
   the anchor-specific fixes (`display`, `text-decoration`) a bare shape rule can't provide. */
button,
.btn-secondary, .btn-ghost, .btn-danger, .btn-warning, .btn-primary, .btn-explore {
  background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-ink); border: 1px solid transparent;
  border-radius: var(--r-sm); padding: 0.5rem 0.95rem; cursor: pointer;
  font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  transition: opacity 0.14s, box-shadow 0.14s;
}
button:hover { opacity: 0.88; }
/* Neutral, not a tint of the primary. The previous fill (`color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 30%,
   var(--surface))`, plus an `in srgb` dark-mode `.btn-primary` override) is what the owner read as a
   washed-out peach/pink Save button (2026-09-26); a disabled action should read as calmly
   unavailable, not as a faded brand colour. Token-only, so it tracks light and dark with no
   per-theme arm and no colour mixing (which also retires the oklch hue-arc trap the old mix had to
   work around). This is the filled treatment — bare `<button>`, `.btn-primary`, `.btn-explore`; the
   outline variants (`.btn-secondary`/`-ghost`/`-danger`/`-warning`) carry their own `:disabled`
   rules next to their base rules below. (0,1,1) still beats every class-only base rule's fill.
   Older comments elsewhere in the admin CSS that describe a "peach"/primary-tinted global disabled
   fill are describing the retired mix; the scoped overrides they justify are still valid. */
button:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 1;
  background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted);
}
/* ============================================================
   FORM CONTROLS — the control layer. Previously two bare-element rules total (this block's old
   `input, select { ... }` plus a `:focus` override); rebuilt against Open Design's own reference
   (`od-settings-external-mcp-customform.png`, `ADS-memory/.local-artifacts/handoff/od-parity-
   20260731/`) rather than invented — height, radius, border weight, and the label idiom below
   are measured off that screenshot, not guessed. Global base rule stays global on purpose (every
   input in every section gets the refreshed metrics/focus ring for free); the `.field*`
   primitives further down are additive and opt-in, so sections that lay inputs out inline
   (Redirects' filter row, menu-item rows) keep their existing sizing/flex behavior untouched.
   ============================================================ */
input, select, textarea {
  padding: 0.55rem 0.7rem; border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-control-border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-sm); background: var(--jini-control-bg); color: var(--fg);
  min-height: 37px; box-sizing: border-box;
  transition: border-color 0.14s, box-shadow 0.14s;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-inset, none);
}
input:where(:not(:focus):not(:disabled)):hover,
select:where(:not(:focus):not(:disabled)):hover,
textarea:where(:not(:focus):not(:disabled)):hover {
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-hover, none);
}
textarea { min-height: 5.5rem; line-height: 1.5; resize: vertical; }
input::placeholder, textarea::placeholder { color: var(--faint); }
/* Focus ring, not just a border-color swap — the previous `:focus { outline: none; border-color:
   ... }` killed the browser's own indicator and replaced it with a 1px color change, which is a
   weak affordance (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 wants a visible, non-color-only state change). This adds a
   real ring back on the token system instead of relying on the browser default. */
input:focus, select:focus, textarea:focus {
  outline: none; border-color: var(--primary); box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-focus);
}
 
/* Select — style the trigger, leave the native popup alone (its internals are not stylable
   cross-browser; faking a custom listbox to get around that trades one set of a11y/behavior bugs
   for another). `appearance: none` removes the OS-drawn arrow so the custom chevron below can
   replace it without doubling up; metrics match the text-input rule above so a `TRANSPORT` select
   sits flush next to an `ID` input, per the OD reference. Two chevron images (not one +
   `currentColor`) because `background-image` data URIs can't read a custom property — light and
   dark each get one baked to that theme's `--muted` hex. */
select:not(:where([class*="tsqd"] select, [class*="tsqd"])) {
  appearance: none; -webkit-appearance: none; -moz-appearance: none;
  padding-right: 2.25rem; cursor: pointer;
  background-image: var(--jini-control-chevron-image);
  background-repeat: no-repeat; background-position: right 0.7rem center; background-size: 14px;
}
select:not(:where([class*="tsqd"] select, [class*="tsqd"]))::-ms-expand { display: none; }
:root[data-theme="dark"] select:not(:where([class*="tsqd"] select, [class*="tsqd"])) {
  background-image: var(--jini-control-chevron-image);
}
 
/* Checkboxes/radios previously had no rule of their own at all — not broken (the browser's UA
   stylesheet's own `input[type="checkbox"]` selector already out-specifies the page's bare
   `input`, so they were never forced into the padded/bordered text-input box; verified via
   computed style before writing this comment), just entirely unstyled 13px OS defaults with no
   connection to the token system. `accent-color` is the sanctioned lightweight way to recolor a
   native checkbox/radio's checked state without rebuilding it as a custom widget. */
input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"] {
  width: 16px; height: 16px; min-height: 0; padding: 0;
  accent-color: var(--primary); cursor: pointer; flex-shrink: 0;
}
 
/* Field primitives — label -> control -> hint/error, and the two-column short-field grid, both
   modeled on the OD custom-form reference. Opt-in (`.field`/`.field-row`/`.field-group`), so nothing
   outside what explicitly adopts them changes size or layout. */
.field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; }
.field input, .field select, .field textarea { width: 100%; }
.field-label {
  font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted);
}
.field-hint { font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); margin: 0; }
.field-error { font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--danger); margin: 0; }
.site-admin-login-hint strong { color: var(--fg); font-weight: 600; }
.site-admin-login-hint .info-tip { margin-left: 0.25rem; }
/* One click selects the whole starter password for copying. */
.site-admin-starter-password { font-family: var(--font-mono); user-select: all; }
/* Every masked secret field — `components/SecretInput` and the Jini ui-kit's password `TextField`
   (which wraps its whole `<label>` + input, toggle outside the label) — carries one eye toggle
   inside the input's right edge. The input is padded so long values never run under it; the
   button is a transparent 40px tap target centred on the ~37px input, so it overhangs invisibly
   instead of resizing the field. */
.jini-secret { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; }
.jini-secret input { width: 100%; padding-right: 2.75rem; }
.jini-secret-toggle {
  /* translateY, not a -20px margin: the phone-width 44px touch-target floor resizes the button. */
  position: absolute; top: 50%; right: 0; width: 40px; height: 40px; min-height: 0; margin: 0; transform: translateY(-50%);
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  background: none; border: 0; box-shadow: none; padding: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm); color: var(--muted); cursor: pointer;
}
.jini-secret > label + .jini-secret-toggle { top: auto; bottom: -1.5px; margin: 0; transform: none; }
.jini-secret-toggle:hover:not(:disabled), .jini-secret-toggle:focus-visible { color: var(--accent-text); background: none; }
.jini-secret-toggle:focus-visible { outline-offset: -5px; }
.jini-secret-toggle:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }
/* Short fields pair into a row (OD: ID + TRANSPORT); long ones (COMMAND, ARGS, ENV) are not
   wrapped in `.field-row` at all and stay full-width — the grid is opt-in per field, not a
   blanket two-column layout. */
.field-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(10rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-4); }
/* Baseline alignment when one cell's label wraps and its neighbours' don't is handled by
   `styles/forms.css`'s `.field-row { align-items: end }` override, which carries the reasoning
   and the measured evidence. Do not add a second mechanism here. */
/* Vertical rhythm: ~4px label-to-control (the `.field` gap above) vs. group-to-group below —
   roughly a 4-5x ratio, matching the OD reference. This ratio, more than any single spacing
   value, is what reads as "organized" rather than "cramped everywhere alike". */
.field-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4); }
.field-group + .field-group { margin-top: var(--space-5); }
/* Command/args/env-style fields signal "this expects code" the same way OD's does — a monospace
   placeholder (COMMAND: "e.g. npx, node, /path/to/binary"; ENV: "GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_..."), not
   decoration. Opt-in: most Tovu text fields (titles, alt text) are prose, not code. */
.field-mono, .field-mono::placeholder { font-family: var(--font-mono); }
/* A read-only value sitting where an input normally would (Media's demoted sha256 field) — same
   metrics as a real input (border/radius/padding/min-height) so it lines up with actual fields
   in the same `.field-group`, but rendered as a `<code>` rather than an `<input readOnly>` since
   there is nothing here for a cursor to land in or a value to submit. */
.field-readonly-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
.field-readonly {
  flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; white-space: nowrap;
  padding: 0.55rem 0.7rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  min-height: 37px; box-sizing: border-box; display: flex; align-items: center;
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2);
}
 
/* Unified label idiom — replaces four different ad hoc versions previously scattered across
   `.settings-value-editor label` / `.integrations-form label` / `.collections-dynamic-field
   label` / `.login-card label` (each its own font-size/weight/color). Those per-section rules
   still exist below (out of this pass's file-scope to touch every caller) but `.field-label`
   above is the one new code should reach for; `.settings-layer-label` already used this exact
   uppercase/letterspaced/muted idiom elsewhere in the file, so this is a consolidation onto an
   existing pattern, not a new invention. */
 
/* Visible keyboard focus on every interactive primitive (buttons, links, and the new drawer
   toggle/close controls below) — WCAG 2.1 AA requires a focus indicator, and the bare `button`
   rule above does not set one of its own. Inputs/selects already get one via border-color above;
   this covers everything else in one place instead of per-component rules. */
button:focus-visible, a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }
/* ONE ring colour for every focus-visible element, whichever stylesheet drew the ring: ~20
   component rules here and in `@jini-ai/ui`'s own CSS each name their own colour (`--accent-text`,
   `--jini-accent`, `--accent`, `--link` — all near-black or blue in this admin), so recolouring them
   one by one would drift again with the next component. `!important` on the colour only: width,
   offset and any rule that deliberately draws no outline (`outline: none`) are left to their own
   rules. `:focus-visible`, never `:focus` — a mouse click on a button or row draws no ring; Tab
   does. */
:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--focus-ring) !important; }
/* Programmatic focus targets, not controls: `<main>` takes focus from the skip link and the dock
   from its open effect (`tabIndex={-1}` on both, see `App.tsx`) so the NEXT Tab starts inside
   them. A ring around the whole page or the whole dock marks nothing actionable. */
#main-content:focus, .admin-chat-dock:focus { outline: none; }
 
/* InfoTip (`@jini-ai/ui/admin-widgets`, 2026-08-09) — a real tooltip, not the native `title`
   attribute: `title` was tried first and rejected live (owner feedback: too slow/inconsistent to
   notice, and the icon itself read as too small). Owner also asked for it to open ABOVE the
   trigger — that's unsafe with a plain CSS `position: absolute` bubble here, since this component's
   first real use sits inside a `<th>` in `.list-table`, which has its own `overflow: hidden` (there
   to clip the table's own rounded corners) and would clip an upward-opening bubble with no room
   above it. So the bubble is portaled straight into `document.body` (see the component) and
   positioned in JS via `getBoundingClientRect()` — `top`/`left` below are only the fixed-position
   base; the component sets the actual coordinates inline per-render. That sidesteps the clipping
   ancestor entirely rather than trading positions for the same bug. `pointer-events: none` keeps
   the bubble from ever intercepting the hover that reveals it in the first place. Colors are a
   literal white/black pairing (owner's explicit ask), not theme tokens — deliberately fixed
   regardless of light/dark mode, unlike the rest of this app's chrome. */
.info-tip { position: relative; display: inline-flex; margin-left: 0.35rem; vertical-align: middle; }
.info-tip-icon {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 1.1rem; height: 1.1rem; border-radius: 50%; color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer;
}
.info-tip:hover .info-tip-icon, .info-tip:focus-within .info-tip-icon { color: var(--accent-text); }
.info-tip-icon:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-text); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 50%; }
.info-tip-bubble {
  position: fixed; transform: translate(-50%, calc(-100% - 8px));
  width: max-content; max-width: min(18rem, calc(100vw - 16px)); padding: 0.55rem 0.75rem; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-bg); color: var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-text); font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 400;
  line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-shadow); border: 1px solid var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-border);
  pointer-events: none; z-index: 1000;
}
.info-tip-bubble::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; top: 100%; left: var(--info-tip-arrow-left, 50%); transform: translateX(-50%);
  border: 5px solid transparent; border-top-color: var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-bg);
}
/* Below-placement variant (`InfoTip.tsx`'s `ABOVE_HEADROOM_PX` fallback, 2026-08-11) — a trigger too
   close to the viewport top for the default above-opening bubble to fit flips to this instead. Same
   box, mirrored: `top: coords.bottom` (component) + `translateY(8px)` here opens downward with the
   same 8px gap the default has, and the arrow moves from the bubble's bottom edge to its top edge,
   pointing back up at the icon it flipped away from. */
/* "• " lines (`infoTipLines`, e.g. the dock's one Tool calls tip): wrapped text hangs past its dot. */
.info-tip-line { display: block; }
.info-tip-bullet { display: flex; gap: 0.4em; }
.info-tip-bullet + .info-tip-bullet { margin-top: 0.3em; }
.info-tip-bullet > span:first-child { flex: none; }
.info-tip-bubble-below { transform: translate(-50%, 8px); }
.info-tip-bubble-below::after {
  top: auto; bottom: 100%; border-top-color: transparent; border-bottom-color: var(--jini-overlay-tooltip-bg);
}
 
/* Page headings + intro copy */
.admin-content h1 { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.65rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--fg); margin: 0 0 0.4rem; }
.admin-content h1 + p { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.95rem; margin: 0 0 1.6rem; }
 
/* ============================================================
   Shared page primitives (canary pass: Posts + Media adopt these now; phase 2 migrates the
   remaining ~30 sections onto the same set instead of leaving `.admin-content h1` above as the
   only shared pattern). Reproduces Settings' measured qualities — kicker/title/description
   header, bordered card with real padding, restrained button hierarchy — using this file's own
   oklch tokens and the scale above, never `--jini-*`.
   ============================================================ */
 
.page { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-6); }
/* Workspace screen measure — `.page` itself carries no max-width anywhere in the app (~39 call
   sites: tables, side-by-side card grids, and other layouts that legitimately want the full
   column), so a cap belongs on a scoped wrapper class, not the shared shell. Workspace is a single-
   column settings form; at a wide viewport it ran edge-to-edge with the card boxes stretching to
   fill leftover space and no readable measure of their own. */
.workspace-page { max-width: var(--form-measure); }
 
/* Form measure (2026-09-06, owner: "excessively long cards" — Roles › Policies, Source Control,
   Workspace, Redirects, Database › Timeline). The ONE width decision every single-column form
   surface now shares, as a token (`--form-measure`, in the token block above) so the screens
   cannot drift apart again.
 
   Measured live at 1440 (`getBoundingClientRect`, 1300px page column) before changing anything:
     - Roles › Policies: a `.notice.integrations-form` 1300px wide holding two 448px inputs.
     - Redirects: a `form.card` 1300px wide, and a `details.notice` 1300px wide around the two
       words "Bulk import".
     - Source Control: three accordion rows 1300px wide; the expanded token input was 1226px.
     - Workspace: already capped at 42rem (`.workspace-page` above, 2026-08-31) — but its inputs
       stayed at 28rem, so a third of the box was still empty, and the ID/Created chips stacked
       because the form's `align-items: flex-start` shrink-wrapped their `auto-fit` grid to one
       column. The owner flagged it in that state, which is what settled "controls fill" below.
   None of these render through one primitive (`.notice`, `.card`, a `<details>`, a per-tab
   wrapper), so the shared fix is a shared class + token applied at each site, not a cap on
   `.card` or `.notice` — both of those also wrap tables, banners and side-by-side grids that
   legitimately want the whole column (`.page` carries no max-width for the same reason, see
   `.workspace-page`'s own note above).
 
   42rem is not a new number: it is the measure already accepted on the two screens the owner
   asked to fix most recently — `.workspace-page` and `/admin/seo`'s `--seo-measure` — and it sits
   inside the 40–46rem band every other deliberate form column here uses (`.onboarding` 40rem,
   `.access-tokens-row` 40rem, `.settings-ui-section--page-flow` 46rem).
 
   A definite measure, not `fit-content`: `.integrations-form label` is `width: 100%`, and a
   percentage inside a shrink-wrapped parent resolves against the children rather than the column,
   so a fit-to-content box would collapse to the input's intrinsic ~11rem. The container has to be
   the definite thing and the controls fill it.
 
   Controls FILL the measure: `.integrations-form label`'s own 28rem cap is lifted inside a
   measured form. The point of the pass is a box no wider than what it holds, and a 42rem box
   around a 28rem input is the same complaint at two-thirds scale. 42rem minus the box's padding
   is the ~40rem control width the SEO defaults form already ships with, so the two rhyme.
 
   Inside the measure a `.field-row` goes two-up, not four-up: the shared `minmax(10rem, 1fr)`
   packs three 10rem columns into the 624px that remain and orphans the fourth field beneath them
   (Redirects' Match type / From / To / Status code). 14rem tracks give two 19rem columns at this
   width and fall back to one column below ~29rem — and a row of two is what reads as a form
   rather than a spreadsheet at this measure. (0,2,0) so it beats the (0,1,0) base rule wherever
   the bundler puts this file. */
.form-measure { max-width: var(--form-measure); }
.form-measure.integrations-form label { max-width: none; }
/* Workspace's ID/Created chips (`.settings-layer-grid` inside the form) span the measured box so
   the `auto-fit` grid has a width to fit into — see the Workspace bullet above. */
.form-measure.integrations-form > .settings-layer-grid { align-self: stretch; }
.form-measure .field-row { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr)); }
 
/* The Database › Timeline filter bar is the one flagged surface that is a TOOLBAR, not a form
   column: five controls with intrinsic widths (a select, a text input, two date inputs, a button —
   ~815px in a row at 1440) that need no measure to fill. Capped at `--form-measure` it would wrap
   the last two onto a second line inside a 672px box; hugging its row is the same decision — a
   box no wider than what it holds — expressed for controls that already have a width of their
   own. `max-width: 100%` hands control back to `.toolbar`'s own `flex-wrap` once the column is
   narrower than the row. */
.database-filter-bar { width: fit-content; max-width: 100%; }
 
/* Kicker + title + description on the left, actions on the right — mirrors the measured
   Settings triad (11px kicker / 26px title / 13px description) instead of a bare <h1>. */
.page-header {
  display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--space-4); flex-wrap: wrap;
}
.page-header-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; min-width: 0; }
/* One row of page-level actions under the header: leading links sit left, everything after them is
   pushed to the far right by the auto margin on the first button. Wraps rather than overflowing on
   narrow viewports, at which point the auto margin collapses and the button simply follows the link. */
.page-toolbar {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3);
  flex-wrap: wrap; margin: var(--space-3) 0;
}
.page-toolbar > button:first-of-type { margin-left: auto; }
/* Phones (mobile catalog TH-1, 2026-10-06): once the row wraps, the auto margin parked "Rescan
   themes" at the right edge opposite "View site" and left "Turn the theme off" alone below — three
   scattered rows. Left-aligned like the header's own actions, it reads as one group; the row's own
   margin goes too, since `.page`'s gap already separates it from the header. */
/* D-31: the FAB also overlays list actions at 800px. A scrollable spacer lets the last row clear
   it without forcing a short flex pane taller than the viewport. Sheet-specific rules below
   override this on phones. Fixed-height settings panels need their own scroll clearance. Skills
   (and Agent Plugins, AP-3) is excluded: it reuses `.settings-ui-section` but sits in page flow at natural height
   (`skills.css`, D-32), so the spacer above already clears it — a second 88px pushed its footer
   note away from the list. The spacer stays when the dock is open: the FAB is gone then, but the
   scroll ↑/↓ pair still sits in the column's corner and would cover the last row. */
@media (min-width: 641px) {
  .admin-content::after {
    content: ""; display: block; flex-shrink: 0; height: var(--assistant-clearance);
  }
  .admin-layout:not(:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open)) .settings-ui-section:not(.settings-ui-section--page-flow):not(.skills-page, .agent-plugins-section) .jini-tabbed-dialog-content {
    padding-bottom: var(--assistant-clearance);
  }
}
 
/* Container, not viewport (2026-10-11): the toolbar wraps whenever the PAGE is narrow — phone, or
   desktop with the nav expanded and the dock open — so the same left-aligned grouping applies.
   620px ≈ the old 640px viewport minus a phone's 2 × 12px page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .page-toolbar { margin-block: 0; }
  .page-toolbar > button:first-of-type { margin-left: 0; }
}
/* Card action row: the Activate switch stays left, the Explore/Duplicate icon group is pushed to the
   right edge. `align-items` centers the short switch against the taller icon buttons. */
.theme-card-actions {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
  gap: var(--space-2); flex-wrap: wrap;
}
/* Explore was solid blue (commit 8a7169b, same day) so it read as a second filled CTA distinct from
   Activate's burnt orange. Reversed on owner feedback: two solid-filled buttons of different hues
   still compete for primary attention instead of establishing one. Explore is the secondary action
   here, so it now takes the app's existing secondary/outline shape (`.btn-secondary`'s
   `--surface`/`--border-strong` pairing, same idiom as the plain-white `<input>` fields) instead of
   a bespoke fill — `--surface` computes to true white and `--fg` to near-black in light mode (see
   those tokens' own definitions above), and both flip correctly under a dark skin without this rule
   knowing it happened. `--fg` rather than `.btn-secondary`'s dimmer `--fg-2`: the owner asked for
   "black text" by name, and a button label is high-emphasis actionable text, not the muted
   secondary prose `--fg-2` is for. No `color-mix` against `--surface` here — that chroma-0 token
   already broke one blend on this exact button (see the `.theme-card button.btn-explore` override
   below); flat token assignments sidestep the hue-interpolation trap entirely. Border makes it read
   as a button against the equally-white card, not as plain text — `button:focus-visible`'s app-wide
   `--accent-text` ring (styles.css, global rules) already resolves dark-on-white in light mode and
   light-on-dark in dark mode, so no button-specific focus override is needed either. */
/* INVERTED 2026-08-11, third and final iteration on this button: blue fill (8a7169b) -> white
   surface with a black outline -> solid black fill with white text, on owner instruction ("make the
   explore button white text black background"). The outline step was a way-point, not the
   destination: it fixed Explore competing with Activate for primary attention, but the owner's wider
   goal is fewer hues overall ("I just wanna have some basic colors. I think I have too many
   colors"). A neutral black fill reads as a strong action without introducing a fourth hue next to
   Activate's burnt orange and the green Active pill.
 
   `--fg`/`--surface` rather than literal black/white, and deliberately inverted from the pair above:
   both tokens already know which theme is active, so under a dark skin this becomes a light button
   with dark text — still a high-contrast filled control against a dark card, with no `@media`
   branch. A hardcoded `#000` background would swallow itself on a dark surface.
 
   Border is `var(--fg)` explicitly, NOT `currentColor`: `currentColor` now resolves to the white
   `--surface` text, which would ring a black button in white and read as a gap against the card.
   Matching the background keeps the box metrics identical to the outlined version it replaces.
 
   Still no `color-mix` against `--surface` — that chroma-0 token already broke one blend on this
   exact button (see the `.theme-card button.btn-explore` override below). Flat token assignments
   sidestep the hue-interpolation trap. Hover moves to `--fg-2`, which is dimmer than `--fg` in BOTH
   modes, so the state change is visible either way rather than only in light. */
.btn-explore { background: var(--fg); color: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--fg); }
.btn-explore:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--fg-2); border-color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1; }
.btn-explore:disabled { border-color: transparent; }
 
/* Explore's subtitle used to inherit the shared `.page-header .page-description` 60ch prose measure
   (above) unscoped, which still ran most of the page's width at this screen's typical container size
   — 60ch is sized for genuinely long copy elsewhere (Settings, Pages), not this one-sentence caption.
   Capped tighter here, to roughly a third of the page per owner feedback ("it's currently wrapping
   across nearly the full page width"). `ch`, not a viewport percentage, for the same reason the
   shared rule already uses it: it tracks the font's own measure rather than the container, so it
   reads as "about a third" at the widths this screen is actually used at without recomputing per
   breakpoint. Three classes deep (`.theme-explore-header.page-header .page-description`, specificity
   0,3,0) to unambiguously outrank the shared 0,2,0 rule regardless of source order — the same
   "re-assert one class higher" pattern `.theme-card button.btn-primary` below already uses to beat a
   tied/lower-specificity shared rule. */
.theme-explore-header.page-header .page-description { max-width: 34ch; }
 
/* Explore screen: the file picker tray on top, then the toolbar and preview at full width (owner,
   2026-10-11: "the file list that's on the left, make that up top ... it's way too small right now
   when the assistant chat is open"). It was a 190px sidebar beside the editor, which with the chat
   dock open left the preview a ~200px thumbnail. `minmax(0, 1fr)` on the single column rather than a
   bare `1fr` — without it a wide `<pre>`/`<textarea>` sets the column's min-content width and pushes
   the grid past its box instead of scrolling inside its own.
   `container-type` sits here, on this inner wrapper, so the rules below respond to the width this
   screen really gets (side nav and chat dock open or not), not the viewport. Not on `.page`:
   containment makes the container the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants, and this
   screen's toasts render as `.page` children. */
.theme-explore {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
  gap: var(--space-4);
  container-type: inline-size; container-name: theme-explore;
}
/* SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11 (owner: "it's taking up too much space... just show 'You're editing your
   own copy' and then a tooltip icon"): `.theme-explore-directions` used to be a bordered `.notice`
   block here, capped to half the page ("it spans the whole page, which is just unnecessary and
   disgusting"), sitting full-width between the header and the file list. It's gone — the same
   reassurance now renders as `.theme-explore-copy-tip` inside the header's own actions column (see
   `.theme-explore-header-actions` below, and the JSX comment above `ThemeExplore`'s `.page-header`
   for the full quote). No width cap needed on the replacement: it's one line of text plus an icon,
   not a wrapping paragraph. */
 
/* Stacks the ← All themes / Save / Reset button row (`.page-actions`, unchanged) above the collapsed
   copy-tip line, both right-aligned under the header. `margin-left: auto` (not just the parent
   `.page-header`'s `justify-content: space-between`) is what keeps this column pinned to the right
   edge even when `.page-header` wraps it onto its own line below the title at narrow widths — with
   only one flex item left on that wrapped line, `space-between` alone has nothing to distribute it
   against and would otherwise leave it flush left. Auto margins are resolved per flex LINE, so this
   keeps working whether the column shares a row with the title or has fallen to a row of its own. */
.theme-explore-header-actions { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; gap: 0.4rem; margin-left: auto; }
/* Back arrow | centred title | Saved/Reset (owner, 2026-10-11: "center the title section ... just make
   it a back arrow to the left"). A grid with equal `1fr` rails, not the flex row above: flex would
   centre the title only in the space left over, and the wider actions column would push it left of
   true centre — the same reason `.page-header-split` below is a grid. Not that modifier itself:
   `.page:has(.page-header-split)` turns `.page` into a size container, and that containment makes
   `.page` the containing block for this screen's `position: fixed` toasts. The rails keep grid's
   `auto` minimum, so when the chat dock squeezes the page the actions column keeps its width and
   the title drifts off-centre instead of overlapping it. Three classes deep (0,3,0) for the same
   reason as the subtitle rule above. */
.theme-explore-header.page-header {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr minmax(0, 2fr) 1fr; align-items: start;
}
.theme-explore-header.page-header > .page-header-text { grid-column: 2; align-items: center; text-align: center; }
.theme-explore-header.page-header > .theme-explore-header-actions { grid-column: 3; justify-self: end; margin-left: 0; }
/* The Edit post/page back arrow (`.content-editor-back`, styles/editor.css) on a `<button>`: same
   size, colour and hover, with the app-wide `button` fill/padding reset away. */
.theme-explore-header.page-header > .theme-explore-back {
  grid-column: 1; justify-self: start;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 2rem; height: 2.4rem; margin-left: -0.35rem; padding: 0;
  border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm); background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2); cursor: pointer;
}
.theme-explore-header.page-header > .theme-explore-back:hover:not(:disabled) { background: transparent; color: var(--fg); opacity: 1; }
/* Phones: arrow and title share the first row (title centred between the arrow and an equal empty
   rail), Saved/Reset and the copy line drop to their own right-aligned row below. */
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .theme-explore-header.page-header { grid-template-columns: 2rem minmax(0, 1fr) 2rem; column-gap: var(--space-2); row-gap: var(--space-3); }
  .theme-explore-header.page-header > .theme-explore-header-actions { grid-column: 1 / -1; grid-row: 2; max-width: 100%; }
}
/* `white-space: nowrap` makes "one line" a guarantee rather than a hope: the visible text plus icon
   ("You're editing your own copy. ⓘ") is short enough to fit even at the narrowest viewport this
   header supports (measured at 390px), so there's no wrap-vs-truncate tradeoff to weigh here the way
   there was for the old block's full sentence. */
.theme-explore-copy-tip { margin: 0; font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
/* Phones: the shared 40px tap-target floor (`[role="button"]`, the P-3 block near the end of this
   file) grows the ~18px ⓘ to a 40x40 box with the glyph centred, which pushed this line ~20px under
   Saved/Reset and left the ⓘ ~11px past its text plus the box's own slack (Chrome check, 2026-10-11).
   Negative margins equal to that slack keep the 40px hit area but take it out of the layout, so the
   line sits right under the buttons with the ⓘ just after the text and flush with their right edge. */
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .theme-explore-copy-tip .info-tip-icon { margin: calc((1.1rem - 40px) / 2); }
}
/* Explore's no-stored-original banner (2026-10-08): message left, "Save as original" right, wrapping
   under the message on a narrow screen instead of squeezing it. */
.theme-explore-no-original { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-3); }
.theme-explore-no-original-action { display: inline-flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
/* The picker tray (`ThemeExploreFileList`): group tabs on top, the active group's files as wrapping
   chips below. In normal flow with no height cap and no scroller of its own, so the page wheel
   scrolls straight past it — the old sidebar's internal scroller stopped the wheel at its bottom
   edge. The 2026-08-11 sidebar trick (an absolutely-positioned `<nav>` in an empty grid cell, to
   borrow the preview column's height) and its 720px/640px fallbacks went with the column. */
.theme-explore-files {
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--surface);
}
/* Group tabs: quiet underline tabs, so they don't read as a second copy of the Preview/HTML segmented
   control just below. They wrap instead of scrolling sideways on a narrow screen, keeping every group
   one tap away with no hidden horizontal scroller. */
.theme-explore-groups {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0 var(--space-1);
  padding: 0 var(--space-2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.theme-explore-group {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px;
  margin-bottom: -1px; padding: 8px 10px 7px;
  border: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 0;
  background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2);
  font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 500;
}
.theme-explore-group:hover { background: transparent; color: var(--fg-1); opacity: 1; }
.theme-explore-group.is-active { color: var(--fg-1); font-weight: 600; border-bottom-color: var(--selected-ring); }
.theme-explore-group-count { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
/* A group's modified dot: same token and size as the per-file `.theme-explore-file-modified` below,
   so the two read as one signal. */
.theme-explore-group-modified { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--warning); }
.theme-explore-files-panel { padding: var(--space-2); }
.theme-explore-file-chips {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px;
  list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0;
}
/* "Show all (N)" / "Show fewer" under a long group (assets): a plain text button, not another chip,
   so it never reads as a file. */
.theme-explore-files-more {
  margin-top: var(--space-2); padding: 2px 4px;
  border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--link);
  font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 500;
}
.theme-explore-files-more:hover { background: transparent; text-decoration: underline; opacity: 1; }
/* One chip per file (`ThemeExploreFileRow`): the filename control (or its inline-rename replacement),
   the modified dot and the ⋮ overflow menu — 2026-08-11 owner ask (Copy/Rename). Flex, so the
   trigger sits fixed-width at the chip's end instead of forcing a second line under the name. The
   chip owns the border, fill and hover; the filename button inside stays transparent so the two
   never stack two tints. */
.theme-explore-file-row {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; max-width: 100%;
  padding-right: 2px;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--surface);
}
.theme-explore-file-row:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
.theme-explore-file-row.is-active { background: var(--accent-dim); border-color: var(--border-strong); }
/* `:not(.row-menu-trigger)` — without it this rule's specificity beats `.row-menu-trigger`'s own
   (0,1,0) (both are plain classes/type selectors, no cascade layers), so the ⋮ button inside a chip
   would inherit the filename's padding and ellipsis rather than staying the small round trigger
   every other row-actions menu in the app uses. `max-width` in `ch` stops one long asset name
   (`inter-latin-400-normal.woff2`) taking a whole row; the ellipsis plus the button's `title` (the
   full path) is the entire truncation implementation. */
.theme-explore-file-row > button:not(.row-menu-trigger) {
  display: block; flex: 0 1 auto; min-width: 0; max-width: 24ch;
  overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; text-align: left;
  padding: 4px 4px 4px 9px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2);
  font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 400; cursor: pointer;
}
.theme-explore-file-row > button:not(.row-menu-trigger):hover { background: transparent; opacity: 1; }
.theme-explore-file-row > button.is-active { color: var(--fg-1); font-weight: 600; }
/* Scaled down from the table row menu's 30px default to fit inside a chip. `flex-shrink: 0` plus the
   fixed width reserve this space in the chip's layout AT ALL TIMES — the `opacity` toggle below only
   ever changes visibility, never the box the chip is laid out around, so revealing the trigger can
   never resize the chip and reflow the whole wrapping row. */
.theme-explore-file-row .row-menu-trigger { width: 20px; height: 20px; flex-shrink: 0; opacity: 0; }
.theme-explore-file-row .row-menu-trigger svg { width: 13px; height: 13px; }
/* Modified marker (`ThemeExploreModifiedMarker`, 2026-09-12): a dot between the filename and the ⋮
   trigger for a file whose bytes differ from its catalog original. Fixed size plus `flex-shrink: 0`,
   so a long filename's ellipsis gives way instead of the dot. */
.theme-explore-file-modified {
  width: 6px; height: 6px; margin: 0 4px; flex-shrink: 0;
  border-radius: 50%; background: var(--warning);
}
/* Eight-plus always-visible ⋮ glyphs read as noise before an operator has touched anything — reveal
   on row hover, on the SELECTED file's own row (so working a file doesn't require re-hovering it to
   reach its menu), and on `:focus-within` rather than `:focus` on the trigger alone: `:focus` would
   never fire for a keyboard user tabbing toward it, since a `focus`-only rule requires the element
   to already be visible/reachable to look right, and `:focus-within` reveals the row the instant
   focus enters it, matching the mouse-hover behavior instead of trailing it. Also forced visible
   while the menu it opens is itself open (`aria-expanded`), so moving the pointer onto the portaled
   popup — which is not a descendant of this row, so `:hover`/`:focus-within` above cannot see it —
   does not make the trigger that opened it disappear underneath an open menu. */
.theme-explore-file-row:hover .row-menu-trigger,
.theme-explore-file-row:focus-within .row-menu-trigger,
.theme-explore-file-row.is-active .row-menu-trigger,
.theme-explore-file-row .row-menu-trigger[aria-expanded="true"] {
  opacity: 1;
}
/* Touch screens have no hover to reveal a chip's ⋮, and the phone tap-target floor (P-3, further
   down this file) grows every trigger to 40px: reserved blank space in every chip. There the ⋮ shows
   on the selected chip only (tap a file, then its ⋮). A selection change re-renders the tray anyway,
   so the hover-reflow reason for reserving the space above does not apply. */
@media (hover: none) {
  .theme-explore-file-row:not(.is-active) .row-menu-trigger:not([aria-expanded="true"]) { display: none; }
}
/* Takes over the filename button's slot and sizing while a rename is in progress, so double-clicking
   a name and typing over it reads as editing that same control rather than swapping to a visually
   unrelated one. */
.theme-explore-rename-input {
  flex: 0 1 auto; width: 22ch; min-width: 0;
  padding: 4px 7px; border: 1px solid var(--link); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg-1);
  font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.8rem;
}
.theme-explore-rename-input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-focus-subtle); }
.theme-explore-main { min-width: 0; }
/* `.page-editor-toolbar`'s shared 1rem top margin exists to separate it from the title/slug rows
   above it on `PageEditor.tsx` — the OTHER screen this class comes from. Here it is the first thing
   inside `.theme-explore-main`, so that margin pushed the Preview/HTML tabs a full line below the
   file list's "PAGES" heading, which starts flush with the grid's own top edge. Owner feedback
   2026-08-11: "make the pages title flush with preview and HTML tabs ... it just looks off." Scoped
   to this one context so `PageEditor`'s own spacing is untouched. Since the file tray moved above
   the toolbar (2026-10-11), `.theme-explore`'s own grid gap is the only space between the two. */
.theme-explore-main .page-editor-toolbar { margin-top: 0; }
/* Preview of a data/style/script file (2026-10-10, `ThemeExploreMainPane`): the shared `CodeView`
   at the HTML tab's own type size instead of the device-scaled iframe, which shrank Chrome's raw
   JSON viewer to unreadable. Same gutter/wrap rules as `.template-source-modal`'s viewer below; the
   code box is its own scroller so the sticky gutter stays put while code scrolls under it. */
/* Sized to the window below its own top (2026-10-11): the old `32rem` floor overrode the viewport
   term on a short window (a ~623px one gave it 512px starting ~192px down), so the page scrolled as
   well as the box. `--theme-explore-code-offset` is the box's top plus `.admin-content`'s 2rem bottom
   padding and a little slack; the `16rem` floor keeps a usable box on a short phone/window. With the
   file tray above the toolbar (2026-10-11) that top is ~300px on desktop (header, a one-row tray,
   toolbar); a narrow container wraps the header, tray and toolbar onto more rows, hence the larger
   offset in the container query below. 22rem still left the page scrolling ~54px past the box on
   a 900px-tall desktop pane (Chrome check, 2026-10-11: `.admin-content` scrollHeight 954 vs 900), so
   the desktop offset carries that measured 3.5rem too. */
.theme-explore-code-view { --theme-explore-code-offset: 25.5rem; }
@container theme-explore (max-width: 560px) {
  .theme-explore-code-view { --theme-explore-code-offset: 28rem; }
}
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto minmax(max-content, 1fr);
  min-height: 16rem; max-height: max(16rem, calc(100dvh - var(--theme-explore-code-offset))); overflow: auto;
  margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface);
  font: 0.82rem/1.6 var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, monospace);
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px;
}
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer code { display: block; padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); white-space: pre; }
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer .gutter {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none;
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer--wrap {
  grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr); align-content: start; padding: var(--space-3) 0;
}
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer--wrap .line-number {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none; padding: 0 var(--space-3);
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.theme-explore-code-view .code-viewer--wrap .line-content {
  padding: 0 var(--space-4); white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
/* The view tabs plus the publish toggle sit together on the LEFT of the toolbar; the preview-width
   control and fullscreen trigger (Preview tab only) sit on the right — `.page-editor-toolbar`'s own
   `justify-content: space-between` then only has to place TWO children (this wrapper and
   `.theme-explore-toolbar-actions`). Save/Reset used to live in here too; the 2026-08-11 toolbar
   restructure moved them up into the outer `.page-actions` row beside `← All themes`, matching
   `PageEditor.tsx`'s own toolbar shape — see `ThemeExplore.tsx`'s `ThemeExploreToolbarButtons` for
   why. `flex-wrap: wrap` of its own (independent of `.page-editor-toolbar`'s own wrap): a locked
   publish toggle's reason text is the longest thing this row can carry, so it gets to drop onto its
   own line without dragging the Preview/HTML tabs down with it. */
.theme-explore-toolbar-start { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-4); flex-wrap: wrap; min-width: 0; }
.theme-explore-toolbar-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); flex-wrap: wrap; }
/* Narrow container (a phone, or a desktop squeezed by the side nav plus the chat dock): the device /
   reload / fullscreen group wraps under the Preview/HTML tabs; tighten that wrapped row's gap from
   the toolbar's 1rem so the two lines read as one toolbar. A container query, not `@media`, for the
   reason on `.theme-explore` above. */
@container theme-explore (max-width: 560px) {
  .theme-explore-main .page-editor-toolbar { row-gap: var(--space-2); }
}
/* The publish toggle for the selected PAGE (2026-08-30 owner ask, restyled from a two-button
   Off/Published segmented control the same day — "Can the publish just be a toggle rather than the
   tab... it will be a toggle, a green toggle, Apple style"). Lives inside `.theme-explore-toolbar-
   start` now, immediately right of the Preview/HTML tabs — no longer its own row below the toolbar.
   Rendered for every file with SOME publish state, live or locked — see `ThemeExplorePublishToggle`'s
   own doc for the two shapes that covers. `flex-wrap: wrap` so a locked toggle's reason text (the
   longest content this group ever carries) drops to its own line rather than forcing the row wider. */
.theme-explore-publish-toggle { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.theme-explore-publish-label { font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--muted); }
/* `.theme-explore-publish-reason` (the LOCKED toggle's visible reason text, 2026-08-30) is gone:
   owner, 2026-10-11, moved the reason into the ⓘ tooltip so the row is just "Publish [switch] ⓘ".
   The disabled switch itself still shows the control exists, which was the 2026-08-30 fix. */
/* The switch itself — a real `<button>`, reset back to a bare pill: the app-wide `button` rule
   (top of this file) paints every button with the burnt-orange primary fill/padding/radius, which
   this control replaces entirely rather than layers on top of. Sized to match `.jini-toggle-row-
   switch`'s own iOS-style dimensions (Open Design's Settings toggle, `.settings-ui-section` block
   further down this file) for one consistent toggle idiom app-wide, rather than a second bespoke
   size living here. */
.theme-explore-switch {
  position: relative;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  width: 34px; height: 20px;
  padding: 0; border: none; border-radius: var(--r-pill);
  background: var(--jini-border-strong, var(--border-strong));
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 0.15s;
}
/* Burnt orange (`--primary`) when on, and the same mid-grey off track, as `.agent-plugin-switch`
   (2026-10-06 mobile catalog P-8: these were the only green toggles left in the app, next to the
   burnt-orange plugin/skill switches). History: it was green when on — the owner's own 2026-08-30 ask, verbatim ("a green toggle, Apple style") — reusing `--ok`
   (the SAME green `.status-ok`/`.tab-bar-dot` use for "this is connected/active") rather than
   inventing a second green token, and `--ok-solid` as its own fallback-preferred value: dark mode's
   plain `--ok` is tuned to read as TEXT on a dark background and is too light to hold this track's
   own contrast against `--surface-2` there, the identical reasoning `.deployment-step-marker-done`'s
   own comment gives for the same `--ok-solid, var(--ok)` pair on a solid-filled shape. */
.theme-explore-switch.is-on { background: var(--primary); }
/* Written as its own compound selector, not left to rely on source order against `.is-on` above:
   both this and that rule set `background` at equal specificity, so without this the locked-ON case
   (index/404 — see `lockedPublishReason`) would depend on which rule happened to come last rather
   than always winning on its own terms. */
.theme-explore-switch.is-on:disabled { background: var(--primary); }
.theme-explore-switch:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: 0.6; background: var(--jini-border-strong, var(--border-strong)); }
.theme-explore-switch-knob {
  position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px;
  width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--surface);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
  transition: transform 0.15s;
}
.theme-explore-switch.is-on .theme-explore-switch-knob { transform: translateX(14px); }
.theme-explore-fullscreen-trigger {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 2rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0; flex-shrink: 0;
  background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.theme-explore-fullscreen-trigger svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; }
.theme-explore-fullscreen-trigger:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-1); opacity: 1; }
.theme-explore-fullscreen-trigger:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }
 
/* Explore preview, fullscreen — same native-`<dialog>` foundation as `.confirm-dialog` (see that
   rule's own comment for the full rationale; the image preview this once also mirrored is Jini's
   shared `.jini-lightbox` since 2026-10-21) and the SAME
   `[open]`-scoped `display` split: an unscoped `display` rule on the bare class beats the UA
   stylesheet's `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }` regardless of specificity, so `display` only
   ever lives on the `[open]` variant below. Sized to most of the viewport rather than the image
   lightbox's content-sized box — a page preview has no intrinsic size to shrink-wrap. The close
   button keeps the image lightbox's former corner-badge treatment (the retired
   `.image-preview-modal-close`) rather than reinventing one, since this is the same "one close
   affordance over the content" shape. */
.theme-explore-preview-dialog {
  position: relative;
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: var(--space-5);
  width: 96vw; height: 92vh; max-width: 96vw; max-height: 92vh;
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg); color: var(--fg); box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.theme-explore-preview-dialog[open] { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
.theme-explore-preview-dialog::backdrop { background: var(--jini-overlay-bg-preview);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.theme-explore-preview-dialog-close {
  position: absolute; top: var(--space-3); right: var(--space-3); z-index: 1;
  width: 2.1rem; height: 2.1rem; padding: 0; border-radius: 50%;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  font-size: 1.3rem; line-height: 1; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
}
.theme-explore-preview-dialog-close:hover { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--fg-1); opacity: 1; }
.theme-explore-preview-dialog-iframe {
  max-width: 100%; height: 100%;
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--tovu-site-preview-bg);
}
 
/* `@jini-ai/ui`'s Toast ships behavior (TTL, exit timing, ARIA) but no styling — it renders class
   names and leaves the look to the host, which is why these live here rather than in the package.
   `.leaving` is the one non-optional rule: the component sets it at `ttlMs - TOAST_EXIT_MS` and
   unmounts at `ttlMs`, so without a matching animation the toast vanishes abruptly instead of
   fading. Fixed position so it never displaces page content the way the old inline banner did. */
.jini-toast {
  position: fixed; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); z-index: 60;
  max-width: min(560px, calc(100vw - var(--space-6)));
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
  border-radius: var(--radius-md, 8px);
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-1);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong);
  box-shadow: var(--jini-overlay-toast-shadow);
  animation: jini-toast-in 140ms ease-out;
}
.jini-toast.placement-bottom { bottom: var(--space-5); }
.jini-toast.placement-top { top: var(--space-5); }
.jini-toast.tone-success { border-color: var(--ok, var(--border-strong)); }
.jini-toast.tone-error { border-color: var(--danger, var(--border-strong)); }
.jini-toast.leaving { animation: jini-toast-out 160ms ease-in forwards; }
.jini-toast-body { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); padding-right: var(--space-4); }
.jini-toast-message { font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.4; }
.jini-toast-details { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--fg-2); }
/* The component renders this X itself whenever `onDismiss` is passed — it is not markup the host
   supplies, only styling the host owes it. Absolutely positioned so a long message wraps under the
   full width instead of reserving a column for a 13px glyph. */
.jini-toast-close {
  position: absolute; top: 6px; right: 6px;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 22px; height: 22px; padding: 0;
  background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  color: var(--fg-3, var(--fg-2)); cursor: pointer;
}
.jini-toast-close:hover { background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg-1); opacity: 1; }
/* The component's optional action (`actionLabel` + `onAction`, e.g. Library's "Open Trash"). A toast
   with one lays out as a row so the action sits beside the message; the right padding keeps it clear
   of the absolutely positioned X. 44px tall so it is a comfortable tap target. */
.jini-toast:has(> .jini-toast-action) {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2);
  padding-block: var(--space-1); padding-right: var(--space-6);
}
.jini-toast:has(> .jini-toast-action) .jini-toast-body { padding-right: 0; }
.jini-toast-action {
  flex: none; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 var(--space-3);
  background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  color: var(--link); font: inherit; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer;
}
.jini-toast-action:hover { background: var(--surface); }
.jini-toast-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 1px; }
@keyframes jini-toast-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, 6px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translate(-50%, 0); } }
@keyframes jini-toast-out { to { opacity: 0; transform: translate(-50%, 6px); } }
/* Honors the OS "reduce motion" setting: the toast still appears and still leaves on the same
   schedule, it just does not slide. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .jini-toast, .jini-toast.leaving { animation: none; }
}
/* Scoped under `.page-header` (not bare `.page-kicker`/`.page-title`/`.page-description`) so
   these reliably beat the legacy `.admin-content h1` / `h1 + p` rules above on specificity
   (0,2,0 vs 0,1,1) — that legacy pair still owns every section this canary does not touch, and
   `.page-title` is itself an `<h1>` sitting inside `.admin-content`, so both rules would
   otherwise match the same element with conflicting margins. */
.page-header .page-kicker {
  font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted); margin: 0;
}
.page-header .page-title {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-xl); font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--fg); margin: 0;
}
.page-header .page-description { font-size: var(--text-md); color: var(--muted); margin: 0; max-width: 60ch; }
/* `max-width: 100%`: `flex-shrink: 0` keeps the group at its one-row width, so once `.page-header`
   wraps it under the title its own `flex-wrap` never fired and a wide group (Widgets: Publish ·
   Regions · type select · Add New, 474px) pushed the whole page sideways at 375px with "Add New"
   off-screen (2026-10-06 mobile catalog WI-1). Capped at the header's width, it wraps instead. */
.page-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); flex-shrink: 0; flex-wrap: wrap; max-width: 100%; }
/* Widget Regions' key field and its Bind button wrap as one unit (`WidgetRegions.tsx`). */
.widget-regions-bind { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); min-width: 0; max-width: 100%; }
.widget-regions-bind > input { flex: 1 1 8rem; min-width: min(8rem, 100%); }
.widget-regions-bind > button { flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap; }
 
/* EXPERIMENT (2026-09-06, owner request — expected to be reverted as one commit if it does not
   land): on the two content editors only, the `← Pages`/`← Posts` link leaves the action group and
   sits alone at the far left, and the kicker/title/description block centres between it and the
   Save/Delete/status group on the right.
 
   A MODIFIER (`.page-header-split`), never the bare `.page-header` primitive: ~39 screens share
   that class and still want title-left/actions-right. It comes after `.page-header` in this file,
   so at equal (0,1,0) specificity these declarations win — presence here is not precedence, source
   order is.
 
   Grid, not a flex row, and the three columns are `1fr auto 1fr` rather than `auto 1fr auto`: in
   flex (or with `auto` rails) the middle is only centred in the LEFTOVER space, so the much wider
   action group on the right would shove the title visibly left of the header's true centre. Equal
   `1fr` rails put it at true centre. Both rails keep grid's `auto` minimum, so a rail whose content
   cannot fit grows and the title merely drifts — it does not overflow the page. */
.page-header-split {
  display: grid;
  /* Bound the title and both rails: long subtitles and multi-action headers must
     wrap inside their columns instead of consuming the neighbouring rail. */
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 1fr);
  align-items: start;
}
/* Explicit placement, because the third rail is EMPTY on the toolbar editors (Pages/Posts/Forms —
   the status/Save/Delete group moved out of this header into `.editor-action-row` below) but
   OCCUPIED on the editors that never grew a separate action row (Widgets/Menus — see
   `.page-header-actions` below). Without pinning the columns, auto-placement would drop these
   children into columns 1 and 2 and the title would sit left of centre; naming the columns keeps
   the third rail reserved (empty or not) so the title stays at true centre either way. */
.page-header-split .page-header-lead { grid-column: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; white-space: nowrap; }
.page-header-split .page-header-text { grid-column: 2; align-items: center; text-align: center; }
/* Third rail, for the editors that keep Save/status IN the header instead of a separate
   `.editor-action-row` (Widgets, Menus — 2026-09-22). `grid-column: 3` because column 2's own
   `justify-items` isn't set to `end`; `justify-self: end` then pins this rail to the column's own
   right edge instead of stretching across it. Bare `.page-actions` (used on the non-split
   `.page-header` elsewhere) needs neither — it is already the grid's last auto-placed child there. */
.page-header-split .page-header-actions { grid-column: 3; justify-self: end; min-width: 0; max-width: 100%; justify-content: flex-end; }
/* Back is a plain 40px arrow at every width, no button chrome (owner, 2026-10-13: the bordered
   square looked off-centre on phones, then "consistent everywhere the same back control is used",
   so desktop/tablet lost the bordered "← Back" pill too), matching the Edit post/page back arrow
   (`.content-editor-back`, styles/editor.css). Its `aria-label` ("Back: Pages" etc.) still names
   it. The 40px square stays as the tap area: -10px puts the glyph on the content's left edge, and
   where a kicker sits above the title (all but Forms) 0.75rem drops the arrow from the kicker's
   line to the title's. */
.page-header-split .page-header-lead > .btn-secondary {
  display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 40px; height: 40px; padding: 0; font-size: 0;
  margin-left: -10px; border-color: transparent; background: transparent; box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow); color: var(--fg-2);
}
.page-header-split .page-header-lead > .btn-secondary::before { content: "\2190"; font-size: var(--text-lg); line-height: 1; }
.page-header-split:has(.page-kicker) .page-header-lead > .btn-secondary { margin-top: 0.75rem; }
.page-header-split .page-header-lead > .btn-secondary:hover { background: transparent; color: var(--fg); }
 
/* CONTAINER query, not `@media (max-width: 900px)` (replaced 2026-09-22 — same swap
   `.agent-plugin-rows` made above, same reason): 900px keyed on the VIEWPORT, and the thing that
   actually squeezes this row is the workspace chat dock, which takes width from `.admin-content`
   while leaving the viewport exactly as wide as it was. Measured live with the chat dock open at a
   1440px viewport: `.page` renders ~560px wide — comfortably past the point the row needs to
   stack — while the media query, seeing 1440, never fired, and the back link wrapped onto four
   lines fighting the grid for room instead.
 
   `container-type` sits on `.page:has(.page-header-split)` rather than bare `.page` (~39 other
   screens share that class for layouts a size-contained ancestor could break — e.g. a
   `position: fixed`/`absolute` descendant would get re-anchored to this box instead of the
   viewport). Scoping to `:has(.page-header-split)` — the same selector idiom the chat-dock rule
   above already uses on a shared ancestor — means only the handful of editor screens that opt into
   this header modifier pay for the new containing block, and every other `.page` is untouched.
 
   620px (not 900px): the container is `.page`'s own inline size, which is already narrower than
   the viewport by the sidebar (232px) and `.admin-content`'s padding (2 × 2.5rem) even with the
   chat dock closed — the viewport figure this replaces was never the row's real budget, that
   offset was. */
.page:has(.page-header-split) { container-type: inline-size; }
@container (max-width: 900px) {
  /* Region binding needs more than the split header's quarter-width action rail on tablets. */
  .page-header-split:has(.widget-regions-bind) .page-header-actions {
    grid-column: 1 / -1;
    grid-row: 2;
    justify-self: start;
    justify-content: flex-start;
    width: 100%;
  }
}
@container (max-width: 620px) {
  /* Left-aligned, Back beside the title (mobile catalog P-6/PG-3/MN-4, 2026-10-06). The stacked,
     centred version this replaced — Back pill, then kicker/title/description, then (Widgets/Menus)
     a Back/Save row — burnt 140-250px of a phone screen before any content, and its centring
     disagreed with every list page's left-aligned header. Back is the 40px arrow square (the
     base rule above) so the title keeps the rest of the row. */
  .page-header-split { grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr); column-gap: var(--space-3); row-gap: var(--space-3); }
  .page-header-split .page-header-lead { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; justify-content: flex-start; }
  .page-header-split .page-header-text { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1; align-items: flex-start; text-align: left; }
 
  /* Widgets/Menus keep their header actions (Save, Copy embed…) — as one left-aligned row under
     the title, the same place every list page puts its `.page-actions`. */
  .page-header-split .page-header-actions { grid-column: 1 / -1; grid-row: 2; justify-self: start; justify-content: flex-start; }
}
 
/* Second half of the same 2026-09-06 experiment (owner: "put the published save and delete buttons
   under the gray desktop/tablet/mobile row"). The status select, Save and Delete leave the header
   entirely and become their own row directly beneath `.page-editor-toolbar`. One shared class, both
   editors, same reasoning as `.page-header-split` above.
 
   RIGHT-aligned, deliberately, not left. Left-aligning would put `Delete` one row below the
   `HTML`/`Editor` view tab — a destructive control sitting directly under one an operator clicks
   constantly, which is exactly the adjacency that produces mis-clicks. Right also keeps these three
   in the column they have always occupied (the header's right edge, and now the template select's),
   so the eye still finds them in the same place after the move.
 
   SPACING (owner, 2026-09-06: "compress the space. There's way too much space above and below the
   new set of buttons ... That's unacceptable"). The first attempt left 36px above and 24px below a
   37px row — a ~97px band, 79% of it empty. The measurable fault was not the total, it was the
   RATIO: 36 above and 24 below put the row nearer the canvas than the toolbar, so proximity
   assigned it to neither and it read as a gap someone forgot to fill. Both sides are now the same
   12px the toolbar was already tuned to sit from the canvas (2026-08-11, "very minimal space"), so
   toolbar / actions / canvas read as one tight chrome stack in the rhythm this screen already had.
   Band: 97px -> 61px, and 37px of what is left is the controls themselves. */
.editor-action-row {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: flex-end;
  gap: var(--space-3);
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  /* Cancels `.page`'s own 24px flex gap so the only air above this row is the toolbar's existing
     0.75rem bottom margin. Same token and same idiom `styles/pages.css` uses to pull the content
     pane up under the toolbar — one mechanism for "sit tight under the row above", not two. */
  margin-top: calc(-1 * var(--space-6));
}
 
/* The status field goes to the row's LEFT end, leaving the actions on the right. Three problems,
   one move:
 
   1. Right-aligning everything left ~1030px of a 1300px row empty, and a bar with content at only
      one end reads as a row someone forgot to finish rather than as a deliberate action bar.
      Anchoring both ends is what makes the whitespace between them read as intentional.
   2. Stacked directly under `.editor-template-picker`'s own select, 12px apart in the same column,
      it put two unrelated dropdowns (which template renders / whether this is published) in one
      vertical pair — the reader has to stop and tell them apart.
   3. Draft-vs-Published is a STATE FIELD, not an action. Sharing a cluster with Save and Delete
      grouped it with the things that commit. Left/right now splits the row the way the meaning
      does: state on one side, actions on the other — matching the toolbar above, whose left is
      likewise view STATE (the tabs) and whose right is configuration.
 
   `order`, not a markup move, so this stays a stylesheet-only change and reverts as one. Focus
   order is unaffected in the way that matters: the reordered select is the first focusable child
   in the DOM too, so tabbing still runs left-to-right across the row exactly as it reads. */
.editor-action-row > select { order: -1; margin-right: auto; }
 
/* Delete is destructive and must not sit at Save's own adjacency — doubling the gap (12px -> 24px)
   makes the row read as [state field] [commit] | [destructive] instead of four equal controls in a
   line. Spacing alone, no new color or size: `.btn-danger` already carries the semantic weight, and
   this row is chrome, not a place to raise the volume of the one control nobody should hit by
   accident. */
.editor-action-row .btn-danger { margin-left: var(--space-3); }
 
/* Inserting a row between the toolbar and the content pane broke an assumption the pane's own
   spacing rule was built on. `styles/pages.css`'s `.page > .page-preview-frame` (and
   `styles/editor.css`'s `.post-editor-pane`) carry `margin-top: calc(-1 * var(--space-6))` to
   cancel `.page`'s flex gap, because the owner asked for "very minimal space between the toolbar
   and the content pane" (2026-08-11) and the toolbar's own 0.75rem bottom margin was meant to be
   the only air left. With this row in between, that -24px stopped closing a toolbar/pane gap and
   started dragging the pane flush against the Delete button — measured 0px, the frame's border
   touching the button. Restore the normal gap, but ONLY for the pane that directly follows this
   row: an adjacent-sibling selector, so Posts' conditional slug-collision warning (which already
   sat between toolbar and pane before this change) keeps the spacing it always had.
 
   `.page >` in front is not decoration — it lifts these to (0,3,0) so they beat the (0,2,0) rules
   they override no matter which stylesheet the bundler emits first.
 
   The replacement is 12px, not the 24px this first shipped with: that is the gap the toolbar itself
   had to the pane before this row existed, so the canvas keeps the "very minimal space" it was
   tuned for and the action row is not left floating closer to the content than to the chrome it
   belongs to. */
.page > .editor-action-row + .page-preview-frame,
.page > .editor-action-row + .page-html-source,
.page > .editor-action-row + .interactive-html-editor,
.page > .editor-action-row + .post-editor-pane,
.page > .editor-publishing-fields + .post-editor-pane {
  margin-top: calc(-1 * var(--space-3));
}
 
/* Scheduled publishing + featured image (2026-10-05) — one compact row right under the action row it
   qualifies, pulled up by the same 12px idiom so the two read as one publishing block. */
.page > .editor-publishing-fields {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: var(--space-4);
  margin-top: calc(-1 * var(--space-3));
}
.editor-publishing-field { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
.editor-publishing-field .field-label { margin: 0; }
/* A featured asset that will not load (deleted, or a non-image saved before the server refused
   those) — an empty hatched box, never a broken image with spilled alt text. The cover slot sizes it;
   the settings Image tab's 2.25rem thumb it was first drawn for is gone (2026-10-11). */
.editor-featured-preview-missing {
  display: inline-block; background: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--surface-3) 0 4px, transparent 4px 8px);
}
/* Cover image above the title node (owner, 2026-10-10) — `PostCoverImage.tsx`. Empty: one quiet
   button. Set: the image across the content column at its natural height, with
   Change/Remove over its corner on hover or focus (always shown where there is no hover). */
.post-cover { position: relative; padding: 1.5rem 2rem 0; background: var(--surface); }
.post-cover + .editor-body { padding-top: 0.75rem; }
.post-cover-add { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); padding: 0.3rem 0.6rem; margin-inline-start: -0.6rem; color: var(--muted); font-weight: 500; }
/* Natural height, uncropped, like the published cover (owner 2026-10-11: "same as the published
   page" — a fixed 220px band with `object-fit: cover` cut the image the public page shows whole).
   The missing placeholder keeps a height.
   Width: the published post column, not the whole editor (owner 2026-10-11: the slot spanning the
   wide editor read much wider and shorter than the public cover). 672px = tovu-theme's
   `.post-detail` (max-width 720px, border-box) minus `.wrap`'s 24px side padding, measured with
   getComputedStyle on /how-tovu-saves-you-time. The admin cannot read the site theme's CSS, so
   this is one constant; change it here if the theme's post column changes. Left-aligned with the
   editor text, which starts at the same edge. `.post-cover-frame` holds the image and its
   Change/Remove so the buttons sit on the image's corner, not the editor's. */
.post-cover { --post-cover-max-width: 672px; }
