.post-cover-frame { position: relative; display: block; max-width: var(--post-cover-max-width); }
.post-cover-image { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); }
.post-cover-missing { display: block; height: 220px; }
.post-cover-actions {
  position: absolute; top: var(--space-2); right: var(--space-2); display: flex; gap: var(--space-2);
  opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.14s;
}
.post-cover-actions .btn-secondary { padding: 0.3rem 0.65rem; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }
/* "Hide the cover image in the body" under the slot (owner, 2026-10-11; was the settings Image tab).
   One quiet line sized to its text; the ⓘ carries the explanation. */
.post-cover-option { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-1); margin-top: var(--space-2); font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--muted); }
.post-cover-option label { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); margin: 0; cursor: pointer; }
.post-cover-option input { margin: 0; }
.post-cover-set:hover .post-cover-actions, .post-cover:focus-within .post-cover-actions { opacity: 1; }
@media (hover: none), (max-width: 640px) {
  .post-cover-actions { opacity: 1; }
}
.editor-scheduled-badge {
  font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 0.1rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted);
}
 
/* Card — content sits inside a bordered surface with real padding, the quality Settings has and
   a bare `.list-table` floating on the page does not. */
.card {
  background: var(--jini-panel-bg); border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-panel-border); border-radius: var(--r-lg);
  padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
/* A card wrapping a table: the table supplies its own cell padding, so the card contributes only
   the border/radius/shadow frame, not a second layer of padding. */
.card-flush { padding: 0; overflow: hidden; }
 
/* Card/section heading — the primitive missing from the set above (`.page-kicker`/`.page-title`/
   `.page-description`/`.card` all existed; the heading INSIDE a card did not). Without it a bare
   `<h2>` in a `.card` inherits the UA default, which measures 24px with 19.92px margins — 91% of
   `.page-title`'s own 26.4px, in a different family, with a 40.7px gap to the first paragraph
   (all four numbers measured live via `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect`, not read off the
   rules). That is not a hierarchy step, it is a near-tie, and the stray UA margin is what reads as
   "nobody chose this".
 
   Size and weight follow Jini's settings scale, the one Settings and Authentication use: 14px/600
   section titles over 13px copy. An earlier 1.15rem/700 tier (borrowed from `.theme-card h3`) made
   every card screen read as another app beside those two (owner, 2026-10-22: "it should all be the
   same text"); it was first patched per screen, then fixed here once so every card screen follows.
   The display face stays, so a card title still rhymes with `.page-title`, which keeps its size.
 
   Additive and opt-in: only elements that take the class change. */
.card-title {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-2);
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1.3; color: var(--fg);
  text-wrap: balance;
}
/* A muted lead line directly under a `.card-title`, for the one sentence that says what the card
   is about before its content starts. `max-width` in `ch` so a long sentence wraps at a readable
   measure instead of running the full width of a 1440px card. */
.card-lead { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); line-height: 1.5; max-width: 68ch; }
/* Card copy and notices: bare paragraphs and list items inside a card, and every `.notice`, take
   the same 13px as `.card-lead` instead of inheriting the 16px page text. `:where` keeps this at
   zero specificity, so any class that sets its own size (hints, labels, empty states) still wins. */
:where(.card p, .card li, .notice) { font-size: var(--text-sm); }
/* Danger-zone card modifier (2026-08-31: the left-accent-border idiom this used to share with
   `.notice.error`/`.notice.warning` is retired everywhere in this app — owner's explicit call,
   "I don't like that idiom at all" — see the `.notice` rules below for the fuller reasoning).
   Recolors `.card`'s own hairline border to `--danger` on all four sides instead of just the left
   edge, and tints the fill with the same subtle `--danger-bg` `.notice.error` already uses, so a
   danger card and an error notice read as the same family of "something serious here" surface.
   `.card-title` gets its own rule below rather than this selector setting `color` directly — a
   whole card's BODY text recolored red would fight the readability of an actual explanatory
   paragraph (Workspace's "Delete workspace" card is a full sentence, not `.notice`'s one-liner);
   the heading alone carries the color signal, `.card-lead`/buttons keep their normal contrast. */
.card-danger { border-color: var(--danger); background: var(--danger-bg); }
.card-danger .card-title { color: var(--danger); }
/* Section eyebrow for a group of cards that needs a name but not a second page-level heading —
   same uppercase/letterspaced idiom as `.page-kicker` and `.field-label`, one tier down from
   `.card-title` so it never competes with it. */
.section-eyebrow {
  margin: 0 0 var(--space-3); font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted);
}
 
/* Toolbar — the row of filters/search/upload controls that sits above a list, so those controls
   read as one control group instead of stray inputs dropped on the page (Media's unstyled
   `<input type="file">` today). */
.toolbar { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); flex-wrap: wrap; margin-bottom: var(--space-4); }
.toolbar input, .toolbar select { font-size: var(--text-sm); }
 
/* Button hierarchy — the global bare `button` rule below is the filled primary CTA (correct for
   one action per screen, e.g. "New Post"/"Upload"). These variants give secondary/destructive
   actions the same restraint Settings' outline `.settings-ui-dialog-btn` pill has, instead of every button on the page
   reading as equally urgent (today: New Post, Upload, Save, Cancel, Edit, and Trash are all
   rendered identically). */
.btn-secondary { background: var(--jini-control-bg); color: var(--fg-2); border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-control-border);
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow, none);
}
.btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
/* Keep state elevation below cover-specific shadows, including while pressed. */
.btn-secondary:where(:hover) {
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-hover, none);
}
.btn-secondary:where(:not(:disabled):active) {
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-pressed, none);
}
.btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid transparent; }
.btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
/* Outline variants disable by fading in place — keep their own frame, drop the label to `--faint` —
   rather than taking `button:disabled`'s neutral fill, which would turn an outline button solid.
   Source order after the `:hover` rules above (same (0,2,0)) keeps hover from repainting them. */
.btn-secondary:disabled { background: var(--surface); color: var(--faint); border-color: var(--border); }
.btn-ghost:disabled { background: transparent; color: var(--faint); }
.btn-danger { background: transparent; color: var(--danger); border: 1px solid var(--danger); }
.btn-danger:hover { background: var(--danger-bg); opacity: 1; }
/* Disabled destructive control, read as calm and deliberately unavailable rather than broken.
   Without this, `button:disabled` (specificity 0,1,1) out-specifies `.btn-danger`'s own background/
   color (0,1,0) and applies the PRIMARY-tinted disabled fill everywhere else on the page — verified
   live via getComputedStyle on Workspace's disabled "Delete workspace" button: a peach background
   (color-mix of the app's burnt-orange primary), near-white text, and `.btn-danger`'s own red border
   all on one button, which reads as a mis-colored/half-rendered control rather than an intentional
   disabled state. Muted red on every channel instead, so it stays legibly in the danger family.
   `.btn-danger:disabled` is (0,2,0), which beats `button:disabled`'s (0,1,1) outright — no
   `!important` or extra scoping needed. */
/* All three mixes are `in oklab`, not `in oklch`. OKLCh interpolates HUE along the shorter arc
   between the two endpoints, so mixing a warm token with a partner that carries real (even tiny)
   blue chroma rotates the result through magenta/purple; OKLab mixes rectangular a/b, so it just
   desaturates. Only a `none` hue (light `--surface`) is carried forward safely in either space —
   and that does not help here, because two of these
   three mix against `--muted` and `--border-strong`, and both of those carry real chroma in LIGHT
   mode as well (`oklch(53% 0.016 258)` and `oklch(86% 0.010 255)`). Measured on this button,
   before -> after:
     color  light  L0.5245 C0.1117 H327.9 -> C0.1003 H21.7  (magenta text -> muted red)
     color  dark   L0.722  C0.0934 H324.3 -> C0.0843 H22.4  (magenta text -> muted red)
     border light  L0.724  C0.082  H307   -> C0.0723 H21.4  (violet border -> muted red)
     border dark   L0.7953 C0.126  H10    -> C0.126  H25    (was already red; now lands exactly
            on `--danger`'s own hue, because `--border-strong` in dark is `oklch(100% 0 0 / 0.18)`
            and its explicit hue 0 was dragging the mix down to 10 rather than off to blue)
     bg     dark   L0.2516 C0.035  H270.6 -> C0.0151 H331.6 (blue-violet ground -> a near-neutral
            dark ground with a faint red-pink lean. The CHROMA HALVING is the real fix here; the
            residual hue is not 25 and is not claimed to be, because at 12% the surface dominates
            the a/b sum and pushes `b` slightly negative)
     bg     light  L0.9424 C0.0228 H25    -> unchanged (this one mixes against `--surface`, whose
            `none` hue is carried forward identically in either space)
   Lightness is identical to 4dp on every channel in both themes — oklab and oklch interpolate L
   the same way — so the "stays legibly in the danger family" goal the comment above states is
   preserved exactly. */
.btn-danger:disabled {
  cursor: not-allowed;
  background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--danger) 12%, var(--surface));
  border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--danger) 40%, var(--border-strong));
  color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--danger) 55%, var(--muted));
}
/* Scaffold for phase 2 (MSG-14's hierarchy audit) — reversible-but-access-affecting row actions
   (Users' Disable/Reset-password) that are neither plain secondary nor fully destructive. No
   caller in this dispatch's own files; see `--warning`'s token comment for why. */
.btn-warning { background: transparent; color: var(--warning); border: 1px solid var(--warning); }
.btn-warning:hover { background: var(--warning-bg); opacity: 1; }
/* Same idea as `.btn-danger:disabled` (muted, still legibly in its family), minus the fill: the
   warning outline has none to mute. Mixed toward `--faint`/`--border` rather than `--muted`/
   `--border-strong` — the warning hue is already soft, and the stronger partners left it looking
   live. `in oklab` for the reason that rule's comment gives. */
.btn-warning:disabled {
  background: transparent;
  border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 30%, var(--border));
  color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warning) 45%, var(--faint));
}
/* Explicit alias for the bare-button styling above — for a primary action that needs to say so
   in the markup (e.g. sitting next to secondary/ghost siblings where the reader benefits from
   seeing the intent in the className, not just inheriting it silently from the element type). */
.btn-primary { background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-ink); border: 1px solid transparent; }
.btn-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { opacity: 0.88; }
/* `.btn-solid` lived here and is GONE (2026-08-11). It existed only for Explore's Save button, which
   cycled green (`--ok-solid`) -> black/white (`--fg`/`--surface`) -> `--primary`, the app's burnt
   orange, on owner instruction ("can you make the saved button the orange color now? .btn-primary").
   Its single consumer now uses `.btn-primary` directly, so the class is deleted rather than left as
   an unused alias — same call already made for `--ok-solid`/`--explore-bg` when their last consumers
   went away.
   Its `:disabled` override goes with it, and that is the point rather than a loss: that rule existed
   solely to BEAT the global `button:disabled` tint (~L242), which color-mixes `--primary` behind
   every disabled button and would have painted a muted brown "Saved" behind a black/white button.
   Now that this button IS `--primary`, the global rule is already the correct treatment — a dimmed
   version of its own resting state, exactly what the removed override was hand-rolling. */
 
/* Anchor-specific fixes the shape rule above cannot provide by itself. An `<a>` is inline by
   default, so the shape rule's `padding` never gets the box to center around — `inline-flex` +
   `align-items: center` is what actually makes a `.btn-*`-classed link look like the button it's
   styled as. `text-decoration: none` undoes the global `a`/`a:hover` rules' underline (`a:hover`
   specifically sets it back on hover, at the same (0,1,1) type+pseudo-class specificity as this
   rule's own `:hover` variant, so both states need an explicit override, not just the resting
   one). Verified against the Dashboard's "View site ↗" `.btn-secondary` anchor, a real caller —
   without this it rendered as underlined text wearing a border, no padding, no centering. */
a.btn-secondary, a.btn-ghost, a.btn-danger, a.btn-warning, a.btn-primary {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; text-decoration: none;
}
a.btn-secondary:hover, a.btn-ghost:hover, a.btn-danger:hover,
a.btn-warning:hover, a.btn-primary:hover { text-decoration: none; }
 
/* Responsive data table — a horizontal scroller so a wide `.list-table` degrades to a scroll
   region on narrow viewports instead of blowing out the page (the 390px canary target). */
.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; }
 
/* Empty state — a list with zero rows (Media with nothing uploaded yet) gets a real message
   instead of a header row floating over blank white space. */
.empty-state {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  gap: var(--space-2); padding: var(--space-8) var(--space-4); color: var(--muted);
  font-size: var(--text-sm); text-align: center;
}
/* A second, explanatory line under the state sentence (Webhooks: "No webhooks yet." / "Add one
   above…") — every OTHER `.empty-state` on this admin (Posts, Media, Collections, Forms) is a
   single line, so it gets this hierarchy for free from `.empty-state`'s own muted color and never
   needed these two classes. The two-line case needs them for real, not cosmetic, reasons: without
   an explicit `margin: 0`, a bare `<p>` keeps the UA default block margin (1em) ON TOP of
   `.empty-state`'s own flex `gap`, which is what put visible daylight between the two lines here
   (owner, 2026-09-13, screenshot `30-webhooks-empty-state-still-poor.png`, "float far apart"). Font
   size matches `.empty-state`'s own `--text-sm` on both — this is emphasis by WEIGHT AND COLOR, not
   by scale, so a two-line empty state still reads at the same size every single-line one already
   ships at. */
.empty-state-title { margin: 0; color: var(--fg); font-weight: 600; }
.empty-state-hint { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
 
/* Styled native file input — `<input type="file">` cannot be restyled into a fully custom
   control without JS, but the cross-browser `::file-selector-button` pseudo-element lets the
   button part match the rest of the button hierarchy instead of rendering as the bare OS widget. */
.file-input,
input[type="file"][data-jini-part^="media."] {
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2);
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong);
  border-radius: var(--r-sm); background: var(--surface);
}
.file-input::file-selector-button,
input[type="file"][data-jini-part^="media."]::file-selector-button {
  margin-right: var(--space-3); padding: 0.4rem 0.8rem; border: none; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-2); font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-sm);
  font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.14s;
}
.file-input::file-selector-button:hover,
input[type="file"][data-jini-part^="media."]::file-selector-button:hover { background: var(--surface-3); }
/* Media hides the native input visually and shows a translated <label> as the chooser; keyboard
   focus still lands on the hidden input, so draw the focus ring on its label. */
.file-input:focus-visible + label { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-text); outline-offset: 2px; }
 
.boot-screen { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; font-size: 1.1rem; color: var(--muted); }
 
/* Login */
.login-screen { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; background: var(--surface-2); }
.login-card { background: var(--surface); padding: 2.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); width: 22rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.9rem; box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); }
.login-card h1 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.8rem; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.login-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
/* Unified onto `.field-label`'s metrics (uppercase/letterspaced/muted/11px) — was its own
   0.85rem/600/fg-2 value, one of four different label idioms MSG-02 asked to consolidate.
   Layout (flex/gap) stays, since that's this context's own, not shared with the primitive. */
.login-card label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
.login-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; }
.login-error { color: var(--danger); font-size: 0.85rem; }
 
/* Layout */
.admin-layout { background: var(--tovu-admin-layout-bg); display: flex; height: 100vh; overflow: hidden; }
/* Wraps the mobile topbar + <main> in a column so the topbar (hidden above the tablet
   breakpoint, see the responsive block at the bottom of this file) can stack above content
   without disturbing `.admin-layout`'s own row of sidebar/content/chat-dock. `<main>` itself
   keeps its existing flex/overflow behavior unchanged at desktop widths. */
/* `position: relative` (2026-09-15) is load-bearing for `styles/editor.css`'s
   `.post-preview-expanded` (Preview fullscreen, Level 1 —
   `ADS-memory/.local-artifacts/handoffs/2026-09-15-preview-fullscreen-PLAN.md`): that rule is
   `position: absolute; inset: 0`, and without a positioned ancestor here it would resolve against
   the viewport instead of this column, escaping `.admin-content`'s scroll clip and covering
   `.admin-chat-dock`. Do not remove this without checking `.post-preview-expanded` first — it was
   removed once already (commit `09923d75`, reverting a DIFFERENT feature that also depended on it)
   and had to be restored for this one. */
.admin-main-col { position: relative; flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100%; }
/* `ScrollJumpButtons` (@jini-ai/ui) sits in a row just left of the assistant FAB's resting spot,
   vertically centred on it. Stacked ABOVE the FAB (the first cut) it reached 158px up, past the
   88px `--assistant-clearance` the page reserves, and covered the last card's controls at max
   scroll on phones and tablets (2026-10-21); beside it, the pair stays inside the FAB's band, so
   that one clearance keeps every row reachable. */
.admin-main-col {
  --jini-scroll-jump-direction: row;
  --jini-scroll-jump-right: calc(var(--admin-chat-fab-inset, 20px) + var(--admin-chat-fab-size, 56px) + 10px);
  --jini-scroll-jump-bottom: calc(var(--admin-chat-fab-inset, 20px) + (var(--admin-chat-fab-size, 56px) - 32px) / 2 + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
}
/* With the dock open the FAB is hidden, so the pair takes the column's own corner instead of
   floating where the FAB used to be. */
.admin-layout.hides-fab-while-open:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open) .admin-main-col {
  --jini-scroll-jump-right: 16px;
  --jini-scroll-jump-bottom: calc(16px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
}
/* Dark: Jini paints the pair `--jini-bg-elevated` (#171717 here, the page's own fill) with a muted
   glyph at 0.85 opacity, so the buttons all but vanished. One surface step up, the strong hairline
   and the secondary text colour make them read as raised controls, as in light. */
:root[data-theme="dark"] .jini-scroll-jump__btn {
  background: var(--surface-3); border-color: var(--border-strong); color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1;
}
/* `MiddleTruncate` (@jini-ai/ui): head and tail are separate flex items, so with `nowrap` a space
   right at the cut is trimmed off the end of the head or the start of the tail —
   "Shot 9.41.02 PM.png" rendered "Shot 9.41.02PM.png". `pre` keeps it; file names carry no
   newlines or runs of spaces for it to expose. */
.jini-middle-truncate__head, .jini-middle-truncate__tail { white-space: pre; }
.admin-content { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; padding: 2rem 2.5rem; }
/* The page's REAL width, as a named size container (2026-10-11, owner: "horrendous" with the side
   nav expanded and the dock open). Page layouts used to key their breakpoints on the VIEWPORT, but
   the width a page actually gets is viewport − nav (232px expanded / 60px rail) − dock (380px) −
   this box's padding: a 1280px window with both open leaves ~590px, so pages kept their "wide"
   layout in a phone-sized column and centred/fixed-width rows overflowed and clipped. Page-level
   "content is narrow" rules now use `@container admin-content (…)` against this box instead;
   rules that really mean "this is a phone" (touch targets, the sheet, the FAB) stay `@media`.
 
   Safe on the scroller itself, no inner wrapper needed: `container-type: inline-size` applies
   style + inline-size containment only, NOT layout containment, so it does not become the
   containing block for `position: fixed` toasts/backdrops rendered inside pages. Probed in
   headless Chromium 149 (2026-10-11): a `position: fixed; inset: 0` child of a 300px
   `container-type: inline-size` box still measured the full 1000×600 viewport. Its width comes
   from `.admin-main-col` (flex stretch), never from its content, so inline-size containment
   changes nothing about how it sizes. Nearer containers (`.dashboard-page`,
   `.page:has(.page-header-split)`, the plugin lists) keep winning their own unnamed/named queries. */
.admin-content { container-type: inline-size; container-name: admin-content; }
 
/* Mobile top bar — hidden above the tablet breakpoint (desktop keeps the always-visible
   sidebar and needs no drawer toggle or page-orientation label). */
.admin-topbar { display: none; }
.admin-topbar-toggle {
  background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); color: var(--fg-2);
  width: 36px; height: 36px; padding: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  flex-shrink: 0;
}
.admin-topbar-toggle:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
.admin-topbar-toggle svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; }
.admin-topbar-title { font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: var(--text-lg); color: var(--fg); }
 
/* Backdrop behind the off-canvas sidebar drawer (mobile only — see `.cms-nav.is-open` below).
   Click-to-dismiss; the drawer is also Escape- and route-change-dismissible (`App.tsx`). */
.sidebar-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: var(--jini-overlay-bg-navigation); z-index: 45;
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
 
/* ============================================================
   SIDEBAR — grouped .cms-nav (replaces the WordPress-shaped menu)
   ============================================================ */
.cms-nav {
  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;
  width: 232px; flex-shrink: 0; height: 100%;
  background: var(--jini-rail-bg, var(--jini-panel-bg)); border-right: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-rail-border, var(--jini-panel-border));
  /* `overflow-y: auto` (for the item list) inescapably clips X too — the CSS overflow spec
     computes an axis to `auto` the moment the *other* axis isn't `visible`, and that holds even
     when `overflow-x: visible` is declared explicitly (checked live: `getComputedStyle` still
     reports `auto` for it). The rail's hover tooltip needs to paint *outside* this box, so it is
     not a CSS-positioned child of this element at all — see `Sidebar.tsx`'s `RailTooltip`, which
     portals it to `document.body` instead. */
  overflow-y: auto; padding: 14px 12px 10px;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px;
  /* `width` here (not only in the `@media (min-width: 901px)` rail block below) so the property
     is already being transitioned before `.is-rail` toggles it — adding `transition` at the same
     time as the value that changes is a common way to lose the first frame of the animation. */
  transition: width 0.18s ease;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); box-shadow: var(--jini-rail-shadow, none);
}
/* Filtering only the paint layer keeps fixed popovers anchored to the viewport. Isolation
   keeps the negative layer above the canvas without changing fixed descendants' containing block. */
.cms-nav::before {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; pointer-events: none;
  border-radius: inherit;
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: var(--jini-rail-backdrop, none);
  backdrop-filter: var(--jini-rail-backdrop, none);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .cms-nav { transition: none; }
}
/* Close row inside the drawer — hidden at desktop widths (the sidebar is always in-flow there,
   nothing to close) and shown once the drawer becomes an off-canvas overlay below. */
.cms-nav-mobile-head { display: none; }
.cms-nav-close {
  background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); color: var(--fg-2);
  width: 30px; height: 30px; padding: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.cms-nav-close:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
.cms-nav-close svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
.cms-section { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
/* Wraps a section's rows so `hidden` can collapse them as one unit. Inherits the column layout
   `.cms-section` used to supply directly — without this the rows would lose their 2px gap the
   moment they gained a wrapper, since `gap` only applies to a flex container's own children. */
.cms-section-items { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
/* MUST accompany the `display: flex` above, and deleting it silently breaks the accordion.
   `hidden` only hides an element because the UA stylesheet carries `[hidden] { display: none }` —
   and ANY author-level `display` declaration beats the UA sheet outright, regardless of
   specificity. So the rule directly above defeats `Sidebar.tsx`'s `hidden={!open}` on its own: the
   button would keep toggling `aria-expanded`, the attribute would keep landing in the DOM, and the
   items would never disappear. `!important` is not needed — this is a plain, more-specific author
   rule beating another author rule. */
.cms-section-items[hidden] { display: none; }
.cms-group {
  font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint); padding: 14px 10px 6px;
}
/* Collapsible section heading (`collapsibleGroups` in App.tsx). A real `<button>`, so this resets
   the UA's own font/background/border rather than restyling from scratch — `font: inherit` is what
   stops the browser's default 13px system font from overriding `.cms-group`'s 10px uppercase
   treatment, which is the usual reason a heading-turned-button suddenly looks wrong. */
.cms-group-toggle {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px;
  width: 100%; font: inherit; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--faint); background: none; border: 0;
  text-align: left; cursor: pointer; border-radius: var(--r-md);
  transition: color 0.14s, background 0.14s;
}
.cms-group-toggle:hover { color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2); }
.cms-group-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, currentColor); outline-offset: -2px; }
.cms-group-chevron {
  width: 14px; height: 14px; flex-shrink: 0; opacity: 0.7;
  transition: transform 0.16s ease;
}
/* Closed points right, open points down — one glyph rotated rather than two icons, matching the
   rail toggle's existing approach directly below. */
.cms-group-toggle.is-closed .cms-group-chevron { transform: rotate(-90deg); }
.cms-item {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: var(--r-md);
  font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--fg-2); cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.14s, color 0.14s; position: relative; text-decoration: none;
}
.cms-item:hover { background: var(--surface-2); text-decoration: none; }
.cms-item svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; color: var(--muted); flex-shrink: 0; }
/* Long translated labels (including Hungarian) stay readable in the expanded desktop sidebar
   and mobile drawer. Rail mode still hides them with its more-specific rule below. */
.cms-item { flex-wrap: wrap; }
.cms-item > span:not(.soon) { flex: 1 0 min-content; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: normal; word-break: normal; }
/* Sites keeps its word and parentheses visible while only the live site name ellipsizes.
   The shared row's original full label remains available to assistive technology and rail tooltips.
   Keyed on the adapter's data attribute, never a JS-added row class: Jini's Sidebar is
   React-rendered, so every active-row change rewrites `className` and dropped such a class, leaving
   both labels visible side by side (2026-10-08). React preserves unmanaged attributes; avoiding
   `:has` also keeps composer keystrokes from re-matching this rule (2026-10-11).
   `.cms-item > span.cms-sites-label` stays below the rail rule's specificity so the collapsed rail
   still clips it. */
.cms-item[data-cms-sites-split] { flex-wrap: nowrap; }
.cms-item[data-cms-sites-split] > span:first-of-type {
  position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
}
.cms-item > span.cms-sites-label {
  display: flex; flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; white-space: nowrap;
}
.cms-sites-prefix, .cms-sites-suffix { flex: 0 0 auto; white-space: pre; }
.cms-sites-name { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; }
/* Rail-mode hover/focus tooltip. `position: fixed`, not `absolute` — this is portaled to
   `document.body` by `Sidebar.tsx`'s `RailTooltip`, not a descendant of the scrollable `.cms-nav`
   (see that component's doc comment for why a CSS-only child tooltip could not escape it), so
   `top`/`left` are plain viewport coordinates computed from the hovered item's own
   `getBoundingClientRect()` rather than relative to any ancestor box. `pointer-events: none` so
   the tooltip itself can never become the mouse target and cause its own hide/flicker loop. */
.cms-tooltip-portal {
  position: fixed; transform: translateY(-50%);
  background: var(--fg); color: var(--bg); font-size: var(--text-xs); font-weight: 500;
  padding: 4px 9px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); white-space: nowrap; z-index: 70;
  pointer-events: none;
}
 
.cms-item.active { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--selected-text-on-tint); font-weight: 600; }
/* "You are here": the rail wears the selection orange (non-text, 3:1 is enough); the label
   wears it too, through `--selected-text-on-tint` — plain orange text on this row's tint measured
   4.4:1, under AA's 4.5, which is why the label was near-black until 2026-10-08. The icon shares the
   label's token so both read as one orange: on the dark tint `--selected-ring` measured 2.96:1 (under
   even the 3:1 non-text floor) and visibly darker than the label; the shared token is 5.08:1 light,
   4.77:1 dark (Chrome, 2026-10-08). */
.cms-item.active svg { color: var(--selected-text-on-tint); }
.cms-item.active::before {
  content: ''; position: absolute; left: -12px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%);
  width: 3px; height: 18px; border-radius: 0 3px 3px 0; background: var(--selected-ring);
}
 
.cms-item.is-soon { cursor: default; color: var(--faint); }
.cms-item.is-soon:hover { background: transparent; }
.cms-item.is-soon svg { color: var(--faint); }
.cms-item .soon, .agent-plugin-maturity .soon {
  flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap; overflow-wrap: normal; word-break: normal;
  margin-left: auto; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint); border: 1px solid var(--border); padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 5px;
}
 
.cms-foot { margin-top: auto; padding-top: 10px; }
/* Keep the existing pill shape inside the shared tap/keyboard tooltip trigger. */
.agent-plugin-maturity .info-tip { margin-left: 0; }
.agent-plugin-maturity .info-tip-icon { width: auto; height: auto; min-height: 24px; border-radius: 5px; }
/* Hidden outside the desktop rail — see the rail block below. There is no mobile-drawer use for
   a rail toggle, since the drawer is always full-width and has its own close control. */
.cms-rail-toggle-row { display: none; }
.cms-rail-toggle {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; padding: 8px 10px;
  background: transparent; color: var(--muted); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.14s, color 0.14s, transform 0.18s ease;
}
.cms-rail-toggle:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); }
.cms-rail-toggle svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
.cms-logout {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; width: 100%; padding: 8px 10px; position: relative;
  background: transparent; color: var(--muted); border: none; border-radius: var(--r-md);
  font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.14s, color 0.14s;
}
.cms-logout:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); }
.cms-logout svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
 
.cms-nav::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 8px; }
.cms-nav::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: var(--border-strong); border-radius: 4px; border: 2px solid transparent; background-clip: padding-box; }
.cms-nav::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: transparent; }
 
/* ============================================================
   ICON RAIL — desktop-only collapse (`.cms-nav.is-rail`, `useSidebarRail`). `min-width: 901px`,
   the mirror image of the drawer's `max-width: 900px` below, so the two mechanisms never overlap:
   below 900px the nav is always the full-width drawer regardless of `.is-rail` (a collapsed rail
   would be pointless real estate on a screen already tight on width), and at/above it the rail
   toggle is live and the drawer machinery (backdrop, close row) stays inert.
   ============================================================ */
@media (min-width: 901px) {
  .cms-nav.is-rail { width: 60px; padding-left: 8px; padding-right: 8px; }
 
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-item { justify-content: center; padding: 10px 0; gap: 0; }
  /* Real label stays in the DOM (Sidebar.tsx never removes it) — clipped with the same recipe as
     `.visually-hidden` elsewhere in this file, not `display: none`, so it is still announced.
     `.cms-tooltip-portal` is a sibling of this element in the DOM (portaled to `document.body`),
     never a child, so there is no `.cms-tooltip` class to exclude here the way an earlier version
     of this rule needed to. */
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-item > span {
    position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
    overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
  }
  /* The active-row indicator bar's `left: -12px` assumes the nav's normal 12px padding — the
     rail's own 8px padding above moved that edge, so the offset needs its own value here or the
     bar floats detached from the rail's left edge instead of sitting flush against it. */
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-item.active::before { left: -8px; }
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-item .soon { display: none; }
 
  /* Group headings become a divider rule instead of disappearing — with icons alone and no
     separation, 26 items in five groups reads as one undifferentiated list. `font-size: 0` (not
     `display: none` or a negative text-indent) collapses the visible glyphs to nothing while
     leaving the text node itself in place for a screen reader, which reads DOM content
     independent of its rendered size. */
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-group {
    height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: 12px 10px; background: var(--border);
    font-size: 0; line-height: 0; color: transparent; overflow: hidden;
  }
 
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-logout { justify-content: center; padding: 10px 0; gap: 0; }
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-logout > span {
    position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
    overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
  }
 
  /* Sits between the ungrouped top row (Overview / AI Assistant) and the first labelled section,
     not in the footer — see `App.tsx`'s split `<Sidebar.Nav>` for why. Only a top margin is needed:
     `.cms-group`'s own `padding: 14px 10px 6px` already supplies the gap to the CONTENT heading
     below, so adding a bottom margin here would double it. */
  .cms-rail-toggle-row { display: flex; margin: 8px 0 0; }
  /* One glyph, two states — rotated 180° rather than swapped for a second icon, since the shape
     (two chevrons pointing away from each other / toward each other) reads correctly either way. */
  .cms-nav.is-rail .cms-rail-toggle svg { transform: rotate(180deg); }
}
 
/* ============================================================
   RESPONSIVE SHELL — the app had zero @media queries before this pass; below ~900px the fixed
   232px sidebar plus 2rem/2.5rem content padding left an unusable sliver of content width (a
   390px phone viewport had ~150px left after the sidebar). Two breakpoints:
 
   - 900px  — "sidebar must transform" per the design brief: the always-visible sidebar becomes
     an off-canvas drawer behind a mobile top bar. Chosen because 900×800 was the stated tablet
     canary viewport and is exactly where the fixed sidebar starts costing more width than a
     dense admin table can spare; nothing below this needs to change yet, so a 380px docked chat
     pane still fits the remaining ~520px comfortably.
   - 640px  — the docked chat pane (`.admin-chat-dock`, fixed 380px per ADR-049) stops fitting
     next to any usable content column, so it becomes a full-screen overlay instead of a sliver.
     Kept as a second, narrower breakpoint rather than folding into the 900px one because a
     900-640px viewport (most tablets in portrait) has room for both the collapsed sidebar drawer
     AND a still-docked 380px chat pane at the same time.
   ============================================================ */
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .admin-topbar {
    display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3);
    padding: 0 var(--space-4); height: 52px; flex-shrink: 0;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface);
    position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 20;
  }
 
  /* Off-canvas drawer. `position: fixed` pulls the sidebar out of `.admin-layout`'s flex row
     entirely, so `.admin-main-col` reclaims the full width instead of leaving a 232px gap.
 
     `visibility` (not just `transform`) gates the closed state: a translated-off-screen element
     is still in the tab order and still exposed to screen readers, so a keyboard user tabbing
     past the topbar toggle would land in a sidebar they cannot see. The `visibility` transition
     is delayed on the way OUT (`0.2s` — matches the slide) so the drawer stays visible for its
     own closing animation, and instant on the way IN so it is interactive the moment it starts
     appearing. */
  .cms-nav {
    position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 272px; z-index: 50;
    transform: translateX(-100%);
    visibility: hidden;
    transition: transform 0.2s ease, visibility 0s linear 0.2s;
    box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-mobile-panel-shadow);
  }
  .cms-nav.is-open {
    transform: translateX(0);
    visibility: visible;
    transition: transform 0.2s ease, visibility 0s linear 0s;
  }
  .cms-nav-mobile-head {
    display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between;
    padding: 2px 10px 12px; margin-bottom: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  }
  .cms-nav-mobile-head span {
    font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--faint);
  }
 
  .admin-content { padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-4); }
}
 
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  /* Bottom sheet instead of the 380px docked pane or a full-screen takeover (MSG-06). Full-screen
     was rejected deliberately, not just for space: `App.tsx` mounts `createDomPageDriver` scoped
     to `<main>`, so the assistant's `page.navigate`/`page.find_elements` calls visibly act on
     whatever is behind the chat — covering the entire viewport would hide the exact surface the
     agent is manipulating and break that feedback loop. A partial-height sheet keeps `<main>`
     in view underneath it.
 
     `.admin-chat-dock`/`.chat-fab` are defined (unconditionally) in `styles/assistant.css`,
     loaded via a separate import in `AssistantDock.tsx` rather than this file — scoped under
     `.admin-layout` here so this override wins on specificity regardless of which of the two
     stylesheets' `<style>` tag lands later in the document.
 
     Open/close itself is intentionally NOT animated (still the plain `hidden` attribute →
     `display: none` from `App.tsx`, unchanged) — only the default↔expanded HEIGHT transition
     below is. Animating the open/close edge as well would need replacing `hidden`'s `display:
     none` with `visibility`/`transform`/`inert` (that combination cannot itself transition), which
     is a real feature, not a drive-by addition; disclosed as deferred in the handoff rather than
     bolted on incompletely. `hidden` already keeps the closed sheet out of the tab order and the
     accessibility tree for free (no rendering at all), which is the load-bearing requirement here. */
  .admin-layout {
    /* Shared with the padding-reservation rules below so the two snap heights can't drift apart. */
    --chat-sheet-peek: 58vh;
    --chat-sheet-expanded: 92vh;
  }
  .admin-layout .admin-chat-dock {
    position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; top: auto;
    z-index: 55; flex: none; width: 100%; border-left: none;
    border-top: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-panel-border); border-radius: 14px 14px 0 0;
    box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-mobile-panel-shadow);
    flex-direction: column;
    height: var(--chat-sheet-peek);
    transition: height 0.2s ease;
  }
  .admin-layout .admin-chat-dock.is-expanded { height: var(--chat-sheet-expanded); }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
    .admin-layout .admin-chat-dock { transition: none; }
  }
 
  .admin-content { padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-3); }
 
  /* FAB clearance (mobile catalog P-1, 2026-10-06): with the sheet CLOSED the 56px `.chat-fab`
     sits fixed over the bottom-right of the page, and at max scroll it covered the last ~70px —
     row icons, footnotes, and on the form editor the page's own Save button. Closed-sheet padding
     reserves the FAB plus its inset and a gap, including the device's safe area. An open sheet
     keeps the taller scrollable spacer below, which avoids growing a short flex pane. */
  .admin-content::after { content: ""; display: block; flex-shrink: 0; height: var(--assistant-clearance); }
  .admin-layout:not(:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open)) .admin-content {
    padding-bottom: calc(var(--assistant-clearance) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px));
  }
  .admin-layout:not(:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open)) .admin-content::after { display: none; }
  /* Same clearance for the fixed-height tab panels that scroll on their own (Settings; Agent
     Plugins is page flow since AP-3): their last rows sat under the FAB at the panel's own max scroll, which the spacer
     above cannot reach. Page-flow panels scroll with the page, so they are left alone. */
  .settings-ui-section:not(.settings-ui-section--page-flow):not(.skills-page, .agent-plugins-section) .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { padding-bottom: 88px; }
 
  /* Owner repro, 2026-08-26: the sheet covers the bottom of the page with nothing left to scroll
     into, so the last elements can never clear it. An `::after` spacer (not `padding-bottom`)
     reserves that room: padding has a hard floor at its own value — on a short viewport with the
     sheet expanded, `padding-bottom: 92vh` plus the existing padding-top exceeds `.admin-content`'s
     entire flex-allotted height, which forces the box itself taller and pushes its true bottom
     edge below the viewport (measured at 375x667: box overflowed by ~15px, leaving the last row
     still 14px under the sheet at max scroll). A spacer is ordinary scrollable content instead, so
     `overflow-y: auto` clips it like any other content and the box never grows past its own height.
     `.admin-chat-dock` isn't a DOM sibling of `.admin-content` (it sits next to `.admin-main-col`,
     `.admin-content`'s parent), hence `:has()` on the shared ancestor. */
  .admin-layout:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open) .admin-content::after {
    content: ""; display: block; height: var(--chat-sheet-peek);
  }
  .admin-layout:has(.admin-chat-dock.is-open.is-expanded) .admin-content::after {
    height: var(--chat-sheet-expanded);
  }
 
  /* Bug fix (owner repro, 2026-08-26): the FAB's default (undragged) bottom-right position only
     avoids the SHEET's own box (`avoidBottomPx` in `App.tsx`/`useFabPosition`) — it has no idea
     where page content sits, so it rests directly above the sheet's top edge, squarely on top of
     whatever card/form is in the ~42vh still exposed above it (measured live: it sat on top of
     the Taxonomy page's "New term" card at 414x896). `.chat-sheet-bar` already renders its own
     close button whenever the sheet is open (see `App.tsx`'s `<aside>`), so the FAB is fully
     redundant here, not just misplaced — hiding it removes the overlap instead of trying to
     out-guess every page's layout with smarter avoidance math. Scoped to `.is-open` only (not
     `.is-expanded`): the sheet bar's close button is present in both the peek and expanded
     states, so the FAB should disappear in both. Closing the sheet drops `.is-open`, so the
     ordinary bottom-right FAB reappears immediately to reopen it. Operator's choice since
     2026-10-06 (Settings → User Interface, default on = this hide); see `styles/assistant.css`. */
  .admin-layout.hides-fab-while-open .admin-chat-dock.is-open + .chat-fab { display: none; }
}
 
/* Sheet chrome (drag handle, title, expand/close) — App.tsx-rendered, sitting above
   `<AssistantDock>` rather than inside it (that component stays untouched, per ADR-049's "never
   unmount" — its own internals are not where this dispatch's changes belong). Hidden at desktop
   widths: the docked panel has no sheet states and closes only via the FAB, same as before. */
.chat-sheet-bar { display: none; }
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .chat-sheet-bar {
    display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); position: relative;
    padding: 8px var(--space-3) 4px;
    /* Overrides `styles/assistant.css`'s `.admin-chat-dock > * { flex: 1; ... }`, which is meant
       for the pane's own root filling the dock — without this override that generic rule would
       also apply here (this bar is now a sibling direct child) and let the bar itself stretch to
       fill the dock's height instead of staying a fixed-size header row. Specificity (3 classes)
       beats that rule regardless of the two stylesheets' load order, same reasoning as the other
       `.admin-layout`-scoped overrides in this section. */
    flex: 0 0 auto;
  }
  .chat-sheet-handle {
    position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 6px; transform: translateX(-50%);
    width: 32px; height: 4px; border-radius: var(--r-pill); background: var(--border-strong);
  }
  .chat-sheet-bar-title {
    font-size: var(--text-xs); font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted); flex: 1; padding-top: 6px;
  }
  .chat-sheet-bar-actions { display: flex; gap: var(--space-1); padding-top: 2px; }
  .chat-sheet-action {
    background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid transparent;
    width: 28px; height: 28px; padding: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  }
  .chat-sheet-action:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
  .chat-sheet-action svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; }
}
 
/* Content bits */
/* Left-accent-border idiom retired 2026-08-31 (owner: "I also wanna get rid of that left accent
   border. I don't like it at all") — was a 3px `border-left` on the base rule, recolored per
   variant (`--border-strong` neutral / `--danger` error / `--warning` warning). Replaced with a
   FULL border in the variant's own color: `.notice` already changes `background`+`color` per
   variant (the danger/warning tint and text color below are unchanged), so the border was always a
   second, redundant expression of the same signal, not the only one — making it symmetric instead
   of left-only loses no information. The neutral base variant (no `.error`/`.warning`) had no tint
   of its own to fall back on, so its border stays `--border-strong` (was already the left edge's
   color) rather than the plain `--border` every bare `.card` uses, so an unmodified `.notice` still
   reads as a slightly more emphatic box than a plain card, just without a directional rail. */
.notice { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border-radius: var(--r-md); color: var(--fg-2); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }
.notice.error { border-color: var(--danger); background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.notice.warning { border-color: var(--warning); background: var(--warning-bg); color: var(--warning); margin: 0.6rem 0; }
.notice.warning label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--fg-2); cursor: pointer; }
/* Banner action pairs (2026-09-16) — the editors' notices put their buttons straight after the
   message (Load latest / Keep my edits, Restore / Discard, Save anyway / Keep editing), and JSX
   leaves no whitespace between them, so each pair rendered touching. Same `--space-2` step
   `.card-head-actions` uses for its buttons. Direct children only: a notice that lays its buttons out
   in its own flex row already has a gap. */
.notice.warning > .btn-secondary + .btn-secondary,
.notice.error > .btn-secondary + .btn-secondary { margin-left: var(--space-2); }
/* Recovery's top-of-screen degraded banner (2026-09-10, owner: read as plain text, not a boxed
   card) — `DegradedBannerView` in `Recovery.tsx`. (Its sibling `RestoreCapabilityNotice` got this
   same treatment the same day, then was cut outright — "seems useless" — later the same day; this
   modifier stays, since `DegradedBannerView` still needs it.) Scoped modifier rather than touching
   `.notice`/`.card` themselves, which stay card-shaped everywhere else in this admin.
   `.notice.recovery-plain-notice` matches `.notice.warning`/`.notice.error`'s own specificity
   (two classes) and is declared after both, so it wins the box-model tie — background/border/
   shadow/padding/margin all go to nothing — but it deliberately never sets `color`, so a toned
   banner (amber warning / red error) still carries that tone as its text color: the owner asked for
   the box gone, not the visual weight a real, disclosed limitation like this one still needs. */
.notice.recovery-plain-notice { background: transparent; border: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat); padding: 0; border-radius: 0; margin: 0; }
.list-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); overflow: hidden; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }
.list-table th, .list-table td { text-align: left; padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); }
.list-table th { background: var(--surface-2); font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted); }
/* Posts list's sortable "Updated" column header (2026-08-10) — a `<button>` sitting inside a
   `<th>`, not a `<td>`, so the row-action reset above (`.list-table td button...`) does not reach
   it; this rule inherits the `<th>`'s own type treatment instead of the default filled-primary
   button chrome, so the column heading still reads as a heading with a click affordance, not a
   loose CTA floating in the table header. */
.sortable-column-header {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 2px;
  background: transparent; border: none; padding: 0; margin: 0;
  font: inherit; text-transform: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit; color: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.sortable-column-header:hover, .sortable-column-header:focus-visible { color: var(--fg); opacity: 1; }
.list-table tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: none; }
.list-table tbody tr:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
/* Row actions default to a quiet/secondary treatment instead of inheriting the bare `button`
   rule's filled-primary orange. A table of N rows each carrying a row action (`/admin/users`:
   "New user" plus 4× "Disable" plus 4× "Manage" — nine identically loud buttons on one screen)
   is the flatness problem the burnt-orange primary was supposed to fix, just recolored. Scoped to
   `td` specifically so header-row/toolbar CTAs ("New Post", "Upload", "Add redirect" — none of
   which live inside a `<td>`) keep their primary treatment; this is a STRUCTURAL rule, so it
   reaches every section sharing `.list-table` (~15) with zero `.tsx` edits, and it composes with
   `.list-table td { padding: ... }` above rather than duplicating it.
 
   `:not([class*="btn-"])` is the load-bearing part: it excludes any button that already opted
   into an explicit variant (Media's `.btn-secondary`/`.btn-danger` Edit/Trash) so those keep
   their own intentional color. Excluding by selector rather than relying on a specificity fight
   matters here — `.list-table td button` alone is (0,1,2), which actually OUTRANKS a bare
   `.btn-danger` (0,1,0) on the same element, so without the `:not()` this rule would have quietly
   overridden every explicit variant it was never meant to touch.
 
   `.link-button` needs its own exclusion rather than riding on the `btn-` substring test: the
   class name contains "button" but not "btn-", so the attribute check does not catch it, and this
   rule silently drew a bordered box around every username in Users. Any future link-styled row
   control must be added here too — a new class alone will lose to this selector.
 
   CSS cannot tell "Disable" from "Manage" apart by meaning, so every unclassed row button lands
   on the same quiet treatment — a safe default, not a claim that they're equally weighted. Per-
   action semantic promotion (a genuinely destructive or access-affecting row action earning
   `.btn-danger` or the `.btn-warning` scaffold below) needs the owning section's own markup and
   is phase 2 — see the report's hierarchy-spec section. */
.list-table td button:not([class*="btn-"]):not(.link-button) {
  background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong);
}
.list-table td button:not([class*="btn-"]):not(.link-button):hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
/* Collision on file, named per this comment block's own convention: `ThemePagesTab.tsx`'s Publish
   switch (`.theme-explore-switch`, reused verbatim from `ThemeExplore.tsx`'s toolbar toggle) sits
   inside a `.list-table td` same as every other row control, so this reset's `:not([class*="btn-"])`
   matched it too — silently flattening its on/off/disabled background to this rule's flat
   `var(--surface)` regardless of state (owner-reported bug, 2026-08-31: a locked-ON switch read as
   indistinguishable from a genuinely-off one). Fixed the same way as every other exception on this
   selector: `ThemePagesTab.tsx` adds `btn-toggle-switch` (a marker class with no rules of its own) to
   that button, which is enough for `[class*="btn-"]` to exclude it — no `!important`, no reordering,
   no `.list-table`-scoped override to win a specificity fight against this rule. */
 
/* Row-scoped destructive/warning actions — quiet at rest, loud on intent.
   The rule above demotes UNCLASSED row buttons, which left the opposite problem for the classed
   ones: `.btn-danger`'s resting state is a full red outline, so a nine-row Posts table painted
   nine red boxes and the most visually dominant thing on a content list was the way to destroy
   its rows. The primary "New Post" CTA lost to a wall of red it had to compete with.
 
   Resting state keeps `.btn-danger`'s red TEXT (the semantic signal survives — this still does not
   read as a neutral action) but drops the box. Hover/focus restores the full outline, and the armed
   state goes solid-filled, which is the one moment the control genuinely should be the loudest
   thing on screen: the operator's next click destroys something.
 
   Keyed on `[data-armed]` from `ConfirmButton`, so this only escalates for a control that has
   actually been armed — a plain non-confirming `.btn-danger` in a row still gets the quiet
   resting treatment and its hover outline.
 
   Specificity: `.list-table td .btn-danger` is (0,2,1), which clears both bare `.btn-danger`
   (0,1,0) and the demotion rule above (0,1,2). Scoped to `td` for the same reason that rule is —
   a header/toolbar destructive action ("Purge all", "Delete workspace") is a deliberate, singular
   page-level decision and keeps its full weight. */
.list-table td .btn-danger,
.list-table td .btn-warning {
  background: transparent; border-color: transparent;
}
.list-table td .btn-danger:hover,
.list-table td .btn-danger:focus-visible { background: var(--danger-bg); border-color: var(--danger); }
.list-table td .btn-warning:hover,
.list-table td .btn-warning:focus-visible { background: var(--warning-bg); border-color: var(--warning); }
.list-table td .btn-danger[data-armed="true"] {
  background: var(--danger); border-color: var(--danger); color: var(--accent-ink); font-weight: 600;
}
.list-table td .btn-warning[data-armed="true"] {
  background: var(--warning); border-color: var(--warning); color: var(--accent-ink); font-weight: 600;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] .list-table td .btn-danger[data-armed="true"],
:root[data-theme="dark"] .list-table td .btn-warning[data-armed="true"] { color: var(--accent-ink); }
.status { padding: 0.15rem 0.55rem; border-radius: var(--r-pill); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; }
.status-published { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-draft { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
/* A disabled form is switched off, not failed or destructive — so it takes the same muted
   treatment as `.status-draft`/`.status-sub-paused`, not the danger tone. This had no rule at all
   until Forms grew a row menu that can actually reach the disabled state: before that, nothing in
   the app could render a non-active form pill, so the gap never showed. */
.status-disabled { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
 
/* Media (ADR-027 walking skeleton) */
.status-active { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-trashed { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.media-edit-row td { background: var(--surface-2); padding-top: 0.8rem; padding-bottom: 0.8rem; }
.media-edit-row .collections-field-row { border: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; background: transparent; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat); }
.media-edit-row .collections-field-row label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--fg-2); }
 
/* Integrations (webhook subscriptions + delivery log) */
/* `.integrations-tab-body` carried no layout rules of its own (a bare `<div>`), so its children —
   the intro line, the create form, the table/empty-state — stacked with whatever margin each one
   happened to bring, which for the intro's "Add webhook" button and the empty-state card under it
   was none: the button sat glued to the card's top edge (owner, 2026-09-13, screenshot
   `30-webhooks-empty-state-still-poor.png`). `gap: var(--space-6)` is `.page`'s own between-section
   rhythm (styles.css's `.page` rule, above) — reused rather than invented, so this tab reads at the
   same rhythm as the page shell it sits under. Flex column, not a stack of individual margins, so a
   future section added here inherits the same gap for free instead of needing its own margin-top. */
.integrations-tab-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-6); }
/* Same owner report, second half ("the intro sentence, the button, and the card all have different
   widths"): the intro paragraph ran the tab body's full width while the create form and the
   empty-state card both stop at `form-measure` (42rem) — three different widths reading as three
   unrelated objects instead of one column. Capping the intro at the same measure (`form-measure`
   class, applied at the JSX call site) is the fix; this rule only adds the vertical gap between the
   sentence and the button row, matching `.page`'s tighter `--space-3` used between a heading and
   its immediate description elsewhere in this file. */
.integrations-tab-intro { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
.status-sub-active { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-sub-paused { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
.status-sub-disabled { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.status-delivery-delivered { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-delivery-pending, .status-delivery-delivering { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
.status-delivery-failed, .status-delivery-dead { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.status-delivery-canceled { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--faint); }
 
/* Deployment (Overview tab) — `.status-ok`/`.status-warning` reuse the same tone tokens
   `.status-published`/`.notice.warning` already use elsewhere; new names because this tab's rows
   (gate passed/not-applicable, daemon known-failure, env var set/unsafe) don't map onto any
   existing published/active/trashed vocabulary above. */
.status-ok { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-warning { background: var(--warning-bg); color: var(--warning); }
.status-neutral { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
.muted-cell { color: var(--faint); font-size: 0.85rem; }
.integrations-form { margin-bottom: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: flex-start; }
/* Same consolidation as `.login-card label` above. */
.integrations-form label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.25rem; font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); width: 100%; max-width: 28rem; }
/* Roles.tsx `PolicyPermissionList` — a bare `<ul>`/`<li>` with no rule of its own here, so the
   `<code>`, optional `(resourceType)` span, and Remove button ran together in normal inline flow
   with zero gap between them (visual QA, 2026-08-31). Same `list-style: none; margin: 0; padding:
   0; display: flex; flex-direction: column;` idiom `.settings-row-list`/`.deployment-env-list`
   already use elsewhere in this file, not a bespoke shape. */
.permission-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; }
.permission-list li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }
/* The "Permission"/"resource type (optional)" input pair (same `PolicyPermissionForm`) has no
   width rule of its own either, so both fall back to the browser's default ~161px input size
   regardless of placeholder length — long enough for "e.g. content.write" but not for "resource
   type (optional)", which read as clipped mid-word. `flex: 1 1 12rem` lets each grow to fill the
   row's leftover space; `min-width: 0` overrides the browser's flex-item default of `min-width:
   auto` (which floors at content size and would otherwise defeat this), same reasoning as
   `.editor-slug input`'s mobile rule above. Own class rather than `.integrations-form
   .editor-actions input` — that combinator also matches Users.tsx's single-input email-edit row
   (`UserManagePanel`), a different screen this pass didn't touch or visually verify. */
.permission-form-fields input { flex: 1 1 12rem; min-width: 0; }
 
/* Dashboard
   The previous version was three `.dash-card`s in an auto-fit grid, and the grid was the whole
   screen — everything below the first 200px was empty. Worse, the three cards disagreed about what
   a card IS: one held a count, one held a theme name rendered at `font-size: 2rem` (display type on
   a proper noun, which is why "Tovu-Official" dominated a screen it should not have), and one held
   a bare sentence with no value at all. Nothing lined up because nothing was the same shape.
 
   Split into two things with two jobs: `.dash-stat` is strictly ONE NUMBER and its label — no
   exceptions, which is what makes a row of them scan — and `.dash-panel` carries everything that
   is prose, a list, or a name. The theme moved into a panel for exactly that reason. */
/* History: owner 2026-10-06 first capped this at a fixed 2x2, `max-width: 34rem` — four one-number
   cards stretched across the full width read as wide empty boxes (the older `auto-fit,
   minmax(12rem, 1fr)` went 4-across on wide screens and 1-per-row on a phone). The desktop bug hunt
   (D-30, same day) then reported that 2x2 as leaving half of a 1360px window blank. Now: two compact
   columns in narrow panes (still 2-up on a 375px phone, where the tighter padding below keeps
   "items in the library" from crowding the edge), four once the PANE (a container query, so the
   dock/sidebar width counts) passes 800px, and bounded by the shared content measure so a single
   count never becomes an unbounded box. */
.dashboard-page { container-type: inline-size; }
/* 2026-10-27 (owner): the four counts are ONE card — cells split by 1px dividers (the grid gap shows
   the card's `--border` background through) — with Appearance beside it on wide panes. Cells are 4x1
   above 600px of pane, 2x2 below; Appearance drops under the card below 1040px. */
/* Owner 10-27: both cards are capped (~10rem per count, Appearance 24rem beside) so they don't stretch across a wide pane. */
.dash-top { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 40rem); justify-content: start; gap: var(--space-4); align-items: stretch; width: 100%; }
@container (min-width: 1040px) { .dash-top { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 40rem) minmax(0, 24rem); } }
/* Owner 10-27: Appearance keeps its 24rem width when it drops under the counts, too. */
.dash-top > .dash-panel { width: 100%; max-width: 24rem; }
.dash-stats {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 1px; overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--border); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
}
@container (min-width: 600px) { .dash-stats { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); } }
 
/* The default-password nag: a compact one-row plain `.notice` (neutral surface + hairline), with
   the icon as its only `--warning` accent — owner: "cap the width" and "make it subtle". The link
   and the × share one muted-to-fg text treatment so they read as a pair. Wraps under ~560px.
   `margin: 0` — `.page`'s own flex `gap` already spaces it; a bottom margin on top of that left
   40px under the banner against 24px above it (owner 2026-10-06 header tidy). */
.notice.dash-password-banner {
  display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-3);
  max-width: 680px; min-height: 44px; box-sizing: border-box;
  margin: 0; padding: 0.45rem 0.5rem 0.45rem 0.85rem;
  border-color: var(--border); box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat); font-size: var(--text-sm);
}
.dash-password-banner p { flex: 1 1 16rem; margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); }
.dash-password-banner-icon { display: inline-flex; color: var(--warning); }
.dash-password-banner-action { font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg); white-space: nowrap; }
.dash-password-banner-action:hover { color: var(--link); text-decoration: underline; }
.dash-password-banner-dismiss {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 28px; height: 28px;
  padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: var(--r-sm); background: transparent; color: var(--muted); cursor: pointer;
}
.dash-password-banner-dismiss:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); }
.dash-password-banner-dismiss:focus-visible, .dash-password-banner-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--link); outline-offset: 2px; }
 
/* "Publish All" and "View site ↗" share ONE row — owner 2026-10-06, replacing the column this
   modifier used to force ("Publish Content" stacked under "View site", `align-items: flex-end`).
   That column is what looked broken on phones: once `.page-header` wrapped it under the subtitle,
   the right-aligned edges left "View site" indented above a wider Publish button. Plain
   `.page-actions` row behaviour fixes both widths — right side of the header on desktop
   (`.page-header`'s `justify-content: space-between`), left-aligned under the subtitle like every
   other screen's actions once it wraps. `flex-wrap: nowrap` keeps the pair together on a 375px
   phone, where both fit with room to spare. */
.dash-header-actions { flex-wrap: nowrap; }
 
/* An `<a>`, not a `<div>` — the number was already the answer to "how many posts", so the card is
   the natural way to go read them. Being a real link also means it is keyboard-reachable and
   announces as a link, which the old div-with-a-nested-"manage"-link was not. */
.dash-stat {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-1);
  background: var(--surface); padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5);
  transition: background 0.14s;
  color: inherit; text-decoration: none;
}
.dash-stat:hover { background: var(--surface-2); text-decoration: none; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .dash-stat { transition: none; } }
/* Phone padding for the 2-up stat grid above — after `.dash-stat` so it wins the cascade. */
/* Container (2026-10-11): keyed on the pane, like the 4-up rule above, so the tight padding also
   applies when the nav + dock leave a phone-width pane on desktop. 456px ≈ the old 480px viewport
   minus a phone's page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 456px) { .dash-stat { padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); } }
.dash-stat-label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--muted); }
/* `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` keeps a column of counts optically aligned as values change
   width (9 -> 10 -> 100) instead of the digits shifting under each other. */
.dash-stat-value {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.1;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--fg); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.dash-stat-meta { font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); }
/* A failed stat still renders its card at full size — the value becomes an em-dash and the reason
   takes the meta slot. The audit's finding here (exec summary #5) was that a failure was SILENT,
   not that it was quiet: replacing the card with a full-width error banner would fix the silence by
   destroying the grid, so the honest state has to fit in the space the healthy state occupies. */
.dash-stat-value.is-error { color: var(--faint); }
.dash-stat-meta.is-error { color: var(--danger); }
 
/* Everything that is not a single number. `minmax(0, …)` on both tracks lets a long title inside
   the activity list ellipsize instead of forcing the column wider than its share. */
.dash-panels { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: var(--space-4); align-items: start; }
/* Container (2026-10-11): 800px ≈ the old 1100px viewport minus the expanded nav and page padding
   (1100 − 232 − 80) — the width the two panels actually had when that breakpoint was picked. With
   the dock open the viewport query kept them side by side in a ~590px pane. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 800px) { .dash-panels { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); } }
.dash-panel { background: var(--jini-panel-bg); border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-panel-border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow); overflow: hidden;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.dash-panel-head {
  display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.dash-panel-title { font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg); margin: 0; }
.dash-panel-body { padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
.dash-panel-body p { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
/* "Recently updated" accordion header (owner 2026-10-13). Resets the bare-`button` primary fill
   so the title reads as a heading, not a CTA; the focus ring is the app-wide `:focus-visible` one.
   Collapsed, the head's bottom border would double up against the card's own, so it drops. */
.dash-panel-toggle {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2);
  background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; color: inherit; font: inherit; letter-spacing: inherit;
}
.dash-panel-toggle:hover { opacity: 1; color: var(--primary); }
.dash-panel-caret { display: inline-flex; color: var(--muted); transition: transform 0.15s ease; }
.dash-panel-toggle[aria-expanded="true"] .dash-panel-caret { transform: rotate(90deg); }
.dash-panel.is-collapsed .dash-panel-head { border-bottom: none; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .dash-panel-caret { transition: none; }
}
 
/* Activity rows. Grid rather than flex so the timestamp column is a fixed track and every row's
   time starts at the same x — with flex the times ragged-right against variable title lengths. */
.dash-activity { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.dash-activity-row {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) auto auto; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-5); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.dash-activity-row:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
.dash-activity-row:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
.dash-activity-title { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: var(--text-sm); }
.dash-activity-time { font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--faint); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
/* Distinguishes a page from a post in a merged list. Deliberately a neutral chip and not a
   `.status` pill — kind is not a lifecycle state, and reusing `.status` would make "page" read as
   if it were a peer of "published"/"draft". */
.dash-kind { font-size: var(--text-2xs); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted); background: var(--surface-3); padding: 0.1rem 0.4rem; border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
 
/* Editor */
/* `.editor-page` (the old `display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:0.9rem` outer wrapper) is
   removed as of this pass — its last four callers (MenuEditor/CollectionEntryEditor/
   WidgetInstanceEditor/WidgetRegionEditor) all moved onto `.page`, `PostEditor.tsx`'s own
   established precedent, leaving zero remaining callers app-wide (verified: grepped for it before
   deleting). `.editor-header` stays — `Database.tsx` and `Media.tsx` still use it and are outside
   this pass's scope. */
.editor-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; }
/* Before reaching for a top margin here: this class is doing three structurally unrelated jobs
   under one name (audited across all 37 call sites app-wide, not sampled), and "just add a
   margin" is wrong for most of them.
     1. Header action group — a `<div>` next to a "← Back" link inside the old `.editor-header`
        pattern (Database.tsx, Media.tsx today; MenuEditor/CollectionEntryEditor/
        WidgetInstanceEditor/WidgetRegionEditor used to, before this pass moved them onto
        `.page-header`/`.page-actions`, which needs no margin here at all).
     2. Bottom-of-form Save bar below the last field — also a `<div>`, and the ONLY role that
        actually wants a top margin (the "flush against the field above" bug). Two known callers,
        both fixed with their own scoped hook rather than a change here: `FormEditor.tsx`'s
        `.form-actions` and `CollectionEntryEditor.tsx`'s `.term-picker-actions`.
     3. Small inline flex group of 1-2 buttons inside a table row or compact form — a `<span>`,
        28 of the 37 call sites (Roles/Users/Taxonomy/Comments/Members/Collections/Media/Seo/
        Settings/WidgetPickerDialog). These sit inline next to other row content; a top margin
        here would misalign every one of them.
   The `<span>` vs `<div>` split is not a hard rule (case 1's header usage was a `<div>` too), but
   in practice every bottom-of-form case found so far has been a `<div>`. Check the actual
   surrounding markup before assuming which role a given caller is in. */
/* `flex-wrap: wrap` (web-design pass, 2026-08-26): narrow the admin content column enough — the
   assistant chat pane open plus a fully expanded sidebar is the reported case — and a row that mixes
   a text `<input>` with 1-2 buttons (`Taxonomy.tsx`'s `NewTermForm`/`NewTaxonomyForm` being the
   found case) no longer fits on one line. Every element here has `overflow: visible` up to the
   parent `.card`/`.taxonomy-namespace-group`, so with `nowrap` the overflow doesn't scroll or clip —
   it bleeds out past the card's own border, left AND right, which is the actual bug (a static
   border-box measurement of the card and the form both nest correctly; it's this row's rendered
   CONTENT that escapes). Wrapping the row onto a second line keeps every child inside the card at
