   any width instead. Harmless for the ~30 button-only callers this class already has: none of them
   are wide enough to trigger a wrap at any width this app supports, so this is a no-op for them. */
.editor-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: center; }
.save-ok { color: var(--ok); font-size: 0.85rem; }
.save-error { color: var(--danger); font-size: 0.85rem; }
.save-warning { color: var(--warning); font-size: 0.85rem; }
.editor-title { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; padding: 0.6rem 0.2rem; width: 100%; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--fg); }
.editor-title::placeholder { color: var(--faint); font-weight: 500; }
.editor-title:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow); border-bottom-color: var(--accent-text); }
/* Title + slug on one row (2026-08-11), matching the Pages editor's `.page-title-row`. The cap
   targets `.editor-title` directly and NOT a class on its wrapping `<label>`: that label carries
   `.a11y-label-wrap` (`styles/editor.css`), which is `display: contents` precisely so the label
   drops out of the layout tree and the input becomes the row's real flex item — a `max-width` on the
   label would sit on a box that is never generated and silently do nothing. That exact mistake was
   made and caught on the Pages side, and only because `getBoundingClientRect` returned an all-zero
   rect; the screenshot looked identical either way. `flex: 1 1 50%` with `max-width: 50%` rather
   than a bare `width: 50%` lets the title grow into its half when the slug group is narrower,
   without ever exceeding it.
 
   `.editor-title` still carries its own `border-bottom` (above) everywhere else it's used bare
   (`MenuEditor.tsx`, `CollectionEntryEditor.tsx`, `WidgetInstanceEditor.tsx`, full-width, so the
   line already spans the whole control) — capping it to 50% width here made that same line stop
   dead in the middle of the row (caught live, 2026-08-11). A same-day fix moved the line off the
   input and onto `.editor-title-row` itself so it spanned both halves as one continuous rule.
   REVERTED the same day, on a second look: spanning the slug half made the rule read as a
   structural divider for the whole row, which drew the eye to the slug group as though it too sat
   "under a line" — a boundary the slug was never meant to have. The owner's actual read of the
   half-width version was not "broken", it was "looks like it was truncated by accident" — i.e. a
   presentation problem (an unstyled hairline stopping with nothing to explain why it stops there),
   not a correctness one.
 
   Tried recoloring the rest state to `--accent-text` first — rejected after checking computed
   style: this theme's `--accent-text` resolves to oklch(26% 0.006 260), a near-black practically
   indistinguishable from `--fg`'s own oklch(24% 0.022 262), so it read as "bolder line", not
   "accent". Worse, `.editor-title:focus` (two lines up) ALREADY uses `--accent-text` as its only
   focus signal on this field (`outline: none; box-shadow: none`) — recoloring the resting state to
   the same token would have made focus invisible on this control, trading a cosmetic fix for an
   accessibility regression.
 
   Landed on a left-to-right fade instead (`border-image`, not `border-bottom-color`): solid for the
   first ~65% of the input's width, fading to transparent at the edge. Verified live, side by side —
   a hard-edged hairline reads as clipped, the same fade with a soft trailing edge reads as a
   deliberate typographic accent (the same idiom pull-quote rules and section dividers use to taper
   rather than stop dead). `border-image` takes over painting that edge entirely once set, so
   `border-bottom-color` above no longer has anything to change on `:focus` — the dedicated
   `:focus` override below swaps the gradient's solid stop to `--accent-text` so the focus affordance
   this input already had is preserved, just carried by the gradient instead of a flat color. Width
   still tracks `.editor-title`'s own rendered box exactly (flex/max-width below) — the fade is
   layered on top of that box, not measured independently, so it can't drift from it. */
.editor-title-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-4, 1rem); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.editor-title-row .editor-title {
  flex: 1 1 50%; max-width: 50%; min-width: 0;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-image: linear-gradient(to right, var(--border) 65%, transparent) 1;
}
.editor-title-row .editor-title:focus {
  border-image: linear-gradient(to right, var(--accent-text) 65%, transparent) 1;
}
.editor-slug { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.85rem; display: flex; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; row-gap: 0.4rem; }
.editor-slug input { width: 14rem; }
.editor-id { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; margin-left: 0.5rem; padding-left: 1rem; border-left: 1px solid var(--border); }
.editor-id input { width: 9rem; background: transparent; border: none; color: var(--muted); font: 12px/1 var(--font-mono, monospace); padding: 0; cursor: text; }
.editor-id input:focus { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow); }
/* `display: flex` added for the "View Template" button (2026-08-10) sitting next to the `<select>`
   — before this the picker's only visible child was the `<select>` itself, so nothing here relied
   on a layout mode; a bare `<select>` and `<button>` both default to `inline-block`, which would
   sit them side by side with no controlled gap. `align-items: center` keeps the button's own
   padding from making it taller than the select and pushing it out of vertical alignment. */
.editor-template-picker { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }
.editor-template-picker select { width: 14rem; font-size: 0.85rem; }
/* Icon-only "View Template" trigger (2026-09-22 owner ask, moved left of the picker and reduced
   from a `.btn-secondary` text button to an eye glyph). `width`/`height: 37px` matches the shared
   `input, select, textarea { min-height: 37px }` rule exactly (not the 2rem/32px
   `.theme-explore-fullscreen-trigger` uses elsewhere) so the square button lines up flush against
   the select's own edge instead of a couple pixels short. Colors are `.btn-secondary`'s own
   (`--surface`/`--fg-2`/`--border-strong`), since this button carried that class before and the
   owner's ask was icon-vs-word, not a restyle. */
.view-template-btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 37px; height: 37px; padding: 0; flex-shrink: 0;
  background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.view-template-btn svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
.view-template-btn:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-1); opacity: 1; }
.view-template-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }
/* Small screens (2026-08-09 live feedback): the slug row was overflowing — the template picker got
   clipped off the right edge instead of wrapping to its own line, and the id block (no visible
   divider, see the JSX comment on `.editor-id`'s markup for why) sat crowded against "view". Stack
   into two clearly separated rows instead of trying to force three variable-width controls onto one
   line at narrow widths. Container, not viewport (2026-10-11): the slug row overflows the same way
   when the nav + dock leave a narrow pane on desktop. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  /* Same reasoning the Pages editor's equivalent rule gives: below this width two halves read as
     cramped rather than usable, and both are free-typed inputs. Stack them full-width instead. */
  .editor-title-row { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; }
  .editor-title-row .editor-title { max-width: 100%; }
  .editor-slug { justify-content: center; text-align: center; }
  .editor-id { margin-left: 0; padding-left: 0.75rem; justify-content: center; }
  .editor-template-picker select { width: 100%; }
  .editor-template-picker { flex-wrap: wrap; }
  /* `width: 100%` here (pre-2026-08-11) was the actual mobile bug: a full-width flex child inside
     `.editor-slug`'s wrapping row always isolates itself onto its own line, forcing the `/` prefix
     above it and `view ↗` below it — three stacked lines instead of one. `.editor-slug` is a flex
     container in its own right (not just the stacked group above it), so the input only needs to
     SHRINK to share the row, not claim the whole row. `flex: 1 1 auto` lets it grow to fill the
     leftover space next to the tiny `/` and `view ↗` siblings while `min-width: 0` overrides the
     browser's default `min-width: auto` on flex items (which floors at the input's content size and
     is what was defeating plain `flex-shrink` here) so it can still shrink below that on the
     narrowest phones. Shared by both editors: Pages' `.page-title-row .editor-slug` and Posts'
     `.editor-title-row .editor-slug` both resolve to this same base `.editor-slug input` rule since
     neither stylesheet overrides the input's width, only the group's alignment. */
  .editor-slug input { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; }
}
 
/* Menu tree editor */
.menu-tree { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.6rem; }
/* A flex column defaults to `align-items: stretch` — correct for the `.menu-item-row` siblings
   (rows of fields that should span the full width) but not for the trailing "+ Add item" button,
   which stretched to the container's full content width (user report, with screenshot: "way too
   large... left align and cap it"). `align-self: flex-start` sizes it to its own content instead,
   satisfying both halves of the report without a `max-width` magic number. Scoped to a direct
   `.menu-tree` child rather than a new class on the element — `.menu-tree`'s only direct
   `.btn-secondary` child is this one button (verified: `.menu-item-row` isn't `.btn-secondary`, so
   this can't accidentally catch a row that wants to stay full-width). Same root cause and same fix
   shape as `.settings-scope-editor .btn-danger` below (another stretch-by-default flex column) —
   audited every other `flex-direction: column` rule in this file for the same pattern (a bare
   button as a direct child) and found no other live instance in a screen this pass owns; the
   `.settings-namespace-loader`/`.settings-principal-selector` forms already guard against it with
   their own explicit `align-items: flex-start`, and every other button-bearing container found
   wraps its buttons in an intermediate row-flex group (`.editor-actions`, `.page-actions`) rather
   than exposing them as direct flex-column children. */
.menu-tree > .btn-secondary { align-self: flex-start; }
.menu-item-row { position: relative; }
.menu-item-row + .menu-item-row { margin-top: 0.6rem; }
.menu-item-fields {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;
  background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  padding: 0.65rem 0.75rem; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm);
}
.menu-item-fields input, .menu-item-fields select { font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; }
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="Label"] { flex: 1 1 9rem; min-width: 7rem; }
.menu-item-fields select { flex: 0 0 auto; width: 6.5rem; }
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="https://…"],
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="route name"],
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="entry id"],
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="term id"],
.menu-item-fields input[placeholder="taxonomy"] { flex: 1 1 10rem; min-width: 8rem; }
.menu-item-fields .tb-btn { flex: 0 0 auto; }
/* Children get a left guide rule instead of bare indentation, so nesting reads visually. */
.menu-item-row[style*="margin-left"] { padding-left: 0.9rem; border-left: 2px solid var(--border); margin-top: 0.6rem; }
/* Phones (mobile catalog MN-2, 2026-10-06): each level's inline `marginLeft: depth * 20` compounds
   inside its parent row, so level-3 cards were ~190px wide and their controls reflowed differently
   at every depth. The guide rule already shows the nesting; one small step per level is enough
   (`!important` only because the depth margin is an inline style). Label + link type share line 1,
   the link target gets line 2 whole (the page select clipped to "Documentatio" at 6.5rem), and the
   move/child/remove buttons share line 3 with Remove pushed to the far end. Container (2026-10-11):
   a desktop pane squeezed by the nav + dock compounds the depth margins the same way. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .menu-item-row[style*="margin-left"] { margin-left: 0 !important; padding-left: var(--space-2); }
  .menu-item-fields { padding: 0.6rem; }
  .menu-item-fields > label:nth-of-type(n+3) :is(input, select) { flex: 1 1 100%; width: auto; min-width: 0; }
  .menu-item-fields > .tb-btn:last-child { margin-left: auto; }
}
.editor-shell { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }
/* Toolbar height (owner feedback on a screenshot, 2026-08-11: "~25% shorter" — two tall rows plus a
   character-count line ate too much vertical space above the writing area). Padding/gap trimmed
   here (8px 10px / 3px 8px -> 6px 8px / 2px 6px) together with `.tb-btn`/`.tb-color`/`.tb-select`
   dropping from a 30px to a 26px frame below is what actually delivers the reduction — this is a
   desktop admin, so 26px still clears a comfortable click/tap target and each control keeps its own
   `:hover`/`:focus-visible` treatment, nothing here removes those. Measured live (Playwright against
   a running admin, `.editor-toolbar`'s own `getBoundingClientRect().height` at a 1440px viewport,
   two toolbar rows wrapped at that width both before and after): 94px before this change, 67px
   after — a 29% reduction, past the ~25% ask. The `.tb-select` fix below (an app-wide `min-height:
   37px` reset was clamping every select regardless of this file's own `height`) is what closes most
   of the gap — without it the reduction was only ~5%, since the toolbar's own row height was still
   governed by its tallest child. */
.editor-toolbar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 2px 6px; padding: 6px 8px; background: var(--surface-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 2; }
/* Selection bubble menu (`BubbleFormattingMenu`, 2026-08-11) — `@tiptap/react/menus`' `BubbleMenu`
   positions this `<div>` itself (Floating UI under the hood); this rule only styles its contents,
   same `.tb-btn` row shape `.editor-toolbar .grp` already uses, just without that row's own
   border/background/sticky-positioning (a floating popover needs its OWN surface + shadow, not the
   toolbar's docked-bar chrome). `z-index` above `.editor-toolbar`'s own `2` since a selection near
   the top of the editor can float the bubble close to the sticky toolbar's edge. */
.bubble-formatting-menu {
  display: flex; gap: 2px; padding: 4px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: 9px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-md, var(--shadow-sm)); z-index: 3;
}
/* Drag handle (`PostEditor.tsx`, 2026-08-11) — `@tiptap/extension-drag-handle-react`'s own plugin
   positions the wrapping element itself (absolute, tracking whichever block is under the cursor);
   this only styles the grip icon inside it. `cursor: grab` signals the affordance since nothing
   else about a small dot-grid icon reads as draggable on its own. */
.editor-drag-handle { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; color: var(--faint); cursor: grab; border-radius: 5px; }
.editor-drag-handle:hover { color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2); }
.editor-drag-handle svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
.editor-toolbar .grp { display: flex; gap: 2px; padding-right: 8px; margin-right: 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--border); }
.editor-toolbar .grp:last-child { border-right: none; padding-right: 0; }
.tb-btn {
  min-width: 26px; height: 26px; padding: 0 7px; display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
  font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: transparent; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.12s, color 0.12s, border-color 0.12s;
}
.tb-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--surface); border-color: var(--border); }
.tb-btn.on { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--accent-text); }
.tb-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.38; cursor: default; }
.tb-btn i { font-style: italic; } .tb-btn s { text-decoration: line-through; }
/* Align-icon buttons (`PostEditor.tsx`'s `Toolbar`, 2026-08-11 — icons replacing the Left/Center/
   Right/Justify word labels) — same size band every other house SVG-in-button already uses
   (`.admin-topbar-toggle svg`, `.cms-item svg`, `.row-menu-trigger svg`: 16-18px). Scoped to
   `.tb-btn` generally rather than a new per-button class: no OTHER `.tb-btn` (Bold/Italic/H1/etc.)
   renders an `<svg>` today, so this can't accidentally resize a future icon button meant to be a
   different size without that button also opting into `.tb-btn`'s own 30px frame. `currentColor` on
   the `<svg>` itself (not here) is what makes the icon track `.tb-btn.on`'s active-state color swap
   for free. */
.tb-btn svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
/* Text/background color swatches (`PostEditor.tsx`'s `Toolbar`, 2026-08-11) — a native
   `<input type="color">` renders with no consistent cross-browser chrome on its own (a raw square
   with a visible native border in some browsers, none in others), so this wraps it in the same
   30px-tall frame every other `.tb-btn` already occupies and gives the input itself a small
   inset + border so it reads as "one more toolbar control", not a stray native form field.
   `.tb-color` (the `<label>` wrapper) itself was never the problem — it already measured exactly
   26px, matching `.tb-btn`.
   Swatch height (owner feedback on a screenshot, 2026-08-12: "half as tall") — this rule already
   said `height: 17px` and had said so since the first toolbar-polish pass, but that was never the
   REAL rendered height: measured live (Playwright against a running admin, `getComputedStyle` on
   the actual `<input type="color">`) at exactly 37px tall, visibly overflowing the 26px `.tb-color`
   frame above and below — "the rule is there" was not evidence it was winning, same trap this
   file's own `.tb-select` comment two rules down already documents and fixes for a DIFFERENT
   element. Identical root cause here: the app-wide `input, select, textarea { min-height: 37px;
   ... }` reset ("Shared page primitives" section, this file) floors every native `<input>`
   including `type="color"`, and `min-height` always wins over a smaller `height` regardless of
   selector specificity (used value is `max(height, min-height)` per spec). Re-declaring
   `min-height` here, not just `height`, is what actually un-clamps it.
 
   ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-12, second pass. The first attempt halved the AUTHORED 17px to 8.5px and
   produced two thin horizontal dashes — the owner's words: "you made the color boxes lines, that's
   ridiculous." The brief was wrong, not the execution. He asked for half the size of *what he could
   see*, and what he could see was the clamped 37px. So the target is half of 37, not half of 17.
   Halve the RENDERED value, never the authored one, whenever the two disagree — the owner is
   describing pixels on his screen, not a number in this file. 18.5px (exact half of the measured
   37px, not the rounded 18px an intermediate pass used) fits inside the 26px `.tb-color` frame with
   room to spare, verified live post-fix the same way the 37px was first found (`getComputedStyle` on
   the real `<input type="color">`, not read off this stylesheet) — same discipline, applied to the
   RIGHT number this time. Reads as a proper small colour chip, not a line. */
.tb-color { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; }
.tb-color input[type="color"] {
  width: 17px; height: 18.5px; min-height: 18.5px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 4px;
  cursor: pointer; background: none;
}
/* Font family/size/line-height `<select>`s (`Toolbar`, 2026-08-11) — sized to match `.tb-btn`'s own
   26px height so the row stays visually level; width left to content (`width: auto`) rather than a
   fixed value since "Sans-serif"/"Courier New" and "12"/"48" need very different widths and a
   shared fixed width would either clip the longest or waste space on the shortest. `min-height: 26px`
   + `line-height: 1` (toolbar-height pass, 2026-08-11) matter more than they look: this select
   measured 37px tall in a real browser (`getComputedStyle`) against `.tb-btn`'s exactly-26px, a
   mismatch that itself forced an extra row of wrap. Root cause traced live, not guessed — the
   app-wide `input, select, textarea { min-height: 37px; ... }` reset ("Shared page primitives"
   section, this file) floors EVERY select's height at 37px, and `min-height` always wins over a
   smaller `height` regardless of selector specificity (the used value is `max(height, min-height)`
   per spec). Re-declaring `min-height` here, not just `height`, is what actually un-clamps it;
   `line-height: 1` on top keeps the select's own intrinsic content-box height from independently
   exceeding that once the floor is gone. */
.tb-select {
  height: 26px; min-height: 26px; line-height: 1; padding: 0 6px; font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: 12px;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: transparent; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 6px;
  cursor: pointer; max-width: 9rem;
}
.tb-select:hover { background: var(--surface); border-color: var(--border); }
/* Dark mode (2026-10-15): the app-wide dark select rule re-adds its chevron image with a higher
   specificity than `.tb-select`, and `.tb-select`'s `background` shorthand had already reset the
   repeat, so the chevron tiled across every toolbar select. Light shows no chevron; match it. */
:root[data-theme="dark"] .tb-select { background-image: none; }
/* Select label pairing (toolbar polish, 2026-08-11 — owner: three `<select>`s that all read
   "Default" gave no clue which was font/size/line-height without hovering the `title`). Metrics
   copied from `.field-label` (this file's existing small-caption convention: uppercase, letter-
   spaced, muted) rather than a new ad hoc size, so this reads as "the same kind of label" as every
   other field caption in the admin, just inline instead of stacked above its control. */
.tb-select-group { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; }
.tb-select-label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
/* CharacterCount readout (`Toolbar`, 2026-08-11) — `margin-left: auto` pushes it to the far end of
   the flex-wrap row, trailing every button/select group rather than sitting between them. */
.editor-toolbar-count { margin-left: auto; padding: 0 4px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--faint); white-space: nowrap; }
/* Phones (2026-10-06 mobile catalog PO-2): wrapped, this toolbar was ~6 ragged rows (~200px) with
   items clipped at the right edge and labels breaking inside their buttons ("• / List"). One row that
   scrolls sideways instead, every group and label kept whole, buttons at a 40px touch size. Nothing
   in it positions out of the row (the Embed menu expands inline), so the scroller clips nothing.
   Split 2026-10-11: the one-scrolling-row LAYOUT follows the pane (container — a desktop pane
   squeezed by the nav + dock wrapped and clipped the same way), while the 40px TOUCH sizes stay a
   phone-only `@media` rule — a mouse on a narrow desktop pane does not need them.
   Replaced 2026-10-15 (owner: "so messed up, janky"). The sideways row hid most controls off-screen,
   and the 2026-10-13 wrap that followed it gave ~8 ragged rows (~530px) with separators dangling at
   row ends. Now the groups dissolve into one flow (no separators), only the `data-tb="primary"`
   controls show plus a "More" toggle, and More drops the rest in below a single rule, wrapped
   tightly. `order` keeps More at the end of the first row in both states; the `::after` break
   (a flex item too) is what forces the rest onto their own rows. Open, the toolbar stops being
   sticky — a ~250px band pinned over a phone screen would leave no room to write.
   2026-10-15 (owner: "move the 3 dots up to be flush with the top row"): at ~280px the six fixed
   primaries filled the row and More wrapped under them. `useToolbarOverflow` now measures the row
   and only marks as many ranked controls `primary` as fit beside More; the rest join the overflow.
   The row's slack is spread between its items (auto margins resolve per flex line, so only the top
   row spreads; the overflow rows stay packed left), keeping B flush left and More flush right. */
.editor-toolbar .tb-more { display: none; }
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .editor-toolbar { gap: 2px; }
  .editor-toolbar .grp { display: contents; }
  .editor-toolbar .grp > *, .editor-toolbar-count { order: 1; }
  .editor-toolbar .grp > [data-tb="primary"] { order: 0; }
  .editor-toolbar .tb-more { display: inline-grid; order: 0; margin-left: auto; }
  .editor-toolbar .grp > [data-tb="primary"]:not([data-tb-rank="0"]) { margin-left: auto; }
  .editor-toolbar .tb-btn { white-space: nowrap; }
  .editor-toolbar:not([data-more-open="true"]) .grp > :not([data-tb="primary"]),
  .editor-toolbar:not([data-more-open="true"]) .editor-toolbar-count { display: none; }
  .editor-toolbar[data-more-open="true"] { position: static; }
  .editor-toolbar[data-more-open="true"]::after { content: ""; order: 0; flex-basis: 100%; height: 0; margin-block: 2px; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
  .editor-toolbar[data-more-open="true"] .tb-more { background: var(--surface); border-color: var(--border); }
  /* Open, the count wraps onto its own last row; pushed right there it sat under the floating chat
     button (owner 2026-10-16: the FAB covered "910 characters"). Left, it starts the row instead. */
  .editor-toolbar[data-more-open="true"] .editor-toolbar-count { margin-left: 0; }
}
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .editor-toolbar .tb-btn { min-width: 44px; height: 44px; white-space: nowrap; }
  .editor-toolbar .tb-color { width: 44px; height: 44px; }
  .editor-toolbar .tb-select { height: 44px; min-height: 44px; }
}
/* Placeholder (`Toolbar`, 2026-08-11) — the extension's own default class/attribute names
   (`is-empty`, `data-placeholder`) kept as-is rather than renamed via `.configure()`, so this rule
   targets them directly. `float: left` + `height: 0` is the standard Tiptap placeholder recipe: the
   pseudo-element overlays the empty block without adding to its layout height (an empty node would
   otherwise briefly grow taller than a populated one while the placeholder is showing). */
.editor-body .is-empty::before {
  content: attr(data-placeholder); float: left; height: 0; color: var(--faint); pointer-events: none;
}
/* Focus extension — REMOVED 2026-08-12, same day it was added. It shipped a `.has-focus` left rule
   ("you are here" on the focused block); the owner saw it in the editor and asked what the black
   lines were for, which is the answer to whether a focus affordance was wanted. It was a
   "low-priority free extra" nobody requested, and a caret already marks the focused block.
   Do not reintroduce the rule without also reintroducing a reason for it. The `Focus` registration
   in `use-post-editor.hooks.ts` goes with it — a class toggling in the DOM with no CSS is dead
   weight, exactly the argument that got UniqueID and TableOfContents dropped the same day. */
/* `WidgetAddControl`'s `<span className="widget-add-control">` (its widget-type `<select>` plus
   the "Insert widget"/"+ Add widget" trigger button, `components/WidgetPickerDialog/WidgetPickerDialog.tsx`) had
   never had any CSS anywhere in the app — the two controls sat flush with zero gap between them.
   First fixed scoped (`.editor-toolbar .widget-add-control` in `styles/editor.css`) because that
   pass didn't own this file and hadn't verified this span's other two call sites. Promoted to a
   plain global rule here now that all three have actually been read, not assumed: `PostEditor.tsx`
   and `CollectionEntryEditor.tsx` both render it inside `.editor-toolbar .grp` (identical
   structure), and `WidgetRegionEditor.tsx` renders it bare at the end of `.widget-region-placements`
   (an unstyled block `<div>` — `display: inline-flex` on this span doesn't care what its parent's
   own display mode is). All three want the identical fix because the defect is in the span's own
   two children, not in any one screen's surrounding layout — the opposite situation from
   `.editor-actions` above, where the same class name really was serving unrelated roles. The
   `styles/editor.css` scoped rule is now redundant and should be dropped by whoever owns that
   file. */
.widget-add-control { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
/* User report: "insert widget button should be one line" — `WidgetAddControl`'s trigger button
   (`components/WidgetPickerDialog/WidgetPickerDialog.tsx`) wrapped to two lines ("Insert" / "widget"). NOT the
   `.menu-tree > .btn-secondary` / `.settings-scope-editor .btn-danger` / `.field-attrs-rows >
   .btn-secondary` species (a flex-COLUMN's `align-items: stretch` blowing a button edge-to-edge) —
   measured and ruled out: `.widget-add-control` is `inline-flex` row with `align-items: center`,
   and the wrap reproduces even with the span fully detached from `.grp`/`.editor-toolbar`
   (`position: fixed`, no ancestor flex context at all, still wraps at the same width). The button
   and the type `<select>` beside it are shrinking EACH OTHER inside this span alone — a flex row's
   default automatic minimum size lets a wrapping-eligible text button collapse toward its
   longest-word width instead of guaranteeing its single-line (`white-space: nowrap`) width, with
   nothing here needing the collapse. Verified live: `flex-shrink: 0` alone fixed it, `white-space:
   nowrap` alone fixed it (120px/one line either way, vs 78px/two lines before); using
   `white-space: nowrap` as the primary fix since it directly encodes "this label must not wrap"
   rather than relying on a flex side effect, per the direct-child idiom the three prior instances
   above already use. */
.widget-add-control > button { white-space: nowrap; flex-shrink: 0; }
/* User report (separate from the one above): toolbar overflows past the right edge instead of
   wrapping to a second line — "Insert…" clipped mid-word — at real (not edge-case) window widths,
   e.g. viewport ~1200-1300px where `.editor-toolbar`'s own rendered width lands around 786-986px.
   Measured with a live sweep across 600-1400px in 20px steps (`getComputedStyle`/`scrollWidth` vs
   `clientWidth`, not eyeballed): this band overflows by 13-113px; every other width in the sweep is
   clean. `.editor-toolbar` already has `flex-wrap: wrap` (styles.css above) and reflows correctly at
   every OTHER width, including down to 500px where it wraps to three lines with zero overflow — so
   this isn't a missing-wrap regression from the `> button` fix above (A/B-verified: reverting that
   fix does make the overflow disappear, but only by reintroducing the two-line "Insert widget"
   label it was written to stop, and adding `flex-shrink: 0`/`min-width: 0` to `.grp` or to
   `.widget-add-control` itself does NOT fix the overflow band either — ruled out live).
   Root cause, isolated by bisecting `.widget-add-control`'s two children: `components/Select/Select.tsx`'s
   trigger (`styles/select.css`'s `.select-trigger`) is `width: 100%`, correct for its normal home
   (a form field filling a container with a real defined width) but meaningless here — this span is
   `inline-flex` with no explicit width of its own, so the trigger's 100% has no resolvable basis.
   That circularity feeds an underestimate into the browser's flex line-breaking pre-pass (which
   must guess each item's width before the real layout runs), so `.grp` gets assigned to line 1
   assuming it needs less room than it actually does once real layout resolves the select's width —
   the same line then can't shrink enough to fit (the button's `flex-shrink: 0` above forbids it) and
   overflows instead of having already wrapped. A/B-verified live: this one rule alone eliminates
   the overflow across the full 600-1400px sweep, with either the default "Text" option or the
   widest label ("Recent Entries") selected; scoped to this control only, so every other `<Select>`
   in the app (built to fill its container) keeps `width: 100%`. */
.widget-add-control .select-trigger { width: auto; }
/* `EmbedInsertControl` (`components/EmbedInsertControl/EmbedInsertControl.tsx`, quick-and-dirty pass 2026-08-05) — the
   "Embed" button's inline choice row (Media / Form / Menu / Widget…) and the "Widget…" branch's
   nested `.widget-add-control`, both rendered inline right after the trigger rather than as an
   absolutely-positioned popover, matching this pass's "get it working" scope. Same gap treatment
   as `.widget-add-control` above so it doesn't sit flush against the "Embed" button. */
.embed-insert-control { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }
.embed-insert-menu { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); margin-left: var(--space-2); }
.editor-body { background: var(--surface); padding: 1.5rem 2rem; min-height: 22rem; }
.editor-body .tiptap { outline: none; min-height: 20rem; }
/* Owner-reported bug (2026-08-12): an inserted image rendered at its raw intrinsic size — a
   2000px+ photo blew out the whole editor pane. Confirmed live (headless Chromium against the
   real dev server): `.editor-body .tiptap img` had `max-width: none` / `display: inline` before
   this rule, on BOTH insertion paths this editor supported at the time — the toolbar's since-
   removed "Img by URL" (plain `setImage`; see `PostEditor.tsx`'s own comment on its 2026-08-12
   removal) and drag/paste upload (`MediaImage`'s NodeView, `lib/media-image-extension.tsx`, the
   surviving path). Both rendered a real `<img class="media-image-node__preview">` inside this
   same `.tiptap` container, so one rule here covered both; this was a missing-CSS gap, not a
   node-shape difference between the two paths — still true for whichever paths reach this
   container today. Values mirror the public theme's own
   `.post-detail-body img` (`src/themes/static/basic/css/styles.css`) so the editor previews the
   published post's actual sizing/rounding/spacing instead of a same-but-different in-editor
   look. `height: auto` is required alongside `max-width` — without it, a node carrying an
   explicit `height` attribute would squash instead of scale once width is constrained. */
.editor-body .tiptap img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; border-radius: 10px; margin: 20px 0; }
/* Owner-reported (2026-08-12, same session as the fix immediately above): the media image node
   view's "Replace"/"Remove" buttons (`lib/media-image-extension.tsx`'s `.media-image-node__actions`
   wrapper) sat flush against each other — measured live, a 0px gap between their bounding boxes.
   `gap` on the flex container, not a margin on one button, so this stays correct regardless of
   which button (if either) is hidden/reordered later; `inline-flex` because the actions strip sits
   inline below the image, not stretched full-width. First landed at 3px (the middle of the owner's
   initial "2-3px" ask); he looked at it live and asked to double it, so 6px is the value he actually
   signed off on — do not "restore" it to the originally-stated range. */
.media-image-node__actions { display: inline-flex; gap: 6px; }
/* Owner-reported (2026-09-11): the generic `media` node's own "Replace"/"Remove" actions
   (`lib/media-embed-extension.tsx`'s `.media-embed-node__actions` wrapper) never got the fix
   immediately above when `media` was added — same 0px-gap bug, new node type. Mirrors that rule's
   `inline-flex`-with-`gap` approach; owner asked for 5px first, then 10px after seeing it live —
   10px is the value he actually signed off on, not the 6px `image` settled on, so don't unify the
   two values without asking again. */
/* Owner-reported (2026-09-22): a `media` block holding a video rendered at native size, overflowing
   the editor column (cut off on the right, taller than the screen); `img` previews were unaffected
   since `.editor-body .tiptap img` above already constrains them. Same `max-width`/`height: auto`
   approach extended to `.media-embed-node__preview` (`lib/media-embed-extension.tsx`, covers both the
   `<video>` and `<img>` preview elements), plus a `max-height` so a tall/portrait video can't fill the
   viewport, and `margin-bottom` so the actions row below sits off the preview instead of touching it. */
.media-embed-node__preview { display: block; max-width: 100%; max-height: 60vh; width: auto; height: auto; margin-bottom: 10px; }
.media-embed-node__actions { display: inline-flex; gap: 10px; }
/* Owner-reported (2026-09-22): a widget/form embed's "Change"/"Remove" buttons
   (`lib/widget-embed-extension.tsx`'s `.widget-embed-node__actions`) touched each other and the
   widget label. Same `inline-flex` + 10px `gap` as the media node's actions above, plus a left
   margin so the label and the buttons don't run together. */
.widget-embed-node__actions { display: inline-flex; gap: 10px; margin-left: 12px; vertical-align: middle; }
/* `font-size`/`color` made explicit here (found while measuring the real default for the toolbar's
   font-size select, 2026-08-11) — without them, the FIRST paragraph of every post's body collided
   with the legacy `.admin-content h1 + p` rule (this file, "Page headings + intro copy"): the
   post-title-in-document feature's `<h1 data-post-title>` sits inside `.admin-content` same as any
   dashboard page's own `<h1>`, so its immediate sibling `<p>` was unintentionally catching that
   rule's `font-size: 0.95rem`/`color: var(--muted)`/`margin: 0 0 1.6rem` meant for a page's intro
   copy, not post body text — verified live (`getComputedStyle`): the first paragraph rendered at
   15.2px muted gray with no top margin while every OTHER paragraph in the same doc rendered at the
   real 16px/`--fg`/1em-both-sides default. Not a fix to the legacy rule itself (still live and
   correct for the dashboard sections that have not migrated to `.page-header` yet, per that rule's
   own comment) — this instead gives every paragraph in the editor its own explicit values so none of
   them are left exposed to whatever unrelated selector happens to match their DOM position. */
.editor-body .tiptap p { font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; color: inherit; margin: 1em 0; }
.editor-body .tiptap pre { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--fg); font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 1rem; border-radius: var(--r-md); overflow-x: auto; }
/* Code block syntax highlighting (coordinator MSG #1, 2026-08-11) — `lowlight` decorates the
   editor's own DOM with `hljs-*` classes on `<span>`s inside the `<pre><code>` this rule's parent
   already styles; without any color rules for those classes the highlighting exists structurally
   but is invisible (every span inherits the same plain `--fg`). A hand-picked set of `hljs-*` rules
   built from this admin's own tokens, not an imported vendor theme (`highlight.js/styles/*.css`):
   every shipped vendor theme hardcodes hex colors for one fixed background, which would fight this
   app's own light/dark skin system (`data-theme`) rather than adapt to it the way every other color
   in this file already does. Two literal hex values (string/number) fill the two hues this token set
   has no existing named color for — every other role reuses an existing token. */
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-comment, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-quote { color: var(--muted); font-style: italic; }
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-keyword, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-selector-tag, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-literal, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-type { color: var(--accent-text); }
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-string, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-attr, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-template-tag { color: var(--jini-code-string); }
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-number, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-symbol, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-bullet { color: var(--jini-code-number); }
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-title, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-section, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-name { color: var(--fg-2); font-weight: 600; }
.editor-body .tiptap .hljs-variable, .editor-body .tiptap .hljs-attribute { color: var(--fg-2); }
.editor-body .tiptap blockquote { border-left: 3px solid var(--border-strong); margin: 1rem 0; padding-left: 1rem; color: var(--muted); }
/* Post-title-in-document feature (2026-08-11) — the doc's own first node
   (`lib/post-title-extension.ts`), rendered as a real `<h1 data-post-title>` so an author can click
   directly into it and use the toolbar's TextAlign buttons on it, same as any other block. Deliberately
   NOT styled as large/bold as `.editor-title` above (the standalone title input the owner asked to
   keep right next to the slug, same day) — both surfaces show the same text, kept in sync
   (`use-post-editor.hooks.ts`), and doubling that input's giant-bold treatment here would read as the
   title appearing twice rather than once in two editable places. Sized just enough above body
   paragraphs to read as a heading. */
.editor-body .tiptap [data-post-title] { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 700; margin: 0 0 0.75rem; }
.editor-body .tiptap [data-post-title]:empty::before { content: "Untitled"; color: var(--faint); font-weight: 500; }
 
/* Appearance — the card backgrounds are intentional theme swatches (a preview of
   each theme's palette); tokens drive the frame, active state, and tag only.
   `auto-fill`, not `auto-fit`: a tab with only one theme (e.g. the `declarative` tier
   today) must not let that lone card's track absorb every other unused column's
   width — `auto-fit` collapses empty tracks and hands their space to the occupied
   ones, ballooning a single card (and its 16:10 preview) to the full grid width.
   `auto-fill` keeps the phantom tracks reserved, so a lone card sizes the same as
   it would in a fully populated row. */
.theme-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15rem, 1fr)); gap: 1.2rem; }
.theme-card { position: relative; border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: 1.4rem; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow); background: var(--jini-panel-bg); border: 1.5px solid var(--jini-panel-border); transition: transform 0.14s, box-shadow 0.14s;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.theme-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); }
/* Active theme card "border beam" (2026-08-09) — replaces the old plain 1px accent outline+ring
   with a broader, animated, multicolored arc that continuously travels around the card edge,
   trailing off into transparency on both ends (owner's own description: "multicolored beam that
   trails the edges"). Pure CSS, no JS: a `conic-gradient` on a `::before` pseudo-element, rotated by
   animating a registered `<angle>` custom property (`@property` — required for the browser to
   interpolate the angle smoothly frame-to-frame rather than jump-cutting), then masked down from a
   filled square to a ring using the standard two-layer `mask-composite: exclude` trick (an opaque
   `content-box` layer subtracted from an opaque `padding-box` layer leaves only the padding-box's
   border-width perimeter visible — `padding: 3px` below IS the beam's thickness, not decorative
   spacing). `.theme-card`'s own base rule already has `position: relative`, which this depends on
   for the pseudo-element's `position: absolute; inset: 0` to anchor correctly. */
@property --border-beam-angle {
  syntax: "<angle>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0deg;
}
.theme-card.active { border-color: transparent; box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); }
.theme-card.active::before {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: inherit; padding: 3px;
  /* Lighter (owner feedback, 2026-08-09): opacity on the whole layer rather than paler individual
     stops — keeps the same hues/contrast between colors, just softer against the card overall. */
  opacity: 0.6;
  /* Gold beam (item 5, 2026-08-31): was a pink/purple/blue/cyan rainbow sweep, same 4-stop
     arc/angles — only the colors changed, reusing `--border-beam-gold-1` as both the first and
     last stop so the sweep tapers pale -> deep -> amber -> pale into the transparent trail rather
     than cutting from amber straight to nothing. */
  background: conic-gradient(from var(--border-beam-angle),
    transparent 0deg, transparent 260deg,
    var(--border-beam-gold-1) 282deg, var(--border-beam-gold-2) 306deg, var(--border-beam-gold-3) 330deg, var(--border-beam-gold-1) 354deg,
    transparent 360deg);
  -webkit-mask: linear-gradient(#fff 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#fff 0 0);
  -webkit-mask-composite: xor; mask-composite: exclude;
  /* 3.2s -> 4.26s: ~33% slower, owner feedback same pass. */
  /* Three sweeps, then still (idle-CPU audit, 2026-09-29): animating a registered custom property in
     a conic gradient repaints the card on the main thread every frame, so an infinite beam kept the
     renderer and GPU busy for as long as the Themes screen stayed open. Hover resumes it. */
  animation: theme-card-border-beam 4.26s linear 3;
  pointer-events: none;
}
.theme-card.active:hover::before { animation-iteration-count: infinite; }
@keyframes theme-card-border-beam { to { --border-beam-angle: 360deg; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .theme-card.active::before { animation: none; --border-beam-angle: 45deg; }
}
.theme-card h3 { margin-top: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.15rem; }
.theme-card p { font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.45; opacity: 0.85; }
/* Dark cards sit on a --surface fill, but inherit the shell's light-theme Jini text colour. */
:root[data-theme="dark"] .theme-card { color: var(--fg); }
:root[data-theme="dark"] .theme-card p { color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1; }
.theme-card button { background: color-mix(in oklch, currentColor 16%, transparent); color: currentColor; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, currentColor 30%, transparent); }
.theme-card button:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, currentColor 26%, transparent); opacity: 1; }
/* Activate (2026-08-10 owner feedback) — the `currentColor`-tinted rule just above exists for the
   three legacy swatch-background cards (`.theme-paper`/`.theme-atlas`/`.theme-glassmorphic`, right
   below) so a button stays legible against an arbitrary swatch hue. It also caught every OTHER
   card's Activate button, though, muting it to a washed-out secondary look instead of this admin's
   actual primary-action color (`--primary`, the same token `PostEditor.tsx`'s bare/default Save
   button gets). `.btn-primary` alone loses that fight — `.theme-card button` outranks a bare
   `.btn-primary` on selector specificity — so this re-asserts it at one class higher than the rule
   it's overriding, same "outrank than replace" approach `.list-table td button:not(...)` documents
   above for the identical bare-`button` shape problem. */
/* 2026-08-11: burnt orange dropped from this button on owner instruction ("change the Activate
   button ... instead of the orange it is now"), continuing the same de-saturation that took Explore
   from blue to a neutral black fill — the stated goal is fewer hues overall, not a different hue.
 
   Activate takes the INVERSE of Explore's pairing rather than the same one. Both buttons sit side by
   side on every non-active card, so giving them identical black fills would make the primary and
   secondary actions visually indistinguishable — the exact problem the blue-vs-orange pairing was
   changed to solve, just re-created in monochrome. Outline for Activate, solid for Explore, keeps
   one of them obviously dominant with no color doing the work.
 
   Scoped to `.theme-card` only. The app-wide `.btn-primary` (~line 729) still owns `--primary` and is
   deliberately untouched: every primary action in the admin uses it, and this instruction was about
   one button on one screen.
 
   Still re-asserted at one class higher for the specificity reason the original comment below
   records — `.theme-card button` (0,1,1) outranks a bare `.btn-primary` (0,1,0), so the card's
   `currentColor` tint wins otherwise. That trap has now been hit three times on this card. */
.theme-card button.btn-primary { background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg); border: 1px solid var(--fg); }
.theme-card button.btn-primary:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
/* Explore loses the same specificity fight `.btn-primary` above documents, and for the same reason:
   `.theme-card button` (0,1,1) outranks a bare `.btn-explore` (0,1,0), so the card's currentColor
   tint won underneath whatever `.btn-explore` said. Re-asserted here at one class higher, exactly as
   Activate is. White surface / near-black text now (reversed from the solid-blue fill commit
   8a7169b shipped the same day — see `.btn-explore`'s own comment above for why and for the
   chroma-0/`color-mix` trap this rule must keep avoiding, since a fix here can't rely on that
   comment alone catching a future edit). */
.theme-card button.btn-explore { background: var(--fg); color: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--fg); }
.theme-card button.btn-explore:hover { background: var(--fg-2); border-color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1; }
.theme-paper { background: var(--tovu-theme-preview-paper-bg); color: var(--tovu-theme-preview-paper-text); }
.theme-atlas { background: var(--tovu-theme-preview-atlas-bg); color: var(--tovu-theme-preview-atlas-text); }
.theme-glassmorphic { background: var(--tovu-theme-preview-glass-bg); color: var(--tovu-theme-preview-glass-text); }
/* Card actions as icons (owner 2026-10-08): the Activate button and the green Active pill became one
   switch — the same `.agent-plugin-switch` the plugin and settings rows use, burnt orange when ON —
   and Explore/Duplicate became compass/copy icon buttons grouped on the right. Every rule here is
   written as `.theme-card button.<class>` for the specificity trap the `.btn-primary`/`.btn-explore`
   overrides above record: `.theme-card button` (0,1,1) would otherwise tint these with
   `currentColor` too. Placed after `.theme-card button:hover` so equal-specificity ties resolve here. */
.theme-card-icon-actions { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-1); margin-left: auto; }
.theme-card button.agent-plugin-switch { background: var(--border-strong); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); padding: 0; border-radius: var(--r-pill); }
.theme-card button.agent-plugin-switch[aria-checked="true"] { background: var(--primary); border-color: var(--primary); }
.theme-card button.agent-plugin-switch:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--primary); opacity: 1; }
.theme-card button.theme-card-icon-btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 36px; height: 36px; padding: 0;
  color: var(--fg); background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.theme-card button.theme-card-icon-btn:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--surface-2); border-color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1; }
/* In flight (a duplicate running): dimmed and waiting, not the "no" cursor — the click is not refused,
   it is queued behind the copy already running. */
.theme-card button.theme-card-icon-btn:disabled { color: var(--muted); background: transparent; cursor: progress; }
/* The card's ⋮ (`RowMenu`'s trigger, owner 2026-10-10) dressed as the compass button beside it —
   same 36px square outline — instead of the round, borderless table-row trigger. Same
   `.theme-card button.<class>` specificity reason as above. */
.theme-card button.row-menu-trigger {
  width: 36px; height: 36px;
  color: var(--fg); background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.theme-card button.row-menu-trigger svg { width: 18px; height: 18px; }
.theme-card button.row-menu-trigger:hover,
.theme-card button.row-menu-trigger[aria-expanded="true"] { background: var(--surface-2); border-color: var(--fg-2); color: var(--fg); opacity: 1; }
 
/* Theme card preview thumbnail (Themes screen, 2026-08-10) — a `static`-tier theme's own
   `screenshots/index.png` (served straight off disk by `theme-static-assets.ts`'s
   `/theme-assets/{id}/...` mount, no new backend work) shown above the card's existing text.
   A theme with no screenshot at that path 404s the `<img>` — `onError` below swaps it for this
   placeholder rather than leaving a broken-image icon. `aspect-ratio` (not a fixed height) keeps
   every card's thumbnail the same shape before either the real image or the placeholder has
   painted, so the grid doesn't reflow when screenshots load in. */
.theme-card-preview { aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; border-radius: var(--r-md); overflow: hidden; margin-bottom: 0.9rem; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); }
.theme-card-preview img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; display: block; }
.theme-card-preview-placeholder { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: var(--faint); }
.theme-card-preview-placeholder svg { width: 2rem; height: 2rem; }
 
/* Generic horizontal tab row (`components/TabBar.tsx`) — shared by the Themes screen (tier tabs)
   and the Pages screen (My Pages / Theme Pages), so both list screens carry one visual language
   for "here are several groupings of the same kind of thing" instead of two. Overrides the global
   `button` rule's filled-primary look entirely (background/border/radius/color), same reasoning
   `.list-table td button:not([class*="btn-"])` documents further up this file for why a bare
   `button` selector needs an explicit opt-out rather than relying on specificity alone. */
/* `flex-wrap: wrap` (2026-08-16, superseding the `overflow-x: auto` approach below) — `display:
   flex` with no wrap means a row wider than its container either clips (no scroll affordance) or
   scrolls invisibly. Both bit the Deployment panel's own 5 tabs: first "History" clipped off the
   right edge outright at the file's documented 390px canary width (`.table-scroll`'s comment);
   then, with `overflow-x: auto` added to fix that, opening the admin chat pane narrowed the
   content column enough to trigger the same overflow again, but this time it scrolled instead of
   clipped — and macOS's overlay scrollbar is invisible until scrolled, so it still read as broken
   rather than reachable. `flex-wrap: wrap` sidesteps both failure modes by reflowing extra tabs
   onto a second line instead of overflowing horizontally at all, so there is no scrollbar to
   need. Re-verify against the 390px canary and the chat-pane-narrowed case if this rule changes
   again — and re-check `TabBar.tsx`'s other consumers (Themes' tier tabs, Pages' two tabs, Media,
   Source Control), since this class is shared and none of those had enough tabs to hit either
   failure mode before. `flex-shrink: 0` on the items is still required: without it, flex's default
   shrink-to-fit squeezes each tab's padding/text before wrap kicks in. */
.tab-bar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.3rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); margin-bottom: 1.3rem; }
/* The tab row's own `margin-bottom` above (20.8px) stacks with the surrounding `.page`'s flex
   `gap: var(--space-6)` (24px) whenever a tab bar sits directly in a `.page` column — true for
   every full-page consumer of this component (Recovery, Providers, Media, Themes, Pages, Security,
   Roles, Deployment, SEO, Database, Source Control, Sites; see `TabBar.tsx`'s own header for the
   full list). Measured on Recovery's Restore tab before touching anything: 44.8px total from tab
   row to content, nearly double the 24px gap that same page already uses one row up, between its
   header and this tab row — an accidental doubling, not a deliberate rhythm. Owner-reported
   2026-09-10: "there's a general pattern where there's a lot of space under the tab... seems to be
   everywhere." Zeroing it here makes every tab row's own bottom space equal to the page's normal
   24px rhythm instead of 44.8px.
 
   Scoped to the `.page > .tab-bar` child combinator, not the bare rule above, because that rule's
   `margin-bottom` is NOT redundant for every consumer of this shared class — only for one sitting
   directly in a `.page`'s own flex column, the specific doubling this fix targets. `.tab-bar` is a
   plain reusable class, not a component with a fixed DOM position, so nothing stops a future
   consumer from nesting it several levels below a `.page` instead (inside some other panel's own
   markup, itself living inside that `.page`) — for a tab row placed like that, this same 20.8px
   margin would be its ONLY source of space before its own content, unrelated to any `.page`'s flex
   gap, and zeroing it there would collapse that gap to nothing for no reason. The child combinator
   is what keeps this rule from reaching a case like that: `.page > .tab-bar` matches only a tab bar
   that is a DIRECT child of `.page`, while a plain `.page .tab-bar` descendant selector would have
   matched the nested case too and broken it.
 
   A consumer nests `.tab-bar` this way TODAY, so this is protecting a live screen rather than a
   hypothetical one: `StaticSiteTab.tsx`'s "Publish target" tab bar renders inside
   `.deployment-card-body`, itself inside Deployment's own tab panel. Do not relax the child
   combinator. A second consumer that used to nest this way,
   `ExternalMcpSettingsPanel.tsx`'s per-row Connection/Tools tab bar (nested inside
   `.external-mcp-source`, itself inside the Providers `.page`), was replaced by a per-server Tools
   button + modal in `14f94e9c` and no longer exists. Kept scoped to the child combinator anyway,
   not loosened to the bare rule above: the reasoning above is about the shape of `.tab-bar` as a
   reusable class, not about that one now-gone consumer, and the next nested tab bar — whenever one
   is added — would hit the identical doubling problem in reverse the moment it exists. */
.page > .tab-bar { margin-bottom: 0; }
.tab-bar-item {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center;
  background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 0;
  padding: 0.65rem 0.9rem; font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--muted); cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.14s, border-color 0.14s; flex-shrink: 0;
}
.tab-bar-item:hover { background: none; color: var(--fg); opacity: 1; }
.tab-bar-item[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--selected-text); border-bottom-color: var(--selected-ring); }
.tab-bar-count { margin-left: 0.4rem; font-size: var(--text-2xs); color: var(--faint); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.tab-bar-item[aria-selected="true"] .tab-bar-count { color: var(--accent-text); opacity: 0.75; }
/* `TabBarTab.tag`'s pill — same shape as the admin sidebar's own `.cms-item .soon` badge (uppercase,
   bordered, muted), just scoped to a tab-bar button instead of a nav row so the app has one "Soon"
   look rather than two. */
.tab-bar-tag {
  margin-left: 0.4rem; font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint); border: 1px solid var(--border); padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 5px;
}
.tab-bar-item[aria-selected="true"] .tab-bar-tag { color: var(--accent-text); opacity: 0.75; }
/* Themes' "Soon" tabs (Declarative/Templated/Code, owner 2026-10-11) and Import & Export's Export /
   Import (owner 2026-10-18 on Sites; moved 2026-10-25): label greyed like the sidebar's
   `.cms-item.is-soon`, but still a live tab (no `disabled`), so hover and the selected state keep
   their normal colours. Scoped to these pages: other screens' tagged tabs are unchanged. */
:is(.themes-page, .import-export-page) .tab-bar-item:has(.tab-bar-tag):not([aria-selected="true"]) { color: var(--faint); }
:is(.themes-page, .import-export-page) .tab-bar-item:has(.tab-bar-tag):not([aria-selected="true"]):hover { color: var(--muted); }
/* Themes header (owner 2026-10-11): "View site ↗" pinned to the header's top-right corner, the
   Rescan / Turn off / Publish buttons as one row under the description, left edge flush with the
   title. The side block takes the full row so it always wraps below the text; the link is absolute so
   it stays in the corner. Colours come from existing variants (black `.btn-explore`, white
   `.btn-secondary`, orange `.btn-primary`); the white one's label goes from `--fg-2` to `--fg` so it
   reads black like its siblings' fills. */
.themes-page > .page-header { position: relative; }
.themes-header-side { flex-basis: 100%; min-width: 0; }
.themes-header-side > a { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; }
.themes-header-side > .page-actions { justify-content: flex-start; }
.themes-header-side .btn-secondary:not(:disabled) { color: var(--fg); }
/* The "this one has something configured" signifier (`TabBarTab.dot`'s own doc) — a small filled
   circle, not a colored ring or outline, so it reads clearly at 6px. `--ok` (the same green
   `.status-ok` uses) rather than `--primary`: this is a fact about STATE ("connected"), not a
   recommendation or a call to action, and reusing the connected/success tone from everywhere else
   on this tab (`.status-ok`, the credential row's own "Connected" pill) is what lets a reader learn
   the color once and reuse it, rather than this tab inventing a second meaning for a color already
   spoken for. `flex-shrink: 0` keeps it a circle even inside a tab whose label wraps the row tight. */
.tab-bar-dot { width: 0.4rem; height: 0.4rem; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ok); margin-right: 0.4rem; flex-shrink: 0; }
/* `TabBarTab.icon`'s own frame — `1em`-relative so it tracks this tab row's own type scale rather
   than a pinned px size (`deployment-visuals.tsx`'s own icon sizing note gives the identical
   reasoning), and `currentColor` inherits `.tab-bar-item`'s own text color so the icon dims/accents
   exactly in step with the label beside it (muted at rest, `--accent-text` once selected) with no
   separate color rule of its own to keep in sync. */
.tab-bar-icon { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; margin-right: 0.4rem; flex-shrink: 0; width: 1em; height: 1em; color: currentColor; }
/* Marketplace (soon) placeholder tab (2026-08-10 owner feedback) — greyed out and inert, not a
   clickable empty state: `disabled` already stops the click and pulls it out of the tab order,
   this just makes that visible instead of leaving it looking like every other tab. `background:
   none` is required here, not cosmetic — the global `button:disabled` rule (styles.css ~L218)
   paints a `color-mix` tint of `--primary` (a burnt-orange hue) behind every disabled `<button>`,
   and beats this rule's own un-suffixed `.tab-bar-item { background: none }` on specificity
   (type selector `button:disabled` outranks the class-only base rule for that property), which
   is what actually produced the reddish/pink overlay the grey text color alone couldn't fix. */
.tab-bar-item:disabled { color: var(--faint); background: none; cursor: not-allowed; }
.tab-bar-item:disabled:hover { color: var(--faint); background: none; }
.tab-bar-item:disabled .tab-bar-count { color: var(--faint); }
 
/* Pages screen's "Theme Pages" tab (2026-08-10) — the active theme's own bundled `pages/*.html`,
   listed read-only (no `PostRecord` backs them, so there is no editor to link into). Reuses
   `.list-table`/`.card`/`.empty-state` rather than new table CSS; `.badge-readonly` is the one new
   class, styled like `.status-draft` (muted, not a tone that implies success/danger) since
   "read-only" isn't a warning, just a fact about where this row's content lives. */
.badge-readonly { display: inline-block; background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); padding: 0.15rem 0.55rem; border-radius: var(--r-pill); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
 
/* Screen-reader-only live region (SPEC-007 ui.spec.md §5 "Status updates")
   `top: 0; left: 0` is a BUG FIX, not cosmetic — do not drop it (2026-08-15, owner-reported as
   "a bunch of white space" below the Deployment page).
 
   Without an explicit offset, `position: absolute` resolves against this element's STATIC position,
   and the offset is measured in the containing block — which is the initial containing block (the
   document) whenever every ancestor is `position: static`. `.tab-bar-item` is exactly that case, so
   the Static Site tab's ", Connected" suffix computed `top: 1049.67px` and stretched the DOCUMENT to
   1050px tall inside a `height: 100vh` shell. The result was 341px of dead white space under a
   layout that is supposed to be unscrollable, and `.admin-content`'s own `overflow-y: auto` could
   not clip it — a static ancestor is not a containing block, so the span was never inside that
   scroll box to begin with. Measured: document scrollHeight 1061 → 720, max document scroll 341px →
   0, with `.cms-nav` and `.admin-content` still scrolling internally exactly as before.
 
   Pinning to the containing block's origin instead of the static position makes that impossible for
   EVERY use of this class (22 across 8 components), rather than fixing one call site by adding
   `position: relative` to its parent and waiting for the next one. Position is irrelevant to what
   this class is for: the box stays 1px and `clip`ped, so it is still rendered, still in the
   accessibility tree, and still announced — verified `display: block`, `visibility: visible` after
   the change. There is no `:focus` variant of this class anywhere in the app, so nothing here is
   ever meant to become visible in place. */
.visually-hidden { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; }
 
/* Forms list "Created / Updated" cell (owner 2026-10-05): created on line 1, updated on line 2.
   Each line is one short date + time that must never break mid-date. */
.forms-dates-line { display: block; white-space: nowrap; }
 
/* Settings (SPEC-007 core-only layered ledger, Phase 6) */
.settings-screen { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; }
.settings-namespace-loader, .settings-principal-selector { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: flex-start; }
.settings-namespace-loader label, .settings-principal-selector label { font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg-2); }
.settings-error-banner { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; }
.settings-body { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(16rem, 1.1fr) minmax(20rem, 1.4fr); gap: 1.2rem; align-items: start; }
.settings-namespace-list { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.2rem; }
.settings-namespace-group { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: 1rem 1.1rem; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); }
/* Same 14px/600 as `.card-title`: Categories & Tags' group titles are card titles by another name. */
.settings-namespace-group h2 { margin: 0 0 0.6rem; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; }
.settings-row-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.settings-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.7rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.4rem; border-radius: var(--r-sm); cursor: pointer; }
.settings-row:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
.settings-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-text); outline-offset: 1px; }
.settings-row.is-selected { background: var(--accent-dim); }
.settings-row-key { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--fg); flex: 1; }
.settings-row-value { font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--muted); max-width: 10rem; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.status-layer-user { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--accent-text); }
.status-layer-workspace { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-layer-global { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--fg-2); }
.status-layer-default { background: transparent; color: var(--faint); border: 1px solid var(--border); }
.settings-detail-panel { background: var(--jini-panel-bg); border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--jini-panel-border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: 1.2rem 1.3rem; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.settings-detail-panel h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 1rem; }
.settings-layer-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(8rem, 1fr)); gap: 0.7rem; }
.settings-layer-cell { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.2rem; background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: var(--r-md); padding: 0.5rem 0.6rem; font-size: 0.85rem; }
.taxonomy-term-detail .settings-layer-cell > .status { align-self: flex-start; }
.settings-layer-effective { border: 1.5px solid var(--accent-text); }
.settings-layer-label { font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--faint); }
/* Groups Workspace's read-only ID/Created facts with the rename form above them (nested inside the
   same `<form>`, after the Save button) instead of floating as a disconnected pair of grey slabs
   below it. Same `border-top` + `padding-top` sub-section idiom `.settings-scope-editor` (below)
   and `.deployment-route-note` already use inside one container. */
.workspace-identity-grid { margin-top: var(--space-4); padding-top: var(--space-4); border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.settings-scope-editor { border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: 0.8rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; }
.settings-scope-editor h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 0.78rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted); }
.settings-value-editor { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.4rem; }
/* Same consolidation as `.login-card label` above. */
.settings-value-editor label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
/* Only the monospace override is this rule's own — padding/border/radius/background/color/resize
   now come from the shared `textarea` rule above; this holds a raw JSON value, hence monospace. */
.settings-value-editor textarea { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.85rem; }
/* The reset-to-defaults trigger uses the shared `.btn-danger` now (was a bespoke
   `.settings-reset-trigger` with the same colors) — matches `PostEditor.tsx`'s own precedent of
   styling a destructive confirm-dialog TRIGGER `.btn-danger` directly, not just the dialog's own
   confirm button. `.settings-scope-editor` is a flex column with default `align-items: stretch`,
   so without this the button would stretch to the container's full width; `.btn-danger` itself
   stays unscoped/full-width-agnostic for its other callers, so the `align-self` fix lives here. */
.settings-scope-editor .btn-danger { align-self: flex-start; }
/* 80, not 40: this is the shared blocking-modal backdrop (confirm dialogs, media/widget pickers),
   so it must sit above `.chat-fab` (75, `styles/assistant.css`). At 40 the raised FAB would float
   over every confirm dialog and let a click open the chat behind the backdrop. */
.settings-dialog-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: var(--jini-overlay-bg); display: grid; place-items: center; z-index: 80;
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.settings-dialog { background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: 1.5rem 1.6rem; max-width: 26rem; box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.9rem;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none);
}
.settings-dialog h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.15rem; }
.settings-dialog p { margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.5; }
 
/* `WidgetPickerDialog.tsx`'s "Place a {type} widget" modal — `.widget-picker-dialog`/`-body`/
   `-section`/`-footer` below all first-appear here; this modal had ZERO CSS anywhere for its own
   structure before this pass (`.widget-picker-section` specifically confirmed empty by
   `styles/forms.css`'s own comment on the neighboring `.widget-config-fields`), so it fell all the
   way back to plain UA defaults — an inline label+select run (a bare `<label>` is inline, a bare
   `<select>` is inline-block, and nothing here set `display` on their shared parent), no seam
   between "Use existing"/"Create new", unstyled bold-serif `<h3>`s, and Cancel stranded in a bare
   `.editor-actions` span with no footer of its own.
 
   `.widget-picker-dialog` widens the shared `.settings-dialog` for this one caller only — 26rem
   read cramped once a real widget type (Social Links, up to 20 rows) is the thing filling the
   "Create new" section below. `max-height` + the scrolling body below is what actually stops that
   content from pushing the dialog past the viewport; the width change alone would not.
 
   `width`, not just `max-width` — found live, not assumed: `.settings-dialog-backdrop` is
   `display: grid; place-items: center`, and `place-items` sets `justify-items: center`, which
   makes every grid item it centers (this dialog included) size by shrink-to-fit (its own
   max-content), not stretch-to-track. A `max-width` on a shrink-to-fit box is only a CAP that
   binds when content is already wider than it — it does not, by itself, make the box that wide.
   A `max-width`-only version of this rule measured as literally inert in the real browser: the
   dialog's used width came entirely from its content's own max-content size regardless of the
   max-width value. `max-width: calc(100vw - 2rem)` alongside the explicit width is what keeps a
   narrow viewport safe, since the explicit width alone would otherwise overflow a phone-width
   screen. */
.widget-picker-dialog { width: 32rem; max-width: calc(100vw - 2rem); max-height: 85vh; }
/* The one flexible, scrolling child between the fixed `<h2>` header above and the fixed Cancel
   footer below. `flex: 1 1 auto` + `min-height: 0` are both required: a flex child's default
   `min-height: auto` refuses to shrink below its own content's height, so without `min-height: 0`
   this would just keep growing past `max-height` above instead of ever engaging its own
   `overflow-y: auto` (the identical gotcha `styles/forms.css`'s `.field-row` comment measured for
   an unrelated property, same underlying mechanism). */
.widget-picker-body {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-5);
  flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto;
}
/* Each "Use existing"/"Create new" `<form>`. `flex column` is what actually fixes the inline
   label+select run described above (stacks the `.field` div's label above its own control instead
   of letting both flow as running text); `gap` matches `.field-group`'s own label-group rhythm
   rather than inventing a new spacing value. */
.widget-picker-section {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3);
}
/* Section-to-section divider — an adjacent-sibling selector, so it only paints between the two
   sections when BOTH render. `hasExisting` conditionally omits the first `<form>` entirely for a
   freshly-registered widget type with zero existing instances; this rule is simply inert then,
   nothing on the TSX side needs to know about it. */
.widget-picker-section + .widget-picker-section {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: var(--space-4);
}
/* Section heading. NOT the `.settings-scope-editor h3` uppercase/small/muted idiom this rule used
   originally — that idiom is character-for-character `.field-label`'s own styling, and unlike
   `.settings-scope-editor h3` (which never sits directly above a `.field-label`), this heading
   does: "Use existing" (the section) sits right above "Existing Text widgets" (a `.field-label`
   inside it). Styled identically, the two were indistinguishable — a flat run of same-weight grey
   shouty labels with no signal that one contains the other. This is deliberately the opposite
   shape: sentence case (not uppercase), full-strength `--fg` (not `--muted`), and a full size step
   up (`--text-base` vs. `.field-label`'s `--text-2xs`) so a section heading reads as visibly ABOVE
   the fields it contains, not another field of the same kind. Do not fix this by restyling
   `.field-label` instead — that class is shared across the whole admin. */
.widget-picker-section h3 {
  margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg);
}
/* Each section's own submit ("Use this widget" / "Create and place") is the one direct-child
   `<button>` of a flex column that now defaults to `align-items: stretch` (the rule above) — left
   unfixed it would stretch edge-to-edge, the same stretch-by-default-flex-column bug
   `styles/forms.css`'s `.widget-config-fields > button` and `.menu-tree > .btn-secondary` below
   already fix elsewhere for the identical shape. Both submits stay the primary fill — each really
   is the one clearly primary action for its own section — only sizing/alignment changes here, not
   color. */
.widget-picker-section > button {
  align-self: flex-start;
}
/* A real footer, separated from the scrolling body above by its own border, instead of Cancel
   being left stranded in a bare `.editor-actions` span with no visual seam of its own.
   `Collections.tsx`'s dialogs (`NewContentTypeDialog`/`EditFieldsDialog`) already wrap their own
   submit+Cancel pair in exactly this `.editor-actions` span — reused here unchanged (Cancel is the
   only dialog-level action; the submits above belong to their own sections) rather than inventing
   a second button-row idiom just for this file. */
.widget-picker-footer {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: var(--space-4);
}
 
/* `MediaPickerDialog.tsx`'s "Choose an image" modal — reuses `.widget-picker-footer` above for its
   own Cancel row (see that component's own header comment on why), but `.media-picker-grid`/
   `.media-picker-item` had ZERO CSS anywhere before this pass (confirmed via grep across
   `apps/admin/src`), so each thumbnail `<img>` rendered at its raw native pixel size with nothing
   constraining it, and the unbounded grid just pushed this dialog's own Cancel footer arbitrarily
   far down the page — live-measured off-screen at y=3254 against a 1400px viewport. Escape still
   closed the dialog, but the visible Cancel control was unreachable, which is the real defect.
