   `width` + `max-height` here follow `.widget-picker-dialog` directly above, not `.field-attrs-
   dialog` (`styles/form-field-attrs.css`)'s two-class version: that file needed the extra
   specificity because ITS import order relative to this stylesheet is unreliable (see its own
   comment). A bare single-class selector declared here, AFTER `.settings-dialog`'s own rule, wins
   on same-file source order alone — exactly how `.widget-picker-dialog` already works two rules up,
   re-confirmed live via `getComputedStyle` for this rule too rather than assumed. `width`, not just
   `max-width`: `.settings-dialog-backdrop`'s `place-items: center` sizes every dialog by
   shrink-to-fit, so `max-width` alone only caps a box already wider than it, it does not establish
   width on its own (`.widget-picker-dialog`'s own comment measured this the hard way; not
   re-deriving it here). */
.media-picker-dialog { width: 32rem; max-width: calc(100vw - 2rem); max-height: 85vh; }
/* The one scrolling region between the fixed `<h2>` title above and the fixed `.widget-picker-footer`
   Cancel row below — same `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0` shape `.widget-picker-body` documents
   above applies here too (a flex child's default `min-height: auto` refuses to shrink below its own
   content's height, so without `min-height: 0` this would keep growing past `max-height` instead of
   ever engaging its own `overflow-y: auto`). Cancel stays visible and clickable no matter how many
   media items load — only the thumbnail grid scrolls, matching this component's own footer already
   borrowing the widget-picker idiom rather than inventing a second one. */
.media-picker-body { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; }
.media-picker-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(7rem, 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-3);
}
/* Overrides the global `button` rule's solid `--primary` background/padding (this file's own button
   block, near the top) — a thumbnail tile reads as a card to click, not a call-to-action button. */
.media-picker-item {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem;
  padding: 0.4rem; background: var(--surface-2); color: inherit;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  text-align: left; font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-weight: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.media-picker-item:hover { border-color: var(--accent-text); }
.media-picker-item img {
  width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; object-fit: cover;
  border-radius: var(--r-sm); display: block;
}
.media-picker-item-title {
  font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--fg-2);
  overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap;
}
 
/* `MediaRefField` (SEO OG/Twitter image picker, 2026-09-05) — its input/"Choose image"/Remove row,
   plus a compact thumbnail preview. Same fixed-square-thumbnail idiom as `.media-picker-item img`
   just above, sized down for an inline field rather than a grid card. */
.media-ref-field-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.media-ref-field-row input { flex: 1 1 12rem; }
.media-ref-field-preview {
  width: 4rem; height: 4rem; object-fit: cover;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  margin-top: var(--space-2); display: block;
}
 
/* Collections / Categories & Tags / Storage / Recovery (design-spec.md) — additive status-pill
 * and layout classes following the exact naming/token conventions already established above.
 * Not in this dispatch's literal touch-scope list, but "match the existing design system" is a
 * hard requirement of the same dispatch — see the Programmer handoff for the disclosed rationale. */
.status-deprecated, .status-unpublished, .status-unavailable { background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); }
.status-tombstone { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.status-cheap { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-expensive { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--accent-text); }
.status-success { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-failure, .status-error { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
 
/* Plugins (SPEC-005 ui.spec.md §5) — the discovery-status pill values and the trust-tier badge,
 * reusing the `.status` pill geometry above rather than introducing a new badge token. */
.status-valid { background: var(--ok-bg); color: var(--ok); }
.status-invalid, .status-incompatible { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); }
.tier { padding: 0.15rem 0.55rem; border-radius: var(--r-pill); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 600; background: var(--surface-3); color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
.plugin-errors { margin: 0; padding-left: 1rem; font-size: 0.8rem; }
 
.collections-type-dialog { max-width: 34rem; max-height: 85vh; overflow-y: auto; }
.collections-field-row { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md); padding: 0.7rem 0.8rem; margin: 0 0 0.7rem; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center; }
.collections-field-row legend { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--faint); padding: 0 0.3rem; }
.collections-row-actions { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; }
.collections-dynamic-fields { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); margin-top: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.7rem; } /* `.card`'s padding, so its content edge lines up with the Categories & Tags card below */
.collections-dynamic-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.3rem; }
/* Same consolidation as `.login-card label` above. */
.collections-dynamic-field label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
/* Categories & Tags box (`features/taxonomy/TermPicker.tsx`). The frame, heading and lead are the
   shared `.card`/`.card-title`/`.card-lead`; the term rows reuse `.field-label`, `.field-hint` and
   `.form-checkbox-field`. What is left here is layout only: the gap above the card, and one block
   per taxonomy separated by the card's own hairline. The taxonomy name sits ABOVE its terms (owner,
   2026-10-10: a name column on the left squeezed the terms and pushed the add box past the card). */
.term-picker { margin-top: var(--space-4); }
.term-picker-groups { margin-top: var(--space-4); border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
/* The `<fieldset>` stays for the group's accessible name; its UA border/padding/margin go, and
   `min-width: 0` undoes the fieldset's `min-content` default so long term lists wrap. The legend is
   floated because a non-floated legend is drawn on the fieldset's border and is never a grid item —
   floated, it becomes an ordinary first cell (float itself has no effect inside a grid). */
.term-picker-group {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); align-items: start;
  gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-4);
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-3) 0; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); min-width: 0;
}
.term-picker-group > legend { float: left; padding: 0; }
.term-picker-terms { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-5); }
/* The row's right-hand cell: its ticks, then the add input (or a category box's "+ Add term"). */
.term-picker-body { display: grid; gap: var(--space-2); justify-items: start; min-width: 0; }
.term-picker-add { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); max-width: 100%; }
.term-picker-add .jini-suggest-input { width: 18rem; max-width: 100%; }
.term-picker-add .jini-suggest-input input { width: 100%; }
/* A long row folds behind "See more" (owner, 2026-10-22) — the button is the shared `.link-button`
   (blue `--link` text); past 100 terms a search box sits above the ticks, as wide as the add box. */
.term-picker-search { width: 18rem; max-width: 100%; }
.term-picker-more { font-size: var(--text-sm); }
 
/* Jini `SuggestInput` (`@jini-ai/ui/admin-widgets`, 2026-10-10): a free-text input with our own
   suggestion list, replacing the native `<datalist>` whose dark macOS bubble and ▼ could not be
   styled. Same white panel look as the admin's other dropdowns (`.select-panel`). */
.jini-suggest-input { position: relative; display: inline-block; }
.jini-suggest-input__list {
  position: absolute; z-index: 30; top: calc(100% + 4px); left: 0; right: 0;
  margin: 0; padding: 4px; list-style: none; max-height: 16rem; overflow-y: auto;
  background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-md);
}
.jini-suggest-input__option {
  padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg); cursor: pointer;
}
.jini-suggest-input__option.is-active { background: var(--surface-2); }
/* Jini `Select` (`@jini-ai/ui/admin-widgets`) portals `.select-panel` to `<body>` and paints it,
   and its search box, with `--jini-bg-elevated`. This admin never maps Jini's surface tokens, so
   that resolved to Jini's own grey default (#f5f5f5) under a white page (owner 2026-10-16: "It
   should be white, right?"). Re-pointed here on the panel itself — every admin-widgets `Select`
   shares this class — to the same `--surface`/`--surface-2`/`--fg` the dropdown above uses, so
   light and dark both follow this admin's theme (`--jini-text` too: Jini's own text token stays
   #202020 under this admin's dark root, which would be dark-on-dark once the panel follows it).
   Doubled class: Jini's `[data-color-scheme]` token scope is the same (0,1,0) and `<style>` order
   is not reliable here (see `styles/select.css`). The trigger (`.select-trigger`, e.g. the SEO
   "Choose an entry…" picker) paints with the same token and read faintly grey next to the white
   inputs around it (owner 2026-10-16), so it shares the re-point. */
.select-panel.select-panel,
.select-trigger.select-trigger {
  --jini-bg-elevated: var(--surface);
  --jini-bg-subtle: var(--surface-2);
  --jini-text: var(--fg);
}
/* Same `.editor-actions` flush-spacing fix as `FormEditor.tsx`'s `.form-actions` — see
   `features/taxonomy/TermPicker.tsx` for why this is scoped here rather than added to
   `.editor-actions` itself (that class is shared with ~30 other, structurally different callers
   across the app, most of them small inline row-action groups that must NOT get a top margin). */
.term-picker-actions { margin-top: var(--space-5); }
 
.taxonomy-new-term-form { margin-top: 0.7rem; }
/* Collapsed resting state of the same form (web-design pass, 2026-08-05) — same top margin as the
   form it replaces at rest, so opening/closing it doesn't shift the group card's height budget. */
.taxonomy-add-term-trigger { margin-top: 0.7rem; }
 
/* Web-design pass (2026-08-05), visual-parity fix: Taxonomy.tsx reuses the since-deleted
   `settings-raw/Settings.tsx`'s SPEC-007 raw-ledger classes (`.settings-namespace-group`/
   `.settings-row-key`/`.settings-detail-panel h2`) for what is a content-management screen, not
   that debug tool — see Taxonomy.tsx's own header comment for the full diagnosis. These three
   rules are additive overrides on top of those shared classes (same specificity, later in the
   cascade wins), scoped to taxonomy's own extra classes so the base `.settings-*` rules above keep
   their original padding/monospace exactly as they were built for — that ledger tool's two-pane
   layout and `namespace.key`-style monospace type were correct for what IT showed, just not for
   ordinary term/taxonomy names. Taxonomy.tsx is now the only live consumer of the base rules;
   they're kept as-is rather than folded into the taxonomy-scoped ones, since a future raw-ledger
   screen would want the un-overridden originals back. */
.taxonomy-namespace-group { padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); } /* was 1rem 1.1rem — `.card`'s roomier padding, matching every other content-list wrapper's weight */
.taxonomy-term-list .settings-row-key { font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-sm); } /* was --font-mono, right for a namespace.key string, wrong for a term name */
.taxonomy-term-detail h2 { font-family: var(--font-display); } /* was --font-mono via `.settings-detail-panel h2`; matches every other page's h1/h2 display font */
 
/* Delete UI (web-design pass, 2026-08-05): the group's own `<h2>` now shares its row with a
   `RowMenu` ("Delete taxonomy") — `.settings-namespace-group h2`'s own margin-bottom rule still
   applies (descendant selector, unaffected by this wrapper), so this only adds the row layout. */
.taxonomy-namespace-group-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-3); }
 
/* Redirects — bulk-import affordance (SPEC-037 REQ-04) */
/* 2026-10-16 (owner: "it looks bad"): the `.notice` frame now matches the add-rule `.card` above it,
   and the summary uses the SEO "Customize for X/Twitter" caret idiom (`styles/seo.css`) instead of
   the native ▼ marker. The summary was a full-width block, so its focus outline boxed the whole
   row; content-width, it rings only the label, and only on keyboard focus. */
.redirects-import { margin: 1rem 0; padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-6); border-color: var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); }
.redirects-import > summary {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: calc(var(--space-2) + 0.375rem);
  width: fit-content;
  cursor: pointer;
  list-style: none;
  font-size: var(--text-sm);
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--fg);
}
.redirects-import > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
.redirects-import > summary::before {
  content: "";
  width: 0.45em;
  height: 0.45em;
  border-right: 1.5px solid currentColor;
  border-bottom: 1.5px solid currentColor;
  transform: rotate(-45deg);
  transition: transform 0.15s ease;
}
.redirects-import[open] > summary::before { transform: rotate(45deg); }
.redirects-import > summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .redirects-import > summary::before { transition: none; } }
.redirects-import form { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); margin-top: var(--space-4); }
/* The label is a one-line `.field-hint`; the rule fields sit behind its ⓘ (`importRulesLabel`). */
.redirects-import form > label { font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); }
/* Same fold as `.settings-value-editor textarea` above — only monospace is this rule's own. */
.redirects-import textarea { width: 100%; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.82rem; }
/* Content-width and left-aligned, like the add-rule form's `.form-actions` button above. */
.redirects-import form > button { align-self: flex-start; margin-top: var(--space-1); }
/* Phone: the 44px tap-target rule (`max-width: 640px` below) already pads the summary and the ⓘ,
   so the desktop gap under the summary would double up. */
@media (max-width: 640px) { .redirects-import form { margin-top: 0; gap: var(--space-1); } }
.redirects-import-result ul { margin: 0.4rem 0; padding-left: 1.2rem; font-size: 0.85rem; }
 
.storage-filter-bar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6rem; align-items: center; }
.storage-filter-bar label { font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--fg-2); }
.storage-restore-point-link { background: transparent; border: none; color: var(--accent-text); cursor: pointer; padding: 0; text-decoration: underline; }
 
.recovery-degraded-banner { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0.7rem; justify-content: space-between; }
 
/* ============================================================
   Restore ceremony — "the discard manifest" (web-design pass #2, 2026-09-10)
   ============================================================
   Pass #1 (c2c8b218) kept the screen's structure — heading card, disclosure card, button — and
   only retuned weights inside it, which the owner rejected on sight. The structure WAS the
   problem: three separately-boxed, equally-weighted regions stacked down the page, so the single
   most consequential screen in this admin scanned exactly like Settings.
 
   This pass treats it as ONE object: an operator's docket for a decision they make once, fast,
   probably mid-incident. `.recovery-restore-card` is a single `.card` with zero padding, and each
   region below pads itself, so the loss manifest can run full-bleed edge to edge instead of
   floating as a box inside a box. Reading order is the argument: where you're going (quiet) ->
   what it costs (loud) -> sign here (deliberate) -> proceed.
 
   Boldness is spent in exactly one place — the manifest — and everything around it stays neutral.
   Three real strengths of the danger hue encode severity, so nothing needs an extra border to
   look important: a 5% tint marks the loss region, a solid 3px spine bounds it, and the
   baseline-unavailable alarm is the one fully-saturated fill on the page.
 
   `.settings-layer-grid`/`-cell`/`-label` are no longer used by this screen at all (they stay
   untouched for Workspace/Taxonomy). Dropping them also fixes a real defect visible in the
   before-screenshot: `.settings-layer-cell` is a stretch-aligned flex column, which blew the
   "Fast restore" `.status` pill out into a full-width green BAR. Taxonomy's equivalent status
   pill opts out locally with `.taxonomy-term-detail .settings-layer-cell > .status`, preserving
   the shared layout for Workspace and every other non-pill cell. */
.recovery-restore-docket { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-2); }
/* Pulls the ghost button's own left padding back so its label optically aligns with the card edge
   below it, rather than sitting indented by a padding it doesn't visually own. */
.recovery-back-link { margin-left: -0.95rem; }
.recovery-restore-card { width: 100%; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; }
/* The disclosure/ceremony error + loading states are `.notice` boxes rendered as direct children
   of the card; without this they'd sit flush against its edges. */
.recovery-restore-card > .notice { margin: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); }
 
/* --- Region 1: where you're going. Deliberately the quiet part. --- */
.recovery-ceremony-summary { padding: var(--space-6) var(--space-6) var(--space-5); }
.recovery-restore-title-row { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-3); }
/* 1.75rem against the 26.4px page title and the 14px `.card-title` used elsewhere — a real
   step, not the near-tie `.card-title` produced here. The timestamp IS the fact this screen is
   about, so it gets the display face and the tightest tracking on the page. */
.recovery-restore-title {
  margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.75rem; font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.15; color: var(--fg); text-wrap: balance;
}
/* Trigger/Kind are reference metadata an operator reads only if something looks wrong — they do
   NOT deserve the same treatment as the cost class, which is a reassurance about THIS action and
   now sits inline with the heading as a real pill. One quiet line, no boxes, no uppercase
   eyebrows, and no middle-dot separator: the gap does that job. */
.recovery-restore-meta {
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-1) var(--space-5);
  margin: var(--space-3) 0 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: 1.5;
}
.recovery-restore-meta > span { display: inline-flex; gap: 0.5ch; }
.recovery-meta-key { color: var(--faint); }
.recovery-meta-value { color: var(--fg-2); font-weight: 500; }
 
/* --- Region 2: what it costs. --- */
/* Pass #3 (2026-09-10) — the owner rejected pass #2 on sight for one specific reason, and it is
   the reason this block is mostly rewritten rather than retuned: the two loudest things on the
   screen were the sentences "at least an unknown number of posts/pages writes" and "…of
   plugin-table rows", set at 1.15rem/600. That is heading-weight type spent on a hedge. It
   promises a magnitude in the split second before it is read and then delivers none, which is the
   exact inverse of what this screen must communicate. Pass #2's own comment called this region
   "the one place this screen raises its voice" — the voice was right, the words it was raised on
   were not.
 
   Pass #3's rule: BIG TYPE IS RESERVED FOR REAL NUMBERS. When a count is a figure, that figure is
   the largest thing in the region. When it is "unknown", nothing in the ledger is set large at
   all, and the screen's loudest element becomes the one sentence that actually earns it — the
   full-bleed `.recovery-baseline-alarm` band below, which says the figures are unverified.
   Uncertainty still dominates the composition; it just does so by saying so, rather than by
   shouting a non-number in headline type. */
.recovery-loss-manifest {
  padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6) var(--space-6);
  /* 5% was invisible in dark mode — verified rendered: `--danger` there is oklch(74%…), so a 5%
     mix against an oklch(18.5%) surface moved the ground by almost nothing and the region lost its
     boundary entirely, leaving the spine to do all the work. 9% reads as a distinct ground in
     both themes, and in dark it lands slightly LIGHTER than the card, which is how depth is built
     on a dark surface rather than with a heavier border. */
  background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--danger) 9%, var(--surface));
  border-block: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--danger) 22%, var(--border));
  /* The spine, as an inset shadow rather than a border-left so it doesn't shift the padding box. */
  box-shadow: var(--jini-status-danger-shadow);
}
.recovery-loss-lede { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-md); line-height: 1.5; color: var(--fg-2); }
.recovery-loss-lede strong { color: var(--fg); font-weight: 600; }
/* The full-width hairlines between rows are gone. Two items do not need dividing, and ruled rows
   read as a data table — which set up the expectation of tabular figures that the "unknown" rows
   then fail to deliver. Spacing and a marker group them instead. */
.recovery-loss-list {
  list-style: none; margin: var(--space-4) 0 0; padding: 0;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3);
}
/* The marker replaces the rules as the thing that says "these are discrete losses, count them".
   Square rather than a round bullet so it doesn't read as prose list decoration, and held at 55%
   so a column of them stays quieter than the region's own spine. */
.recovery-loss-list li {
  margin: 0; padding: 0 0 0 var(--space-4); position: relative;
  line-height: 1.4; color: var(--fg);
}
/* Mixed toward `--surface` rather than toward `transparent`: every other mix in this block is
   opaque, and an oklch mix with `transparent` premultiplies against transparent BLACK, which
   drags the hue on a light ground. Opaque keeps the marker the same muted red in both themes. */
/* `in oklab`, not `in oklch` — see `.btn-danger:disabled`'s comment for the full mechanism.
   The claim above that this "keeps the marker the same muted red in both themes" was only true
   in light mode: dark `--surface` is `oklch(18.5% 0.018 255)`, real blue chroma rather than a
   powerless hue, so the oklch mix rotated `--danger` (hue 25) the short way round through
   magenta and landed at `C 0.0961 H 326.5` — a clearly PINK marker, the loudest instance of
   this bug in the file. OKLab has no hue arc to take the wrong way: measured `C 0.0830 H 20.7`
   after, the muted red the rule always intended. Light mode is bit-identical (`L 0.7360
   C 0.1045 H 25` before and after), so the declaration stays single-armed. */
/* `0.72em` rather than a smaller value: the row's tallest element is `.recovery-loss-what`, not
   the muted qualifier that starts the line, so the marker is aligned to the noun's optical centre
   — at 0.55em it sat visibly high against it. */
.recovery-loss-list li::before {
  content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0.72em;
  width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 1px;
  background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--danger) 55%, var(--surface));
}
/* The quantity slot. Two states, deliberately not interchangeable (INV-05: an "unknown" is never
   a verified 0, and the type must not let them be mistaken for each other). */
/* A REAL figure — the characteristic element of the whole screen when it exists. Display face,
   tabular figures so a column of them aligns, and the only thing here allowed to outweigh the
   restore-point heading, because it is the actual size of what is being destroyed. */
.recovery-loss-qty {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: var(--fg); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
/* No figure. Steps all the way down to a muted qualifier — smaller than the noun it qualifies —
   so the row reads "…posts/pages writes", with the hedge audibly parenthetical. Nothing on an
   all-unknown ledger is set at heading size, which is the whole point of the pass. */
.recovery-loss-qty[data-unknown] {
  font-family: inherit; font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 400;
  letter-spacing: normal; color: var(--muted);
}
/* The category noun — what is actually at stake, and the only thing that differs between one row
   and the next. Carries the row when there is no figure to carry it. */
.recovery-loss-what { font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--fg); }
/* Genuinely secondary — it qualifies the ledger's completeness, it is not itself a loss figure.
   Steps all the way down to 12px/muted and takes a reading measure so it reads as a footnote. */
.recovery-loss-caveat {
  margin: var(--space-4) 0 0; max-width: 68ch;
  font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: 1.55; color: var(--muted);
}
/* --- Region 3: the verdict. The single loudest element on the screen. --- */
/* The one sentence that changes what an operator should do: every figure they just read is
   unverified. `.save-error`'s shared rule is 13px `--danger` text on nothing — indistinguishable
   from the paragraph above it — and pass #1's pale `--danger-bg` outline was barely better. This
   is the one solid `--danger` fill in the app, which is exactly what `--danger-ink` was added for
   (see that token). Two classes (0,2,0) beats `.save-error`'s own (0,1,0), so the shared rule
   stays untouched for every other screen that uses it.
 
   Full-bleed as of pass #3 (see the JSX note in `Recovery.tsx` on why it is now a sibling of the
   manifest rather than a child): a rounded red box inset within a tinted box was a box inside a
   box, and it made the alarm look like a footnote attached to the ledger rather than the ruling
   on it. Edge to edge, it is unmistakably the rank-1 band in a stack of bands. */
/* The BAND is full-bleed; its TEXT still takes a reading measure. Verified rendered at a 1512px
   viewport, the sentence ran as one ~130-character line across the whole card — past twice the
   length prose stays readable at, on the one sentence here that most needs to be read rather than
   skimmed. Two lines at a comfortable measure beat one line nobody finishes.
 
   The measure is trailing padding, NOT `max-width`: this `<p>` carries the band's background
   itself, so capping its width would shrink the red band along with the text and undo the
   full-bleed treatment that makes it rank 1. `max()` keeps the ordinary gutter once the card is
   narrower than the measure, where `calc()` would otherwise go negative. */
.recovery-disclosure-panel .recovery-baseline-alarm {
  display: block; margin: 0;
  padding: var(--space-5) max(var(--space-6), calc(100% - 92ch)) var(--space-5) var(--space-6);
  background: var(--danger); color: var(--danger-ink); border-radius: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.5;
  max-width: none;
}
.recovery-ceremony-step .save-error {
  display: block; margin: 0; padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5);
  background: var(--danger); color: var(--danger-ink); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.45;
}
 
/* --- Region 4: the gate. The only thing between "safe" and "issuing a destructive plan". --- */
/* Given a full-bleed band rather than being a sentence with a 16px native box in it.
 
   Pass #3 dropped its `--surface-2` ground. Three alert-looking treatments were stacking with no
   rank — the tinted manifest, the solid red alarm, and this band — and `--surface-2` is the one
   COOL surface in the token set (oklch hue 250) sitting directly under a composition of warm reds,
   so it read as a third alarm borrowed from a different design system. A gate is a control, not an
   alert; unfilled, it is the calm step between the verdict above it and the button below, and the
   `:has(:checked)` tint below is now a real state change rather than one wash replacing another.
 
   2026-09-10 owner feedback: this used to turn `--ok` (green) when checked — reusing the same
   token `.status-ok`/`.tab-bar-dot` use for "connected/active" (see that comment further up this
   file). Checking this box isn't a success state, though — it's the operator acknowledging a loss
   window on a DESTRUCTIVE action, and green's "you're safe now" vocabulary said the opposite of
   what this screen means. Recolored to `--primary`, the same burnt-orange token `.btn-primary`
   (the "Continue to confirm" button directly beneath this gate) already carries as its fill, so
   checking the box visually previews the action it is about to unlock rather than borrowing an
   unrelated "all clear" signal. */
.recovery-ack-gate {
  display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-4);
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6);
  background: var(--surface); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
  font-size: var(--text-md); font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--fg);
  cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.14s ease;
}
/* Deliberately a much weaker tint than `--primary-dim` itself: full-strength it sits directly
   beneath the solid `--danger` alarm and the two saturated bands fight each other. The checkbox's
   own `accent-color` carries the signal; this only needs to confirm the band's state changed. */
/* Both declarations are `in oklab` — see `.btn-danger:disabled`'s comment for the mechanism.
   The background is the familiar dark-mode case: the oklch mix rotated toward purple and came
   out MORE chromatic than the surface it tints (`C 0.0237 H 265.4`); in oklab the 7% of warm
   primary partly cancels the surface's blue instead, `C 0.0113` — less saturated than the plain
   surface, which is the point of a 7% tint. Light mode is bit-identical (`H 43.4`) either way.
   The BORDER was wrong in BOTH themes, for the two different reasons this file has now hit:
   light `--border` is `oklch(91.5% 0.007 255)`, a real blue hue, so the short arc from
   `--primary`'s 44 ran backwards through purple to `H 292.1` — a lavender hairline under a
   warm band; dark `--border` is `oklch(100% 0 0 / 0.11)`, whose hue is a literal `0` and
   therefore NOT powerless (only `none` is — see `--surface`'s token comment), so the same mix
   landed at `H 11`, a red. In oklab both resolve to the intended warm `H 36.8` (light) and
   `H 44` (dark). Found by measuring the whole rule rather than only the one declaration it was
   reported on. */
.recovery-ack-gate:has(input:checked) {
  background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 7%, var(--surface));
  border-bottom-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 25%, var(--border));
}
.recovery-ack-gate input[type="checkbox"] {
  width: 1.35rem; height: 1.35rem; margin: 0.02rem 0 0;
  accent-color: var(--primary); cursor: pointer; flex-shrink: 0;
}
/* This admin gives `button`/`a` an app-wide focus ring but never gave one to inputs. This control
   gates a destructive action, so it does not get to be the keyboard-invisible one. */
.recovery-ack-gate input[type="checkbox"]:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--accent-text); outline-offset: 2px;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .recovery-ack-gate { transition: none; }
}
 
/* --- Region 5: proceed. Inside the same card, directly under the gate it depends on. --- */
/* Pass #1 left this floating below the card as a detached button, so nothing visually connected
   the checkbox to the control it unlocks. */
.recovery-ceremony-step {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4);
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6);
}
.recovery-ceremony-step p { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-md); line-height: 1.5; color: var(--fg-2); }
/* Same flex-column stretch trap `.settings-scope-editor .btn-danger` documents above: without this,
   `align-items: stretch` (the default) blows every ceremony-step button out to the container's full
   width. The `<p>`s inside these steps still want the stretch (so their text wraps at the container
   width, not their own shrink-to-fit width) — only the button opts out. */
.recovery-ceremony-step button { align-self: flex-start; font-size: var(--text-md); padding: 0.62rem 1.2rem; }
/* The global `button:disabled` mix puts a washed peach fill under near-white text — on this screen
   that read as a half-rendered control rather than a locked one. Neutral and legibly OFF instead,
   so "blocked by the gate above" is the message. (0,2,0) beats `button:disabled`'s (0,1,1). */
.recovery-ceremony-step button:disabled {
  background: var(--surface-2); border-color: var(--border-strong); color: var(--faint); cursor: not-allowed;
}
/* `.btn-danger` is an outline everywhere else in this admin, which is correct for a row-level
   Delete sitting among ten other row actions. Here it is the TERMINAL control of a four-step
   ceremony, and as an outline it rendered visibly lighter than the filled `.btn-primary` that
   merely *starts* that ceremony — the one button in the product that actually discards data was
   the weakest-looking thing on its own screen. Filled, the three reachable ceremony buttons now
   escalate monotonically with commitment: primary fill (plan) -> neutral outline (confirm) ->
   solid danger (execute). Scoped to this ceremony (0,2,0), so `.btn-danger`'s shared outline
   treatment is unchanged for every other screen. */
.recovery-ceremony-step .btn-danger {
  background: var(--danger); color: var(--danger-ink); border-color: var(--danger);
}
.recovery-ceremony-step .btn-danger:hover { background: var(--danger); opacity: 0.88; }
 
/* SEO — per-entry overrides + analyze (SPEC-037 REQ-06/07) */
.seo-entry-section { margin-top: 1.6rem; }
.seo-entry-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.7rem; margin-top: 0.8rem; }
.seo-entry-panel label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--fg-2); }
.seo-analyze-panel { margin-top: 0.8rem; }
.seo-analyze-panel ul { list-style: none; margin: 0.5rem 0 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.4rem; }
 
/* `SitemapModal.tsx`'s "View sitemap" modal. `.sitemap-modal` widens the shared `.settings-dialog`
   (`.settings-dialog-backdrop`'s own rule above `place-items: center`s every dialog by
   shrink-to-fit, so an explicit `width` is required, not just `max-width` — `.widget-picker-dialog`
   /`.media-picker-dialog` above already measured this live; not re-deriving it here) to ~900px, a
   wide-but-not-fullscreen cap for a URL table that can run to hundreds of rows. `max-height` +
   `.sitemap-modal-body`'s own scroll below are what actually stop that table from pushing the
   dialog past the viewport. */
.sitemap-modal { width: 56.25rem; max-width: calc(100vw - 2rem); max-height: 85vh; }
.sitemap-modal-header { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-3); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.sitemap-modal-header h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.15rem; }
.sitemap-modal-header-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); }
.sitemap-modal-source-link { font-size: var(--text-sm); white-space: nowrap; }
/* The one scrolling region between the fixed header above and the fixed `.widget-picker-footer`
   Regenerate/Close row below — same `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto` shape
   `.widget-picker-body`/`.media-picker-body` above already establish for the identical "shrink-to-
   fit dialog, growing content" problem. */
.sitemap-modal-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; }
.sitemap-modal-filter { width: 100%; }
/* Phone: the two columns cut "Last modified" off at the dialog's right edge (375px), so each row
   stacks its date under its URL in one column and the header row goes. */
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .sitemap-modal .list-table thead { display: none; }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table tr,
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td { display: block; }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td { border-bottom: none; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td:first-child { padding-bottom: var(--space-1); }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td + td { padding-top: 0; font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table tbody tr + tr { border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
  /* The URL link is text-height; an invisible area over its whole cell (at least 44px, reaching into
     the date line under a one-line URL) makes it a phone-sized target without moving anything. */
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td:first-child a { display: block; position: relative; }
  .sitemap-modal .list-table td:first-child a::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: calc(-1 * var(--space-3));
    left: calc(-1 * var(--space-4));
    right: calc(-1 * var(--space-4));
    height: calc(100% + var(--space-3) + var(--space-1));
    min-height: 44px;
  }
}
.sitemap-modal-raw {
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-3); background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-md); font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: var(--text-xs);
  line-height: 1.5; white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word;
}
 
/* AI Assistant — the public assistant's master switch + the not-yet-built roadmap accordion.
   The accordion reuses the native <details>/<summary> affordance `.redirects-import` above already
   established in this admin, rather than introducing a second, JS-driven disclosure widget. */
/* Capped rather than full-bleed. These are prose-and-a-checkbox blocks, and on a 1440px+ window an
   uncapped one stretches a 90-character sentence edge to edge, which is well past the ~75ch where a
   line stops being comfortably readable. 68ch keeps the measure sane while staying wide enough that
   the label and its two explanatory lines never wrap awkwardly at the narrow end.
   `.assistant-roadmap details` gets the same treatment so the checklist rows below line up with the
   blocks above instead of running out past them. */
.assistant-switch,
.assistant-roadmap details { max-width: 68ch; }
.assistant-switch { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; }
.assistant-switch > label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg); }
.assistant-switch p { margin: 0; }
 
.assistant-roadmap { margin-top: 1.6rem; }
.assistant-roadmap > p { margin: 0.3rem 0 0.8rem; max-width: 62ch; }
.assistant-roadmap details { border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md); background: var(--surface); margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }
.assistant-roadmap summary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.55rem; cursor: pointer; padding: 0.65rem 0.85rem; font-size: 0.88rem; color: var(--fg-2); }
.assistant-roadmap summary input { pointer-events: none; }
.assistant-roadmap summary > span:first-of-type { flex: 1; }
.assistant-roadmap-tag { font-size: 0.72rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--faint); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm); padding: 0.1rem 0.4rem; }
.assistant-roadmap details p { margin: 0; padding: 0 0.85rem 0.75rem 2rem; max-width: 62ch; }
 
/* --- Settings (ported Open Design settings dialog) ------------------------
 * Layout only. The dialog's own look ships as `@jini-ai/ui`'s opt-in
 * `settings-dialog.css`, imported by `features/settings/SettingsUi.tsx`; everything
 * there resolves through `--jini-*` custom properties, so an override belongs
 * in a `:root` block here rather than in an edit to the package's rules.
 *
 * The section deliberately has no heading strip of its own: the shell renders
 * its own kicker/title/subtitle, and stacking a second header above it was
 * what made the first pass look cluttered. The page is admin sidebar →
 * settings sidebar → panel, nothing else. */
.settings-ui-section { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; height: 100%; }
.settings-ui-section > .jini-tabbed-dialog { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; }
.settings-ui-load-error { margin: 0 0 0.75rem; color: var(--danger); font-size: 0.85rem; }
.settings-ui-save { font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--faint); align-self: center; }
.settings-ui-save.is-error { color: var(--danger); }
.settings-ui-save.is-saved { color: var(--ok); }
.settings-ui-dialog-btn {
  font: inherit; font-size: 0.75rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.6rem; cursor: pointer;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill);
}
.settings-ui-dialog-btn:hover { color: var(--jini-text); border-color: var(--jini-border-strong); }
/* Privacy tab: telemetry consent controls with no real collection pipeline
 * behind them yet (see the panel comment in SettingsUi.tsx). `inert` on
 * `.settings-ui-inert-control` already makes it unusable; this is the visual
 * complement so it also *looks* disabled rather than merely being inert to
 * screen readers/keyboard while appearing fully interactive to the eye. */
.settings-ui-inert-note {
  margin: 0 0 12px; padding: 10px 14px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted); background: var(--jini-bg-subtle);
  border: 1px dashed var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
}
.settings-ui-inert-control { opacity: 0.55; }
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Agent Plugins screen (AgentPlugins.tsx) — scoped to `.agent-plugins-section`
   so none of these touch any other `.settings-ui-section`/`.jini-*` consumer.
   All colors use Jini's own `--jini-*` tokens rather than Tovu's `--muted`/
   `--fg`/`--surface`: this screen pins `data-theme="light"` on its own wrapper
   (same pattern as Settings/AI Assistant), and Jini's tokens redefine at both
   `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]` (`tabbed-dialog.css`),
   while Tovu's own tokens only redefine at `:root[data-theme="dark"]` with no
   `[data-theme="light"]` reset — so a Tovu-token color here would leak the
   admin's root-dark value into this light-pinned island (verified live: the
   existing `.btn-secondary` "Inspect package files" button already does this
   pre-existing, unrelated to this pass — flagged in the design report rather
   than fixed here, since correcting it means adding a `[data-theme="light"]`
   reset block to Tovu's own token set, a shared/global change outside two
   screens' scope). ------------------------------------------------------ */
 
/* Measure — this panel has no `--page-flow` variant (`.settings-ui-section--page-flow` above), so
   it had none of that modifier's own `max-width` fix for the identical problem: a card holding a
   couple of sentences and a short list, stretched to the full ~1300px+ admin column.
 
   Widened 46rem -> 58rem with the row redesign (2026-09-09). 46rem was measured for a CARD, whose
   controls sit UNDER its text; a row carries its state word, switch, and two icon buttons to the
   RIGHT of the text, and at 46rem that action cluster squeezed the description into a two-line
   wrap on the very packages whose descriptions are longest. Still capped well short of the full
   column, so the list keeps a readable measure rather than running edge to edge. */
/* D-32: list and header share the same page width; prose keeps its own readable measure below. */
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { max-width: none; }
 
/* Card removed (2026-09-09, owner request). `.jini-tabbed-dialog`'s own base rule
   (`@jini-ai/ui`'s `tabbed-dialog.css`) paints this shell as a MODAL — an elevated
   background, a 1px border, and rounded corners — and the `--inline` presentation
   this screen passes only drops the FLOATING variant's width/height/shadow, not
   that chrome. Inside an admin page that already carries its own background, the
   leftover chrome read as a second white rounded box wrapping the whole screen
   rather than the row list sitting directly on the page.
 
   Same fix, same reasoning as `.settings-ui-section--page-flow`'s "Flat variant"
   block further down this file (written for the AI Assistant tab): CSS rather than
   an `@jini-ai/ui` change, since the shared shell has no `flat`/`chromeless` prop.
   Scoped to this screen's own class rather than to `.settings-ui-section` itself —
   Settings, Authentication, and the placeholder tabs are the shell's other three
   consumers and keep the panel look, which is still correct for them. Unlike that
   `--page-flow` block, this leaves `.jini-tabbed-dialog-head` and
   `.jini-tabbed-dialog-content`'s own padding alone: this screen has no separate
   page header of its own (same as Settings), so the shell's title/subtitle strip
   is still this page's only heading, and `.admin-content`'s existing 2rem/2.5rem
   page padding already keeps the list off the viewport edge without help from the
   modal's internal padding. */
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog {
  background: transparent;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat);
  /* THE clipping fix (2026-09-10). `@jini-ai/ui`'s own `.jini-tabbed-dialog` is
     `display: grid` + `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr)` and declares NO
     `grid-template-columns` at all, so the shell gets one implicit `auto` column
     — and an `auto` track's MINIMUM is its items' min-content width, which a
     grid item cannot be shrunk below. Paired with the same rule's
     `overflow: hidden`, that is a silent clip rather than a scrollbar.
 
     Measured live at a 1180px viewport with the workspace chat panel open: this
     element is 488px wide, its single column resolves to 556px, and the extra
     68px — precisely the eye and trash buttons — is cut off behind the panel
     with nothing on screen to say it exists. `minmax(0, 1fr)` lets the one
     column shrink to the box that holds it, which is all this ever needed.
 
     Fixed here, scoped to this screen, rather than in `tabbed-dialog.css`:
     that file is a published `@jini-ai/ui` asset shared by Settings,
     Authentication, and the placeholder tabs, and a grid-sizing change there
     reaches every consumer. If the same clip turns up on another tab, promote
     it upstream instead of copying this rule a second time. */
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
}
 
/* Alignment fix (2026-09-10, owner report). The "Card removed" rule above only zeroed the
   MODAL's outer chrome (background/border/radius/shadow) — it deliberately left
   `.jini-tabbed-dialog-head` and `.jini-tabbed-dialog-content`'s own padding in place (see that
   rule's comment), on the reasoning that `.admin-content`'s page padding alone already kept the
   list off the viewport edge. That reasoning covered the edge case (nothing clips) but missed the
   ordinary one: those two `@jini-ai/ui` defaults (`padding: 24px 24px 12px` on the head,
   `padding: 16px 24px 22px` on the content — both are a floating dialog's own inset from ITS OWN
   border, not overridden here) STACK on top of `.admin-content`'s 32px/40px page padding rather
   than replacing it. Measured live at 1440px: the "PLUGINS" eyebrow and the row-list card both
   sat 24px right of `/admin/plugins`' flush `.page-kicker`/`.plugin-rows` at the same viewport,
   and the head's own 24px top padding pushed the whole block 24px further down the page than
   every sibling screen that renders straight into `.admin-content`.
 
   Same diagnosis and same fix as `.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-content`'s
   "Flat variant" padding-inline rule further down this file: a dialog edge that no longer exists
   should not still be indenting content away from it. Zeroed here rather than there because this
   screen was never given the `--page-flow` modifier (see the "Card removed" comment for why: it
   has no `.page-header` of its own competing with the shell's title strip, so hiding the strip —
   the other half of that variant — is not wanted here, only the padding half is).
 
   Head's `padding-top` goes to 0 so the title block starts flush with `.admin-content`'s own
   inset instead of 24px below it; its 12px `padding-bottom` is untouched — that's the gap to the
   tab strip below, not an edge inset, and removing it would just move the crowding rather than
   fix it. Both sides zero `padding-inline` rather than only the left, matching the Flat variant's
   own reasoning: a lopsided 24px right gutter with nothing on the left would read as its own new
   misalignment. Content's `padding-top`/`padding-bottom` are untouched for the same reason as the
   head's bottom padding — that's rhythm between the subtitle and the tab strip, not an edge. */
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-head {
  padding-top: 0;
  padding-inline: 0;
}
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content {
  padding-inline: 0;
}
 
/* AP-3, all widths (2026-10-21, owner report: the Installed list was cut off around "Render").
   This was phone-only; on desktop the fixed-height shell kept its own nested scroller, which
   showed the list cut mid-row at the panel's bottom edge with the page scrolling only its 88px
   spacer — the two-scroller trap the `--page-flow` block documents. Same release Skills uses
   (D-32): every shell layer takes its content height and `.admin-content` is the one scroller. */
.settings-ui-section.agent-plugins-section,
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog,
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-body,
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content {
  height: auto;
  max-height: none;
  min-height: 0;
}
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog,
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { overflow: visible; overscroll-behavior: auto; }
 
/* The "Add a plugin" and "Marketplace" tabs' "Soon" tags (`add-plugin-tab-soon.ts`), carried as each
   tab's `navHint` since `@jini-ai/ui`'s tab has no tag slot. This screen uses nav hints for nothing
   else, so they are drawn as the sidebar's `.cms-item .soon` pill beside the label rather than as a
   grey sub-line under it. Jini tokens for the light-pinned island (see this block's header).
   `display` is set because Jini hides nav hints in its phone tab strip, which dropped the pill there. */
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-text { flex-direction: row; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; }
.agent-plugins-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-text small {
  display: inline-block;
  font-size: 9px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted); border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); padding: 1px 5px; border-radius: 5px;
}
 
/* "Add a plugin" card on Agent Plugins and Plugins (owner, 2026-10-17): the drop zone ran the full
   ~1300px column on a wide screen. Capped at the shared `--form-measure` every single-column form
   uses (see `.form-measure`) and centered in the tab. Scoped to these two pages: Skills renders the
   same card and keeps its own width. */
.agent-plugins-section .install-tab-card,
.plugins-page .install-tab-card { width: 100%; max-width: var(--form-measure); margin-inline: auto; }
 
/* The one-sentence lede above the list. Replaced `.settings-ui-inert-note`'s dashed-border grey
   box: that treatment means "this control does nothing yet" everywhere else in this admin, which
   is now the opposite of true on this screen — the switch below it is live. A plain lede also
   stops the panel opening with a boxed paragraph competing with the list for first attention. */
.agent-plugins-lede {
  margin: 0 0 18px; max-width: 46rem;
  font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
 
/* Load failure and refused-toggle messages. Not `.settings-ui-inert-note` for the same reason as
   above, and given the danger token so a failure does not read as ambient help text. */
.agent-plugins-alert {
  margin: 0 0 14px; padding: 9px 12px;
  font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--jini-danger);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 6%, transparent);
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 22%, transparent);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
}
.agent-plugins-empty-note { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Installed rows (AgentPluginRow.tsx)
 
   Was one bordered `.jini-settings-section-card` per plugin, each holding a `<dl>` of stacked
   VERSION/STATUS/KEYWORDS pairs plus two labelled chip lists — three plugins came to 1275px of
   inner scroll with every field at equal weight. This is one bordered container with hairline
   dividers between rows: a list reads as a list, and one border for the whole set replaces three
   competing boxes. Nothing was dropped — keywords, portable components, and MCP server ids moved
   into the per-row detail panel below.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.agent-plugin-rows {
  margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none;
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-md);
  background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.agent-plugin-row + .agent-plugin-row { border-top: 1px solid var(--jini-border); }
 
/* Applied state, signal 1 of 3 (the state word and the switch position are the other two — colour
   alone must not carry meaning). A rail rather than a row tint: a filled row would fight the
   chips inside its own expanded panel for contrast. The "on" paint (rail, glyph, switch track) is
   `--primary` — the assistant FAB's burnt orange — not `--jini-accent`, which in this admin is a
   near-black (#363636) and made every enabled row read as black (owner, 2026-10-06). */
.agent-plugin-row { position: relative; }
.agent-plugin-row::before {
  content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; width: 3px;
  background: var(--primary);
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 140ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.agent-plugin-row[data-enabled="true"]::before { opacity: 1; }
 
/* `flex-wrap` + the summary's `--row-text-min` basis decide whether the actions fit beside the
   text (owner, 2026-10-07): while the summary keeps that much width the actions stay on its line,
   right-aligned and vertically centred; once they don't they wrap under the text, still
   right-aligned (`margin-left: auto`). 15rem is the glyph, chevron and padding (~100px) plus ~140px
   of name. Same mechanism as `.plugin-row-main` on the Plugins screen. */
.agent-plugin-row-main { --row-text-min: 15rem; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0 12px; padding: 0 14px 0 0; }
 
/* The row's summary IS its expander — one hit target for "tell me more", rather than a fourth
   control competing with the three real ones on the right. */
.agent-plugin-row-summary {
  flex: 1 1 var(--row-text-min); min-width: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
  padding: 13px 8px 13px 17px;
  border: 0; background: transparent; text-align: left; font: inherit; color: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
}
.agent-plugin-row-summary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-text) 3.5%, transparent); }
.agent-plugin-row-summary:focus-visible,
.agent-plugin-switch:focus-visible,
.agent-plugin-icon-btn:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--jini-accent); outline-offset: 2px;
}
 
.agent-plugin-row-glyph {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 34px; height: 34px;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
  background: var(--jini-bg-subtle);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
  transition: color 140ms var(--jini-ease-out), border-color 140ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
/* The glyph picks up the accent on an enabled plugin — the same accent as the rail and the switch
   track, so "on" reads as one state across the whole row rather than three unrelated details. */
.agent-plugin-row[data-enabled="true"] .agent-plugin-row-glyph {
  color: var(--primary);
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 32%, var(--jini-border));
}
 
.agent-plugin-row-text { min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.agent-plugin-row-heading { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; min-width: 0; }
.agent-plugin-row-name {
  font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 650; color: var(--jini-text-strong);
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.agent-plugin-row-version {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  font-size: 11px; font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); color: var(--jini-text-muted);
  background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill); padding: 1px 7px;
}
/* The maturity pill sits on the title line beside the version (owner, 2026-10-24): one shared
   line-height gives both chips the same box (1px padding + 1px border each), and it drops the
   sidebar `.soon` push-right, which stays as is everywhere else. The negative margin keeps the
   pill's 24px tap target without making the title line taller. */
.agent-plugin-row-maturity { flex: 0 0 auto; align-self: center; display: inline-flex; }
.agent-plugin-row-version, .agent-plugin-row-maturity .soon { line-height: 14px; }
.agent-plugin-row-maturity .soon { margin-left: 0; }
.agent-plugin-row-maturity .info-tip-icon { min-height: 0; padding-block: 3px; margin-block: -3px; }
/* One line, clamped. The full text is never lost — it is the first thing the assistant reads and
   it stays in the package's own manifest; on this screen its job is to identify the row, and a
   four-line paragraph per row is what made the old cards unscannable. */
.agent-plugin-row-desc {
  font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--jini-text-muted);
  display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 1; -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  overflow: hidden;
}
 
.agent-plugin-row-chevron {
  flex: 0 0 auto; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; color: var(--jini-text-disabled);
}
.agent-plugin-chevron-glyph { transition: transform 160ms var(--jini-ease-out); }
.agent-plugin-row-summary[aria-expanded="true"] .agent-plugin-chevron-glyph { transform: rotate(90deg); }
 
/* The hairline between the summary zone and the action zone. Without it the summary's own chevron
   read as a control floating between the description and the switch, belonging to neither — seen
   rendered before this rule existed. Two zones, one divider, and the chevron is visibly the end of
   the first one. */
/* A plugin's "Manage" entry (its own admin screens) sits against the actions divider, outside that
   column, so the switch keeps one x position down the list. */
.agent-plugin-row-manage { flex: 0 0 auto; margin-left: auto; }
/* `AgentPluginManageButton` renders nothing for a plugin with no admin screens, leaving this wrapper
   empty -- and the `+` rule below then zeroed the actions' auto margin, so on a narrow list the
   wrapped actions sat flush left and the rail clipped "Enabled" (owner report, 2026-10-21). */
.agent-plugin-row-manage:empty { display: none; }
.agent-plugin-row-manage .btn-secondary { padding: 0.3rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.8rem; }
.agent-plugin-row-manage + .agent-plugin-row-actions { margin-left: 0; }
.agent-plugin-row-actions {
  flex: 0 0 auto; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
  margin-left: auto; padding-left: 14px;
  border-left: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  align-self: stretch;
}
/* Signal 2 of 3. Fixed-width so the switch column stays put between an "Enabled" and a "Disabled"
   row — a shifting switch position reads as a layout bug while scanning down the list. */
.agent-plugin-state {
  min-width: 4.6rem; text-align: right;
  font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
.agent-plugin-row[data-enabled="true"] .agent-plugin-state { color: var(--jini-text); }
 
/* iOS-style switch. `role="switch"` + `aria-checked` in the markup; this is only its paint.
   The off track is a solid mid-grey, not `--jini-bg-subtle`: on that near-white fill the white knob
   disappeared (owner screenshot, 2026-10-06). */
.agent-plugin-switch {
  flex: 0 0 auto; position: relative;
  width: 38px; height: 22px; padding: 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border-strong);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill);
  background: var(--jini-border-strong);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 160ms var(--jini-ease-out), border-color 160ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.agent-plugin-switch-knob {
  position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px;
  width: 16px; height: 16px;
  background: var(--jini-control-thumb-bg); border-radius: 50%;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-thumb-shadow-strong);
  transition: transform 160ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.agent-plugin-switch[aria-checked="true"] {
  background: var(--primary); border-color: var(--primary);
}
.agent-plugin-switch[aria-checked="true"] .agent-plugin-switch-knob { transform: translateX(16px); }
.agent-plugin-switch:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--primary); }
/* In flight. Dimmed and inert rather than mid-travel: the position it will land on is not known
   until the server answers, and animating to the requested state first would show a position the
   server may refuse. */
.agent-plugin-switch:disabled { cursor: progress; opacity: 0.55; }
/* A provider plugin's assistant face (`AgentPluginLinkedLock`, owner 2026-10-25): a red padlock in
   the switch's column — it is switched on the Plugins page, which the padlock opens — and the row
   reads as disabled. The padlock itself stays at full strength: it is the one live control. */
.agent-plugin-linked-lock { flex: 0 0 auto; display: inline-flex; justify-content: center; width: 38px; }
.agent-plugin-linked-lock .info-tip { margin-left: 0; }
.agent-plugin-linked-lock .info-tip-icon--custom { width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: var(--r-sm); color: var(--danger); }
.agent-plugin-linked-lock .info-tip:hover .info-tip-icon--custom,
.agent-plugin-linked-lock .info-tip:focus-within .info-tip-icon--custom { color: var(--danger); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--danger) 10%, transparent); }
.agent-plugin-linked-lock .info-tip-icon--custom:focus-visible { border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
.agent-plugin-row[data-linked="true"] :is(.agent-plugin-row-glyph, .agent-plugin-row-text, .agent-plugin-state) { opacity: 0.55; }
 
.agent-plugin-icon-btn {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 28px; height: 28px; padding: 0;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
  background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: color 140ms var(--jini-ease-out), background-color 140ms var(--jini-ease-out),
    border-color 140ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.agent-plugin-icon-btn:hover:not(:disabled) {
  color: var(--jini-text-strong); background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); border-color: var(--jini-border);
}
/* Honest-disabled, and it must LOOK unavailable rather than merely fail on click — the reason is
   in `aria-describedby` and in the section footnote. Not `cursor: not-allowed`: a "no" cursor
   invites the click that produces nothing. */
.agent-plugin-icon-btn:disabled { color: var(--jini-text-disabled); cursor: default; }
 
/* Detail panel — everything the old card shouted, on request. `[hidden]` needs its own rule here
   for the reason `.cms-section-items[hidden]` above already documents: the UA stylesheet's
   `[hidden] { display: none }` loses to any `display` declared on the element itself. */
/* Indented to start at the row's TEXT column (17px summary padding + 34px glyph + 12px gap), not
   at the row's own edge — so the panel visibly belongs to the row above it rather than to the
   list. */
.agent-plugin-row-detail {
  display: grid; gap: 14px;
  padding: 2px 17px 16px 63px;
}
.agent-plugin-row-detail[hidden] { display: none; }
/* The one thing the collapsed summary clips to a line — wraps freely here, first, above every
   chip group; no clamp, no ellipsis. */
.agent-plugin-detail-description {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--jini-text);
}
/* `PlainTextBlocks` paragraphs and `- ` lists: the author's blank lines become real gaps instead
   of one wall of text. */
.agent-plugin-detail-description { display: grid; gap: 8px; max-width: 68ch; }
.agent-plugin-detail-description :is(p, ul) { margin: 0; }
.agent-plugin-detail-description ul { padding-left: 1.2em; }
.agent-plugin-detail-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 7px; }
.agent-plugin-detail-label {
  font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
.agent-plugin-chips { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
.agent-plugin-chips li {
  font-size: 12px; font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); color: var(--jini-text);
  background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill); padding: 2px 9px;
}
.agent-plugin-chips code { font: inherit; color: inherit; background: none; }
 
/* Section-wide footnotes (why uninstall is unavailable; the package format link). Separated from
   the list so they read as a footer rather than a stray trailing line — the same job the removed
   `.agent-plugins-format-note` did for one line, now doing it for the pair. */
.agent-plugins-footnotes {
  margin-top: 1.15rem; padding-top: 1.15rem;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  display: grid; gap: 6px;
}
.agent-plugins-footnotes p { margin: 0; }
 
/* Marketplace empty state — a designed nothing, not a mocked store. Centered and generously
   spaced so the panel reads as "deliberately empty" rather than "failed to load". */
.agent-plugins-marketplace-empty {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center;
  gap: 10px;
  max-width: 30rem; margin: 8px auto;
  padding: 34px 26px;
  border: 1px dashed var(--jini-border-strong); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-md);
  background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.agent-plugins-marketplace-glyph {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 54px; height: 54px; margin-bottom: 2px;
  color: var(--jini-text-disabled);
  background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill);
}
.agent-plugins-marketplace-empty h3 {
  margin: 0; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 650; color: var(--jini-text-strong);
}
.agent-plugins-marketplace-empty p { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.agent-plugins-marketplace-link { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 13px; }
 
/* Narrow LIST: the divider goes and the action cluster keeps its size; it stays on the text's line
   while `--row-text-min` still fits beside it, and wraps under the text rather than crushing it
   (owner, 2026-10-07 — this block used to stack the actions on their own line at every narrow
   width, leaving a strip of empty space beside them).
 
   A CONTAINER query, not the `@media (max-width: 700px)` this replaced (2026-09-10). That media
   query keyed on the VIEWPORT, and the thing that actually squeezes this row is the workspace chat
   panel, which takes width from the admin column while leaving the viewport exactly as wide as it
   was. Measured live at a 1180px viewport with the chat panel open: the list renders 440px wide —
   comfortably past the point the row needs to stack — while the media query, seeing 1180, never
   fired. So the row kept its one-line layout, the name truncated to "Site …", and the trash and eye
   buttons were pushed outside the clip described on `.jini-tabbed-dialog` below. Every viewport
   width the media query DID catch is a subset of what this catches, so nothing is lost by the swap.
 
   560px is where the inline layout runs out: glyph (34) + gaps + chevron (16) + the row's own
   padding (~53) + the action cluster (~207) leaves ~237px of text column, and the longest installed
   name plus its version chip needs ~170px of that. Below it, the name — the one thing a row exists
   to identify — is what starts giving way, so that is where the layout changes instead. */
.agent-plugin-rows { container-type: inline-size; container-name: agent-plugin-list; }
@container agent-plugin-list (max-width: 560px) {
  /* The row's bottom inset lives on `.agent-plugin-row-main`; the summary keeps only the rest of
     its 13px. An inline row is 13px top and bottom as before, and actions that wrapped get the
     inset under them instead of sitting on the card edge. `row-gap` only exists between lines. */
  .agent-plugin-row-main { gap: 2px 8px; padding: 0 14px 9px 0; }
  .agent-plugin-row-summary { padding: 13px 8px 4px 17px; }
  /* The text column no longer has a stable left edge once the actions stack, so the detail panel
     returns to the row's own edge and reclaims the width for its chips. */
  .agent-plugin-row-detail { padding-left: 17px; }
  .agent-plugin-row-actions {
    justify-content: flex-end; padding: 0;
    /* Beside the text or wrapped under it, a left border would cut through the wrapped line. */
    border-left: none; align-self: center;
  }
  /* A real Manage button stays on the text's line while the actions wrap under it, so the actions
     need their own auto margin back to stay right-aligned rather than start at the rail. */
  .agent-plugin-row-manage + .agent-plugin-row-actions { margin-left: auto; }
  /* Keeps its 8px gap to the switch rather than being pushed to the far edge by a `margin-right:
     auto`, which is what an earlier revision of this block did: at 440px that put the word 290px
     from the control it labels, and a state word that far from its switch stops reading as its
     label. It is signal 2 of 3 for applied state (see `.agent-plugin-row::before`) — it has to stay
     legibly attached to the other two. Only the fixed `min-width` goes, since the column no longer
     has a switch below it to stay aligned with. */
  .agent-plugin-state { min-width: 0; text-align: right; }
}
 
/* Every transition above is feedback, not spectacle, and none of it is load-bearing — the switch
   still reads its position from `aria-checked` and the state word, and the chevron from
   `aria-expanded`. So it all simply stops. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .agent-plugin-row::before,
  .agent-plugin-row-glyph,
  .agent-plugin-chevron-glyph,
  .agent-plugin-switch,
  .agent-plugin-switch-knob,
  .agent-plugin-icon-btn {
    transition: none;
  }
}
/* OD's Local CLI / BYOK toggle shows only the mode name, no second line —
 * confirmed against `od-settings-execution.png`. `ExecutionTab` renders that
 * description unconditionally (`.jini-seg-meta`, no prop to suppress it), so
 * parity is restored here rather than by forking the component. Scoped to
 * this section: `.jini-seg-title`/`.jini-seg-btn` are shared with Appearance
 * and Notifications, but only `ExecutionTab` ever emits `.jini-seg-meta`. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-seg-meta { display: none; }
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Observability screen (Observability.tsx) header history.
 
   Owner report 2026-09-12 (screenshots `12-observability-header.png` vs.
   `13-secrets-header-spacing-reference.png`): this page's header should match
   Secrets' (`Security.tsx`'s `.page-header`) — kicker top-left, title below
   it, description below THAT at full width. First pass (this block, now
   superseded) un-glued `@jini-ai/ui`'s `.jini-tabbed-dialog-head-line`
   (`tabbed-dialog.css`), which renders the active tab's title and subtitle on
   ONE baseline row (`display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px`) by
   default, so the subtitle no longer read as a caption glued to the title's
   right edge. That fixed the STACKING but not the POSITION: a follow-up
   audit measured the title still sitting 24px right / ~24px down from
   Secrets' — exactly `.jini-tabbed-dialog-head`'s own `padding: 24px 24px
   12px` dialog-chrome inset, which Secrets' borderless `.page-header` has
   none of.
 
   2026-09-13 fix: `Observability.tsx` now renders its own `.page-header` —
   the same kicker/title/description markup Secrets and `AiAssistant.tsx`
   already use — above the shell, and the shell itself opts into
   `settings-ui-section--page-flow` (below), whose `.jini-tabbed-dialog-head {
   display: none }` retires the strip these two rules used to target. Scoped
   to `.observability-section` was the right call for the stacking fix, but a
   scoped PADDING override alone would still have left the title inside the
   card's own rounded top-left corner rather than flush against the page —
   see `Observability.tsx`'s own doc comment for why the page-header move won
   out instead. Left here as history rather than deleted outright: the same
   glued-baseline default will bite the next `SettingsDialogShell` consumer
   that passes a tab `subtitle` without either fix. */
 
/* --- Page-flow variant: the shell inside a NORMALLY SCROLLING admin page ----
 *
 * Used by `features/ai-assistant/AiAssistant.tsx` and, since 2026-09-13,
 * `features/observability/Observability.tsx` (see that file's own doc comment). The
 * Settings screen owns its whole viewport, so `.settings-ui-section`'s `height: 100%` above and the shell's own
 * `height: min(720px, 90vh)` (settings-dialog.css) cooperate: the panel becomes
 * a fixed-height box whose `.jini-tabbed-dialog-content` scrolls internally.
 *
 * On a page that ALSO has its own header and scrolls normally, that same pair is
 * a trap, and the symptom is specific and confusing: content taller than the box
 * scrolls in a nested scroller while the page itself does not move, so the
 * operator scrolls down, reaches the inner scroller's end, and cannot get back
 * up because the wheel is captured by `overscroll-behavior: contain`. Reported
 * as "I can't scroll back up on the tab" — it was never a scroll-position bug,
 * it was two scroll containers where the page expected one.
 *
 * The fix is to give the shell no height of its own and let the page be the only
 * scroller. `height: auto` on all three levels, `overflow: visible` on the
 * content, and `max-height: none` so nothing reintroduces a clip.
 *
 * Deliberately a MODIFIER rather than a change to `.settings-ui-section`: the
 * Settings screen genuinely wants the fixed-height behaviour, and the tab-strip
 * rules below are all scoped to `.settings-ui-section`, so this screen needs
 * that class for its chrome while opting out of its layout. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow,
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog,
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-body {
  height: auto;
  max-height: none;
}
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog {
  width: auto;
  overflow: visible;
}
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-content {
  overflow: visible;
  /* Released with the scroller itself. Left in place it would keep swallowing
     wheel events at the boundary of an element that no longer scrolls. */
  overscroll-behavior: auto;
}
 
/* The shell's own kicker/title/subtitle strip ("SETTINGS" / the active tab's
 * title / its subtitle). Hidden in this variant because on a page that already
 * has a `.page-header` it is a SECOND heading block saying roughly the same
 * thing, and the tab strip immediately below it already names the active tab —
 * so it read as three competing titles stacked above the actual controls.
 *
 * The Settings screen keeps it, and that asymmetry is deliberate rather than an
 * oversight: `.settings-ui-section`'s own comment above records that that screen
 * has NO page header precisely so this strip can be its heading. Two screens,
 * two different owners of the same job.
 *
 * `tab.title`/`tab.subtitle` are still supplied in AiAssistant.tsx and Observability.tsx — they
 * are part of the shell's contract and feed its accessible naming; this hides the
 * visual duplicate, it does not strip the semantics. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-head {
  display: none;
}
 
/* --- Flat variant: the AI Assistant tab reads as page, not as a floating panel ---
 *
 * `settings-dialog.css` styles `.jini-tabbed-dialog` as a MODAL: its own
 * elevated background (`--jini-bg-elevated`, #fffefc), a border, a large
 * radius, and `--jini-shadow-lg`. That is right for the surface it was built
 * for — a dialog floating over a dimmed page. Rendered inline inside an admin
 * page that already has its own header and its own background, the same
 * treatment paints a near-white card on a white page: a visible seam, a shadow
 * with nothing to lift the panel off, and a second nested container around
 * content that is already inside the admin's content column.
 *
 * So the chrome is removed rather than recolored. `transparent`, not
 * `var(--bg)`, on purpose — whatever the page is standing on shows through,
 * including the dark-theme `--bg` at :root line 105, so this needs no second
 * rule per theme.
 *
 * Scoped to `--page-flow`, which `features/ai-assistant/AiAssistant.tsx` and
 * `features/observability/Observability.tsx` set. The Settings screen renders the identical
 * shell and keeps the panel look, which is correct there: it owns its whole viewport and the
 * panel IS the page.
 *
 * Upstream note: the shell has no `flat`/`chromeless` prop, so this is CSS
 * rather than a `@jini-ai/ui` change — same reasoning as the tab-strip block
 * below, and the same "delete to revert" property. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog {
  background: transparent;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat);
}
 
/* The modal's horizontal padding indents content from a dialog edge that no
   longer exists, which left the form and the tab strip hanging ~24px inside
   the page title above them. Zeroed so both align to the page's own column. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-content,
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
  padding-inline: 0;
}
 
/* Measure. The card used to bound this form; with its box gone the inputs
   inherited the full admin content column — ~1140px of text field for an API
   key, with the label at the far left and the "Show" button 1100px away from
   it. A line length nobody reads and a pointer distance nobody wants.
   Restores the constraint the card was incidentally providing, without
   restoring the card. Sibling of `.assistant-switch`'s own `max-width: 68ch`,
   set in the same spirit. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { max-width: 46rem; }
/* Recovery holds tables and empty cards, which should align with its full-width tab/header. */
