.settings-ui-section--page-flow.recovery-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { max-width: none; }
.settings-ui-section--page-flow.observability-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { max-width: none; }
.observability-page-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
.observability-queries-scroll { max-width: 100%; min-width: 0; overflow-x: auto; overscroll-behavior-x: contain; }
/* Keyed on the pane like the settings strip below (2026-10-11). */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .admin-layout .page:is(.ai-assistant-page, .observability-page) .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar,
  .admin-layout.wraps-tabs .page:is(.ai-assistant-page, .observability-page) .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
    flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; scrollbar-width: thin;
    padding-right: 0;
    mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, #000 0, #000 calc(100% - 32px), transparent);
  }
  .admin-layout .page:is(.ai-assistant-page, .observability-page) .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item { padding-inline: 6px; gap: 5px; }
  .admin-layout .page:is(.ai-assistant-page, .observability-page) .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item strong { white-space: nowrap; font-size: 12px; }
}
 
/* Vertical separation between the tab's three blocks (switch → intro → form).
   The card and `.notice` boxes were carrying this implicitly through their own
   padding and borders; flattened, everything butted together into one
   undifferentiated column of text. Explicit now, because it is real structure
   and not a side effect of boxes. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .see-more { margin-top: 1.15rem; }
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-settings-byok { margin-top: 1.5rem; }
 
/* --- Card-free credential form -------------------------------------------
 *
 * `.jini-byok-card` is a bordered, filled, 16px-padded box. On this tab it was
 * the third nested container in a row (page → panel → card) around a form that
 * is the only thing on the tab, so it framed content that had nothing to be
 * separated from. Its flex column and 14px field rhythm are what actually do
 * the layout work, and those are kept — only the box is dropped.
 *
 * `.jini-byok-card-head` (the provider name, "Google Gemini") is deliberately
 * LEFT ALONE. It looks like card chrome and is not: with the box gone it is the
 * only thing on the tab that names which provider the key below belongs to. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .jini-byok-card {
  padding: 0;
  border: none;
  background: transparent;
}
 
/* --- The API-key footer slot (`apiKeyFooter` on `ByokProviderForm`) --------
 * Test the key, see what it allows, know it saved — all directly under the key
 * field, because that is where the operator is looking when they have those
 * three questions. */
.assistant-key-footer { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; }
/* The host footer already explains server encryption and replacement. Hide only the shared
   storage hint, keeping format warnings visible and standalone forms' host hint intact. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-byok-card > .jini-field:has(+ .jini-byok-key-footer) > .jini-field-hint:not(.is-error) { display: none; }
 
.assistant-key-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
 
.assistant-key-status { font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
.assistant-save-line { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
/* --- The form footer slot (`formFooter` on `ByokProviderForm`) ------------
 * "Save settings", at the foot of the card under the fields it writes. Same column
 * layout as the key footer above — it reuses `.assistant-key-actions` and
 * `.assistant-save-line` for the row and the status line, so the two footers cannot
 * drift apart visually while being two separate controls. */
.assistant-settings-footer { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; }
 
/* --- The admin's own BYOK migration prompt (`AdminByokKeyPanel.tsx`) ------
 * A `.notice` (global) with its own action row — reused rather than styled from scratch since the
 * two callers (Settings' modal presentation and the Admin tab's page-flow presentation) already
 * agree on what a `.notice` looks like in each context. */
.admin-byok-migration p { margin: 0 0 0.6rem; }
.admin-byok-migration-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
 
/* --- One type scale for the whole tab -------------------------------------
 *
 * This tab renders two typographic systems side by side: Tovu admin copy
 * (`rem`-based, `--fg`/`--faint`) and the Jini form (`px`-based, `--jini-text`
 * tokens, 12px labels and hints). Left alone they disagree on size, color AND
 * family — the switch label at 0.95rem sat above `.muted-cell` at 0.85rem sat
 * above a 12px `.jini-field-label`, three sizes in three consecutive blocks,
 * none of them matching. It read as unfinished rather than as hierarchy.
 *
 * The Jini scale wins here because the form is the majority of the tab and the
 * one part whose sizing is not Tovu's to choose. Everything below simply joins
 * it: 12px muted body copy, 13px for the one label that is a control.
 *
 * Scoped to `--page-flow` so the Settings screen, which renders the same
 * `ExecutionTab`/`ByokProviderForm` inside its own type scale, is untouched.
 *
 * `see-more.css` deliberately sets no typography of its own (only clamp
 * mechanics), which is exactly why `.assistant-intro` can own it here. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-intro > p,
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-switch p {
  margin: 0 0 0.4rem;
  font-size: 12px;
  line-height: 1.55;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-intro > p:last-child,
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-switch p:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
 
/* The one bold thing on the tab. `600` and `--jini-text-strong` make it the
   single emphasis point now that the body copy carries no `<strong>` at all. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-switch > label {
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--jini-text-strong);
}
 
/* Breathing room between the admin switch's last line of copy and the
   Local CLI / BYOK segmented control that now follows it. Set as a margin on
   the execution block rather than on `.assistant-switch p:last-child`, because
   that paragraph rule is shared with the Visitor tab, where the spacing below
   the switch is already right and does not want changing. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-execution { margin-top: 1.25rem; }
 
/* `AssistantDaemonRestart` (`AiAssistant.tsx`) — the Local CLI daemon's manual restart control,
 * directly under the execution-mode block above. `h2`/`.muted-cell` reuse the same page typography
 * `RoadmapChecklist` does; only the spacing and the button row need their own rules. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-daemon-restart { margin-top: 1.5rem; }
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .assistant-daemon-restart h2 { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--jini-text-strong); margin: 0 0 0.35rem; }
.assistant-daemon-restart-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin: 0.5rem 0; }
 
/* Matches `.jini-field-hint`, so the toggle reads as part of the form's own
   quiet layer rather than as a link competing with the copy above it. */
.settings-ui-section--page-flow .see-more-toggle { font-size: 12px; }
 
/* --- Page mode: settings nav as a top tab strip, not a left sidebar --------
 *
 * `SettingsDialogShell` lays its body out as `grid-template-columns:
 * <sidebar> minmax(0, 1fr)` and gives the nav `flex-direction: column`. The
 * admin content column is already one sidebar deep by the time this screen
 * renders, so a second 240px column left the panel — CLI cards, connector
 * grids, MCP tables — starved of horizontal space. Re-flowing the same DOM
 * into a horizontal strip above the panel buys all 240px back.
 *
 * Pure CSS on purpose: the shell has no `orientation` prop, and the change is
 * layout-only, so nothing here needs an upstream `@jini-ai/ui` edit (which
 * would also mean a `dist` rebuild before Tovu saw it). Delete this block to
 * go back to the sidebar.
 *
 * Scoped to `--inline`: this screen's own admin-page constraint (a sidebar
 * already one column deep before the panel even starts) is what this block
 * solves, and `--inline` is the only presentation this screen mounts — the
 * modal `SettingsDialogShell` this used to also be scoped against (1040px of
 * dedicated width, no admin chrome competing for it, so it never had this
 * problem) was removed 2026-09-19 along with the "Open as dialog" button
 * that opened it.
 *
 * Semantics are deliberately unchanged: still an `<aside>` of `aria-pressed`
 * buttons, not an ARIA tablist. Painting a nav to look like tabs is not the
 * same as promising arrow-key tab semantics, and claiming the role without
 * the roving-focus behaviour would be the worse of the two. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-body {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  /* A grid item (of `.jini-tabbed-dialog`) defaults to `min-width: auto`, i.e. its content's
   * min-content width — so a wide table inside a tab grew the body past the column and panned the
   * whole page sideways (mobile catalog RC-1, Recovery at 375px: body 433px in a 351px column,
   * "Create restore point" and every "Restore" cut off). `0` keeps it to its track and lets the
   * table's own `.table-scroll` do the scrolling. */
  min-width: 0;
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  flex-direction: row;
  /* Wrap rather than scroll: 13 tabs overflow a narrow viewport, and a second
   * row costs ~38px of height, whereas an x-scroller silently hides the tail
   * of the list behind a scrollbar most people never look for. */
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: stretch;
  gap: 0 2px;
  padding: 0 var(--jini-modal-padding);
  background: transparent;
  border-right: none;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  overflow: visible;
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item {
  width: auto;
  /* Sidebar mode reserves a fixed 18px icon track so labels can't fall into
   * it (see the shell's own comment); in a row, `auto` just shrink-wraps. */
  grid-template-columns: auto auto;
  gap: 7px;
  padding: 9px 11px;
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm) var(--jini-radius-sm) 0 0;
  /* Underline sits *on* the strip's own bottom border, not below it. */
  border-bottom: 2px solid transparent;
  margin-bottom: -1px;
  color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item strong {
  white-space: nowrap;
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item.active,
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item.active:hover {
  /* The filled pill that reads as "selected" in a vertical list reads as a
   * button in a row; an underline is the tab-strip idiom for the same state. */
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--selected-text);
  border-bottom-color: var(--selected-ring);
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item.active svg,
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item.active .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-icon {
  opacity: 1;
}
 
/* Collapsing a full-width strip would hide the nav outright rather than
 * reclaim space, so the chevron has nothing left to do here. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar-toggle {
  display: none;
}
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-content {
  flex: 1 1 auto;
  min-height: 0;
}
 
/* Phones: ONE horizontally-scrolling tab row instead of the wrap above (mobile catalog P-2,
 * 2026-10-06). At 375px the wrap turned every strip into 2-4 rows — Settings' nine tabs took ~130px
 * and reordered under the underline as the active tab changed — and the strip's own
 * `--jini-modal-padding` indented it 24px from the heading. Desktop keeps the wrap and its reasoning
 * (an x-scroller hides the tail behind a scrollbar nobody looks for); on a phone a swipeable tab row
 * is the platform idiom, and the last tab cut at the edge is itself the "there is more" hint.
 * Covers both strips the admin renders: Jini's inline tabbed-dialog nav (Agent plugins, Skills,
 * AI Assistant, Authentication, Observability, Settings, Recovery) and Tovu's own `.tab-bar`
 * (Plugins, Providers, Media, Themes, Deployment, SEO, Pages — see that rule's comment for why it
 * wraps on desktop). The strip's bottom rule moves to an inset shadow because `overflow` clips
 * the nav items' `margin-bottom: -1px` overlap; an inset shadow paints under the children, so the
 * active tab's 2px underline still sits on top of the 1px rule. */
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  .tab-bar,
  /* The Jini host sheet loads later; the admin scope keeps this mobile behavior
     above its desktop wrap rule regardless of stylesheet order. */
  .admin-layout :is(.jini-page, .jini-dialog) .jini-tab-bar {
    flex-wrap: nowrap;
    overflow-x: auto;
    overflow-y: hidden;
    overscroll-behavior-x: contain;
    scrollbar-width: none;
  }
  .tab-bar::-webkit-scrollbar,
  .admin-layout :is(.jini-page, .jini-dialog) .jini-tab-bar::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
  /* Slightly tighter tab padding so the common three-tab strips (Plugins, Agent plugins) still
   * fit 375px whole instead of scrolling by a few pixels. */
  .tab-bar-item,
  .admin-layout :is(.jini-page, .jini-dialog) .jini-tab-bar-item { padding-inline: 0.7rem; flex-shrink: 0; white-space: nowrap; }
  /* Settings → User Interface → "Wrap tabs instead of scrolling" (owner, 2026-10-07; class from
     `useInterfacePreferences`): the operator opted back into the wrap, every tab visible at the
     cost of a taller strip. The inset bottom rule above stays, under the last row. */
  .admin-layout.wraps-tabs .tab-bar,
  .admin-layout.wraps-tabs :is(.jini-page, .jini-dialog) .jini-tab-bar {
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    overflow: visible;
  }
  /* Themes (Chrome check, 2026-10-11): at 390px its strip scrolled with the Code tab entirely off
     screen and nothing said more tabs were there. Same right-edge fade the AI Assistant /
     Observability strips use (above); the 32px end padding lets the last tab scroll clear of the
     fade. Not when the operator chose wrapping tabs, where nothing is hidden.
     Every `.tab-bar`, not just Themes' (2026-10-17): Plugins and Agent Plugins grew a fourth tab, so
     at 360px Marketplace sat fully off screen with the same missing cue. On a strip that fits, the
     fade covers only the empty end padding, so it is invisible there. Agent Plugins' strip is the
     Jini tabbed-dialog one; its cue is in the `@container admin-content` rule below. */
  .admin-layout:not(.wraps-tabs) .tab-bar {
    padding-right: 32px;
    mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, #000 0, #000 calc(100% - 32px), transparent);
  }
}
/* The settings-shell half of the strip above, keyed on the PANE, not the viewport (2026-10-11): with
   the nav expanded and the assistant dock open, a desktop pane is phone-narrow, and the wrap turned
   Settings' nine tabs into four rows above the form. Same one swipeable row as on a phone. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
    flex-wrap: nowrap;
    overflow-x: auto;
    overflow-y: hidden;
    overscroll-behavior-x: contain;
    scrollbar-width: none;
    padding-inline: 0;
    border-bottom: none;
    box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-divider);
  }
  .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; }
  /* The right-edge "more tabs" fade `.tab-bar` uses on phones (2026-10-17): at 360px Agent Plugins'
     Marketplace tab sat fully off screen with nothing saying the strip scrolls. Invisible on a strip
     that fits; off when the operator chose wrapping tabs. */
  .admin-layout:not(.wraps-tabs) .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
    padding-right: 32px;
    mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, #000 0, #000 calc(100% - 32px), transparent);
  }
  .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item {
    flex-shrink: 0;
    margin-bottom: 0;
    padding-inline: 8px;
  }
  .admin-layout.wraps-tabs .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-sidebar {
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    overflow: visible;
  }
}
 
/* NOTE: the "whole CLI card is the click target" fix that briefly lived here
 * now ships in `@jini-ai/ui`'s own `settings-dialog.css` (see the
 * `.jini-agent-card-main:last-child` rules there). It was a property of that
 * component's grid, not of Tovu's page, so every host had the dead zone —
 * keeping a copy here would just be a second place to update. */
 
/* --- Compensating styles for classes `settings-dialog.css` never defined ---
 *
 * Cross-referenced every `className` emitted by the seven mounted tabs'
 * source (Jini `packages/ui/src/features/{instructions,notifications,
 * privacy,language,integrations}`) against `settings-dialog.css`. Roughly
 * fifty classes are used by those components and never appear in that
 * stylesheet at all — not a naming nuance, `grep` returns zero matches. Five
 * tabs render with browser-default box/typography as a result: Instructions'
 * textarea had no card and no sizing, Notifications' toggle became a
 * full-width bar instead of a pill next to its title, Privacy's consent
 * copy showed raw `<dd>` indentation, Language's own tile concatenated
 * "English" + "en" into "Englishen" with no line break, and MCP server's
 * client picker concatenated "Claude Code" + "CLI command" the same way.
 * The last two read as outright typos, not just an unstyled control.
 *
 * This is a Jini `@jini-ai/ui` package gap, not a Tovu one — the locked
 * project decision is gaps get pushed upstream, not forked here. Written
 * anyway, scoped and using only the existing `--jini-*` tokens (never a new
 * hard-coded color), because leaving five of seven mounted tabs visibly
 * broken blocks the visual-parity pass this section exists for. Delete this
 * block once `settings-dialog.css` grows the real rules upstream — every
 * selector below matches a class already documented in this file's JSDoc
 * cross-reference, so removal is a clean no-op once Jini catches up.
 */
 
/* Card/section titles across these tabs are bare `<h4>` elements with no
   className of their own; the browser's ~1.33em block margin would otherwise
   fight every `gap` set below. */
.settings-ui-section h4 { margin: 0; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--jini-text-strong); }
 
/* `.jini-hint` — Notifications/Privacy/MCP server's helper-text class.
   `settings-dialog.css` only ever defined `.jini-field-hint`; same look. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-hint { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
/* `.jini-button` / `-ghost` / `-primary` / `-disabled` — Privacy's "Delete my
   data" and MCP server's "One-click install" use this family; the
   stylesheet only ever defined `.jini-btn` / `.jini-btn-ghost`. Mirrors that
   recipe, plus a filled variant for the one primary use. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-button {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px;
  padding: 7px 14px; font: inherit; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500;
  color: var(--jini-text); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
  cursor: pointer; text-decoration: none;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-button:hover { border-color: var(--jini-border-strong); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-button-ghost { background: transparent; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-button-primary { color: var(--jini-control-solid-ink); background: var(--jini-accent); border-color: var(--jini-accent); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-button-primary:hover { background: var(--jini-accent-hover); border-color: var(--jini-accent-hover); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-button-disabled { opacity: 0.55; pointer-events: none; }
 
/* `.jini-empty-card-error` / `-warning` — color modifiers on the already-
   defined `.jini-empty-card` (MCP server's daemon-error / prerequisite-
   missing states). */
.settings-ui-section .jini-empty-card-error {
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 45%, var(--jini-border));
  color: var(--jini-danger);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 6%, var(--jini-bg-subtle));
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-empty-card-warning {
  border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-accent) 45%, var(--jini-border));
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-accent) 6%, var(--jini-bg-subtle));
}
 
/* Instructions — `od-settings-instructions.png`: one bordered card holding
   the title, description and textarea; textarea spans the card and is
   several lines tall, not a ~80px browser-default box. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-section-card {
  margin-top: 0; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-field-block { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-instructions-input,
.settings-ui-section .jini-custom-instructions-input {
  width: 100%; min-height: 96px; box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: 10px 12px; font: inherit; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--jini-text); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
  resize: vertical;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-instructions-input:focus,
.settings-ui-section .jini-custom-instructions-input:focus {
  outline: none; border-color: var(--jini-accent);
  box-shadow: var(--jini-control-shadow-focus-accent);
}
 
/* Notifications — `od-settings-notifications.png`: title and its On/Off
   pill share one row inside a bordered card; description sits below both,
   still inside the same card. Without this, the pill's `--seg-cols: 1`
   `.jini-seg-control` stretches to the full panel width instead of sizing
   to its own label. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-subsection { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-notify-card {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px;
  padding: 14px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-notify-card-header {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-field > label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
/* AI agent tab (Chrome check, 2026-10-11; design checklist: no control wider than its content).
   The Local CLI / BYOK segmented switch spanned the whole panel (~530px for two short words) and,
   inside the selected CLI's card, Jini's narrow-strip rule (`@container (max-width: 480px)`, which
   the card always is) stretched Model and Reasoning effort to the card's full width. The switch
   now sizes to its labels (its `1fr` columns keep the two halves equal) and the stacked selects
   stay full width only up to 16rem. Three classes deep so it beats Jini's two-class rules in any
   stylesheet order. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-execution > .jini-seg-control { width: max-content; max-width: 100%; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-agent-settings :is(.jini-searchable-select, select.jini-input, .jini-agent-settings-custom) {
  max-width: min(100%, 16rem);
}
 
/* Privacy — the two choices show once, as real switches, not unstyled
   `<button>`s (the disclosure list and share/decline buttons that repeated
   them were removed 2026-10-26). */
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-privacy-toggles { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px;
  width: 100%; padding: 12px 14px; font: inherit; text-align: left;
  color: var(--jini-text); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius); cursor: pointer;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row-label { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--jini-text-strong); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row-hint { font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row-switch {
  position: relative; flex: 0 0 auto; width: 36px; height: 20px;
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill); background: var(--jini-border-strong);
  transition: background-color 120ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row-switch::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 16px; height: 16px;
  border-radius: 50%; background: var(--jini-control-thumb-bg); box-shadow: var(--jini-shadow-xs);
  transition: transform 120ms var(--jini-ease-out);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row.on .jini-toggle-row-switch { background: var(--jini-accent); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-toggle-row.on .jini-toggle-row-switch::after { transform: translateX(16px); }
 
/* Language — `od-settings-language.png`: a grid of bordered tiles, each
   title above its locale code. Without this the title and code spans sit
   on one line with no separator at all — "English" + "en" reads as
   "Englishen". */
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-grid {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr)); gap: 8px;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px;
  padding: 10px 12px; font: inherit; text-align: left;
  color: var(--jini-text); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius); cursor: pointer;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile:hover { border-color: var(--jini-border-strong); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile.active {
  border-color: var(--selected-ring);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-accent) 8%, var(--jini-bg-panel));
  color: var(--jini-accent);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile-title { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile-code { font-size: 11px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-settings-language-tile.active .jini-settings-language-tile-code { color: inherit; }
 
/* MCP server — `od-settings-mcp-server.png`: an uppercase-kicker capabilities
   card, a bordered client-picker dropdown (not a dark pill — and its name
   and method sub-label need to be on separate lines, or "Claude Code" +
   "CLI command" reads as "Claude CodeCLI command"), and a dark code block
   with the Copy button overlaid on it rather than sitting below as its own
   row. */
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-capabilities-card {
  padding: 14px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-capabilities-label {
  margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-capabilities-list {
  margin: 0; padding-left: 18px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px;
  font-size: 13px; color: var(--jini-text);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-setup-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-instruction { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-restart-note { font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-mcp-deeplink-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker { position: relative; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-trigger {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px;
  width: 100%; padding: 10px 14px; font: inherit; text-align: left;
  color: var(--jini-text); background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius); cursor: pointer;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-trigger:hover,
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-trigger.open { border-color: var(--jini-border-strong); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-meta { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; min-width: 0; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-title { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-sub { font-size: 12px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-chevron { flex: 0 0 auto; color: var(--jini-text-muted); transition: transform 120ms var(--jini-ease-out); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-popover {
  position: absolute; z-index: 20; top: calc(100% + 4px); left: 0; right: 0;
  padding: 6px; background: var(--jini-bg-elevated); border: 1px solid var(--jini-border);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius); box-shadow: var(--jini-shadow-lg);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-list { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; max-height: 260px; overflow-y: auto; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-item {
  display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px;
  padding: 8px 10px; font: inherit; text-align: left; color: var(--jini-text);
  background: transparent; border: none; border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm); cursor: pointer;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-item:hover { background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-item.active { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-accent) 10%, transparent); color: var(--jini-accent); }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-item-title { font-size: 13px; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-picker-item-sub { font-size: 11px; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
.settings-ui-section .jini-snippet-block { position: relative; }
.settings-ui-section .jini-snippet-pre {
  margin: 0; padding: 14px 16px; overflow-x: auto;
  background: var(--jini-text-strong); border-radius: var(--jini-radius);
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-snippet-code {
  font-family: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6;
  color: var(--jini-bg-panel); white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-all;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-snippet-copy-btn {
  position: absolute; top: 10px; right: 10px;
  color: var(--jini-bg-panel); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-text-strong) 60%, transparent);
  border-color: transparent;
}
.settings-ui-section .jini-snippet-copy-btn:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-text-strong) 75%, transparent); }
/* The MCP page uses the shared visible Copy label; keep it legible over its code surface. */
:root .providers-page .jini-snippet-copy-btn {
  color: var(--fg);
  background: var(--surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-strong);
}
:root .providers-page .jini-snippet-copy-btn:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
:root .providers-page .jini-snippet-copy-btn > span { display: inline; color: inherit; }
 
/* Row action menu (`RowMenu.tsx`) + confirm dialog (`ConfirmDialog.tsx`) — replaces the
   one-visible-button-per-row pattern and `window.confirm` respectively, wired into
   `Posts.tsx`/`Pages.tsx`'s Edit/Disable/Delete row actions. See both components' own file-header
   comments for the portal-to-`document.body` and native-`<dialog>` rationale; this block is just
   their visual styling on top of the existing token system. */
 
/* Icon-only trigger — quiet at rest like every other row action, but round rather than the
   rectangular outline `.list-table td button:not([class*="btn-"])` gives unclassed row buttons
   further up this file (a "⋯" glyph inside a full rectangular outline reads as a broken label,
   not a control). The `.list-table td` prefix matches that rule's own scoping technique
   (specificity (0,3,0) here vs. its (0,1,2)) so this cleanly outranks it instead of fighting it. */
.row-menu-trigger {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 30px; height: 30px; padding: 0; flex-shrink: 0;
  background: transparent; color: var(--muted); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-pill);
}
.row-menu-trigger svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }
.list-table td .row-menu-trigger { background: transparent; color: var(--muted); border-color: transparent; }
.row-menu-trigger:hover,
.row-menu-trigger[aria-expanded="true"] { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-2); opacity: 1; }
 
/* Popup — portaled to `document.body`, so this is a DOM sibling of the app root and needs its own
   `position`/`z-index` rather than relying on any ancestor's stacking context; `RowMenu.tsx` sets
   `position: fixed` inline per-instance (computed from `getBoundingClientRect()`), so only the
   static box styling and stacking live here. `z-index: 70` matches `.cms-tooltip-portal` above,
   the file's other portal-to-body element — both are transient overlays that never need to
   outrank a modal `<dialog>` (the browser's top layer always wins over any `z-index` regardless),
   and never coexist with each other. */
.row-menu-popup {
  min-width: 9rem; padding: var(--space-1);
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg); border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow); z-index: 70;
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1px;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
/* Flipped-above variant gets a shadow that reads as "resting on top of" its anchor instead of
   underneath it — a purely cosmetic tell so the flip doesn't look like a positioning bug. */
.row-menu-popup-above { box-shadow: var(--jini-overlay-menu-shadow-above); }
.row-menu-item {
  display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left;
  background: transparent; color: var(--fg-2); border: none; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  padding: 0.45rem 0.65rem; font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer;
}
.row-menu-item:hover, .row-menu-item:focus-visible { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); opacity: 1; outline: none; }
/* Warning/danger menu items reuse the shared `.btn-warning`/`.btn-danger` classes for their color
   tokens (`RowMenu`'s three-tier `tone` API) rather than a bespoke class — was
   `.row-menu-item-destructive` (danger-only, its own color literals) until this pass. Composed
   here rather than left to fight the base classes: a `RowMenu` item is portaled to
   `document.body`, so it is never a descendant of `.list-table td` and the row-scoped quiet-at-
   rest rules below (which key off exactly that ancestry) cannot reach it — and `.btn-danger`/
   `.btn-warning`'s own base rule is a bordered pill button, which painted a full red/amber outline
   at rest inside a 3-item dropdown, the same "wall of red" problem those row-scoped rules exist to
   prevent, just recreated in a new context. Chained-class selectors here (0,2,0 and up) outrank
   both `.row-menu-item` alone and `.btn-danger`/`.btn-warning` alone (0,1,0 each) regardless of
   source order, so shape stays `.row-menu-item`'s (block, full-width, menu-item padding) while
   color and hover state come from the tone. */
.row-menu-item.btn-danger, .row-menu-item.btn-warning { background: transparent; border: none; }
.row-menu-item.btn-danger { color: var(--danger); }
.row-menu-item.btn-danger:hover, .row-menu-item.btn-danger:focus-visible { background: var(--danger-bg); color: var(--danger); outline: none; }
.row-menu-item.btn-warning { color: var(--warning); }
.row-menu-item.btn-warning:hover, .row-menu-item.btn-warning:focus-visible { background: var(--warning-bg); color: var(--warning); outline: none; }
 
/* Confirm dialog — native `<dialog>`; un-styled, the UA stylesheet centers it with a system
   border/background and a plain black `::backdrop`. This replaces both with the token system but
   deliberately leaves `position`/`margin` alone, so the browser's own top-layer centering (what
   `showModal()` was chosen for in the first place) keeps doing the layout work. */
.confirm-dialog {
  border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: var(--space-6);
  max-width: 26rem; width: calc(100% - var(--space-6));
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg); color: var(--fg); box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
/* `display` lives on its own `[open]`-scoped rule rather than the bare `.confirm-dialog` rule
   above — an author-stylesheet `display` declaration always wins over the UA stylesheet's
   `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }` regardless of selector specificity (origin outranks
   specificity in the cascade), so a bare `.confirm-dialog { display: flex }` would force the
   dialog visible even while closed. Caught live in the browser, not just by reasoning about it:
   the dialog rendered open-by-default on page load until this was scoped. */
.confirm-dialog[open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4); }
.confirm-dialog::backdrop { background: var(--jini-overlay-bg);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.confirm-dialog h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.confirm-dialog-body { margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); font-size: var(--text-md); line-height: 1.5; }
.confirm-dialog-actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: var(--space-3); }
 
/* Image preview lightbox (`ImagePreviewModal`): styled entirely by Jini's shared `Lightbox`
   (`@jini-ai/ui/admin-widgets.css`, `.jini-lightbox*`) since 2026-10-21 — no host rules. */
 
/* `MessageOverflowModal.tsx` — the chat pane's "Show in modal" affordance (chat-overflow fix,
   2026-08-30). Same native-`<dialog>` foundation as `.confirm-dialog`, but sized like
   `.theme-explore-preview-dialog` instead: this shows arbitrary chat content (a wide code block, a
   full-size MCP-UI surface), not a single image with an intrinsic size to shrink-wrap to, so the
   box is sized to most of the viewport and its body scrolls independently. Close button mirrors
   `.theme-explore-preview-dialog-close`'s reasoning, not the image lightbox's (now Jini's
   `.jini-lightbox-button`): this dialog's content sits on the app's own light surface (a table, a
   code block, an MCP-UI card), so a token-based badge reads correctly there the way the lightbox's
   fixed dark-stage chip (tuned for sitting around a photograph) would not. */
.message-overflow-modal {
  position: relative;
  border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border-strong);
  border-radius: var(--r-lg);
  padding: var(--space-5);
  width: 90vw;
  height: 85vh;
  max-width: 90vw;
  max-height: 85vh;
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg);
  color: var(--fg);
  box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none);
}
.message-overflow-modal[open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.message-overflow-modal::backdrop { background: var(--jini-overlay-bg-preview);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.message-overflow-modal-body {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  overflow: auto;
}
.message-overflow-modal-close {
  position: absolute; top: var(--space-3); right: var(--space-3); z-index: 1;
  width: 2.1rem; height: 2.1rem; padding: 0; border-radius: 50%;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-2); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  font-size: 1.3rem; line-height: 1; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); cursor: pointer;
}
.message-overflow-modal-close:hover { background: var(--accent-dim); color: var(--fg-1); }
 
/* `ThemePageDetailsModal.tsx` — the Theme Pages tab's per-row "Details" info modal (2026-08-31 owner
   review pass, replacing that row's old inline "see more" disclosure). Same native-`<dialog>`
   foundation as `.confirm-dialog` above and the SAME `[open]`-scoped `display` split those rules'
   own comments explain (an author `display` rule on the bare class always wins over the UA
   stylesheet's `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }` regardless of specificity). Sized like
   `.confirm-dialog` (a fixed, content-fit box), not `.message-overflow-modal`'s viewport-filling one
   — this shows a short list of facts about one row, not arbitrary full-size content. */
.theme-page-details-dialog {
  border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: var(--space-6);
  max-width: 28rem; width: calc(100% - var(--space-6));
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg); color: var(--fg); box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.theme-page-details-dialog[open] { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
.theme-page-details-dialog::backdrop { background: var(--jini-overlay-bg);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
/* Kicker + title (2026-08-31 visual pass — `ThemePageDetailsModal.tsx`'s own header, PART 3): the
   same eyebrow/heading PAIRING `.page-header .page-kicker`/`.page-title` use for "CONTENT" →
   "Pages", re-declared under this dialog's own class names rather than reusing those two — they are
   deliberately scoped to `.page-header` (see that rule's own comment), which this dialog is not, and
   `.section-eyebrow` is unscoped but sized for a card group, not a dialog's own title. The id was
   the owner's complaint ("renders small and lowercase... reads like a stray word"): `--text-xl`
   matches `.page-title` itself rather than the previous `--text-lg` card-heading size. */
.theme-page-details-kicker {
  margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted);
}
.theme-page-details-dialog h2 {
  margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-xl); font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--fg);
}
/* File/Publish as an actual label/value grid instead of two "Label: value" sentences — the two
   facts the owner called "the most scannable... and they look like prose". `auto-fit`/`minmax` sits
   them side by side at this dialog's own width for the common short-path case (`about.html`) and
   folds to one column on its own when a longer file path needs the room, rather than truncating it. */
.theme-page-details-facts {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(9rem, 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); margin: 0;
  padding: var(--space-3) 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.theme-page-details-fact { margin: 0; min-width: 0; }
.theme-page-details-fact dt {
  margin: 0 0 2px; font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted);
}
.theme-page-details-fact dd { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg); }
.theme-page-details-fact dd code { font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--fg-2); word-break: break-all; }
/* The two explanatory asides (what Publish means, no original to reset to) — supporting detail, not
   the row's own facts above, grouped into one quiet block rather than reading as full-weight body
   prose in the middle of the dialog (the owner's "documentation pasted into a dialog" complaint). */
.theme-page-details-notes { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); margin: 0; }
.theme-page-details-muted { color: var(--muted); font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: 1.5; margin: 0; }
/* The collision warning's own body — icon beside the (unchanged) message text, action button below.
   `align-items: flex-start` plus the icon's own small top nudge keeps it lined up with the first
   line of text rather than the vertical center of however many lines it wraps to. */
.theme-page-details-collision { margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.theme-page-details-collision-body { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 0.5rem; }
.theme-page-details-collision-body p { margin: 0; }
.theme-page-details-collision-icon { flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 2px; color: var(--warning); }
.theme-page-details-collision .btn-warning { align-self: flex-start; }
/* Close/Edit — the owner's other complaint was these sat flush against the content above with no
   separation; a hairline + its own top padding (rather than relying on the dialog's own `gap` alone,
   which reads the same whether or not this is meant as a distinct footer) makes it read as one. */
.theme-page-details-actions {
  display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: var(--space-2);
  margin-top: var(--space-2); padding-top: var(--space-3); border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
}
 
/* `OverflowAwareMcpUiSurfaceCard.tsx` — the small "Show in modal" trigger under an MCP-UI surface
   that overflows its own box. `.mcpui-surface-overflow-wrap` gets no layout rules of its own
   beyond the width cap (`assistant.css`'s `.mcpui-surface-card` rule already covers the card it
   wraps); this is purely the trigger button's own look, styled like the pane's other small
   secondary actions (`.jini-chat-pane__new-thread`) rather than a new visual language. */
.mcpui-surface-overflow-expand {
  margin-top: 6px;
  padding: 4px 10px;
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--surface-2);
  color: var(--fg-2);
  font-size: 12px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.mcpui-surface-overflow-expand:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); }
 
/* Agent Plugin package inspector — Jini's exported `PreviewModalShell` supplies the accessible
   dialog/Escape/close behaviour and `CodeWithLines` supplies the read-only line-number pane. Tovu
   owns only this host layout around its compile-time source allowlist. */
/* The assistant button sits under this modal's backdrop yet still shows through at its corner; hide it while open. */
body:has(.agent-plugin-source-modal) .chat-fab { display: none; }
.agent-plugin-source-modal {
  z-index: 80;
  padding: var(--space-4);
  background: var(--jini-overlay-bg-source);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal] {
  max-width: 72rem;
  max-height: min(52rem, calc(100vh - 2rem));
  overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg);
  color: var(--fg);
  border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
/* Header: title + close on the first row, the Package files / Memory tabs wrapped onto their own
   row under the title (owner, 2026-10-06). The shell lays the header out as one flex row of title,
   tabs, actions, close; at phone width that squeezed the title into a narrow column beside the tabs
   and wasted the top third of the modal. Wrapping + `order` re-flows it without touching Jini: the
   title block claims all but the close button's width, so the tabs always break to row two. */
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-header] {
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-title-block] { order: 0; flex: 1 1 calc(100% - 3rem - 12px); min-width: 0; }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-close] { order: 1; }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-tabs] { order: 2; }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-actions] { order: 3; }
/* Nothing renders actions here; the shell's inline `display: flex` would still claim a gap. */
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-actions]:empty { display: none !important; }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-title] { font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-subtitle] { margin-top: 2px; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-close],
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  min-width: 2rem; min-height: 2rem; padding: 0.4rem;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] { position: absolute; z-index: 1; top: var(--space-3); right: var(--space-3); }
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] { width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 0; }
/* Expand puts the shell's stage itself in browser fullscreen, where the only thing behind it is
   the UA's black backdrop. The stage painted no background of its own, so the file bar went black
   with dark, unreadable text and the expand toggle became a black box (owner screenshot,
   2026-10-15). Painting the modal's surface here keeps the expanded view identical to the docked
   one; docked, it sits on that same surface and changes nothing. The template viewer shares it. */
.agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage],
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage] { background: var(--surface); color: var(--fg); }
.agent-plugin-source-browser { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(14rem, min(16rem, 24%)) minmax(0, 1fr); width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 0; }
.agent-plugin-source-files {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px;
  min-width: 0; padding: var(--space-2) 0; overflow: auto;
  border-right: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface-2);
}
.agent-plugin-source-files > .page-description { margin: 0 var(--space-3) var(--space-2); }
/* VS Code-style file tree (2026-09-29, `PackageFileTree` in `PackageFilesModal.tsx`): flat 24px
   rows, full-width highlight, indent guides drawn by one gradient on the indent spacer (a 1px line
   centred under each ancestor's chevron), names truncated with the full path as the tooltip. */
.agent-plugin-source-tree {
  --tree-indent: 12px;
  --tree-guide: var(--border-strong);
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0;
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs);
}
.agent-plugin-source-tree-row {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;
  height: 24px; min-width: 0; padding: 0 var(--space-3) 0 var(--space-2);
  color: var(--fg-2); cursor: pointer; user-select: none; outline: none;
}
.agent-plugin-source-tree-row:hover { color: var(--fg); background: var(--surface-3); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-row[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--fg); background: var(--accent-dim); font-weight: 600; }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-row:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: -1px; }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-indent {
  flex-shrink: 0; align-self: stretch;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(to right,
    transparent 0 calc(var(--tree-indent) / 2 + 1.5px),
    var(--tree-guide) calc(var(--tree-indent) / 2 + 1.5px) calc(var(--tree-indent) / 2 + 2.5px),
    transparent calc(var(--tree-indent) / 2 + 2.5px) var(--tree-indent));
}
.agent-plugin-source-tree-twistie { flex-shrink: 0; width: 16px; color: var(--muted); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon { flex-shrink: 0; color: var(--muted); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-folder { color: var(--jini-file-icon-folder); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-json { color: var(--jini-file-icon-json); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-markdown { color: var(--jini-file-icon-markdown); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-javascript { color: var(--jini-file-icon-javascript); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-typescript { color: var(--jini-file-icon-typescript); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-config { color: var(--jini-file-icon-config); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-html { color: var(--jini-file-icon-html); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-css { color: var(--jini-file-icon-css); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-image { color: var(--jini-file-icon-image); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-icon.is-shell { color: var(--jini-file-icon-shell); }
.agent-plugin-source-tree-label { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.agent-plugin-source-content { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; overflow: hidden; }
/* Header bar: title + the wrap toggle (item 1, 2026-08-31). The padding/border that used to sit
   directly on the bare `h3` now live on this row instead, so the toggle shares the same bar rather
   than stacking under the title; the 4rem right padding is still reserved space for the modal's
   absolutely-positioned fullscreen toggle (`[data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen]`), which floats
   over this corner of the pane regardless of which view is showing. On phones the tree stacks above
   this bar, so the phone block below moves the toggle down into the same reserved slot. */
.agent-plugin-source-content-header {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-3) 4rem var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.agent-plugin-source-content-header h3 {
  margin: 0; min-width: 0; font: 600 var(--text-sm)/1.4 var(--font-mono); overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.agent-plugin-source-content-header button {
  flex-shrink: 0; padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg-2); font-size: 12px; cursor: pointer;
}
.agent-plugin-source-content-header button:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); }
.agent-plugin-source-content-header button[aria-pressed="true"] {
  color: var(--fg); background: var(--surface); border-color: var(--selected-ring);
}
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto minmax(max-content, 1fr);
  flex: 1; min-height: 0; margin: 0; overflow: auto;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface); font: var(--text-xs)/1.6 var(--font-mono);
}
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer code { display: block; padding: var(--space-4); white-space: pre; }
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer .gutter {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none;
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
/* Wrap mode (item 1): one grid row per source line instead of `CodeWithLines`'s two monolithic
   `pre` blocks — see `WrappedCode` in `components/CodeView/CodeView.tsx` for why the two-block
   layout can't wrap without desyncing the gutter. `minmax(0, 1fr)` here (not the base rule's
   `minmax(max-content, 1fr)`) is the load-bearing change: `max-content` sizes the column to the
   widest *unwrapped* line, which would defeat wrapping outright. Vertical padding moves to the grid
   container itself, since CSS Grid applies container padding once around every row, not per cell —
   putting it on `.line-number`/`.line-content` instead would pad every single line. */
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer--wrap {
  grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr);
  /* Rows pack at the top. Without this the grid's default `align-content: stretch` shares the
     pane's spare height across every line, so a 5-line file spread its lines down the whole pane
     (owner screenshot, 2026-09-29). */
  align-content: start;
  padding: var(--space-4) 0;
}
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer--wrap .line-number {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none; padding: 0 var(--space-3);
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer--wrap .line-content {
  padding: 0 var(--space-4); white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
 
@media (max-width: 720px) {
  /* Phone: a thinner backdrop margin and header, and full-width tabs, so the tree and code get the room. */
  .agent-plugin-source-modal { padding: var(--space-2); }
  .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal] { max-height: calc(100dvh - 1rem); }
  .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-header] { padding: var(--space-3); }
  /* Full width, and a plugin's extra tabs (Memory, its own screens) scroll sideways instead of
     squeezing every label into an equal slice that overflows the modal at 375px. */
  .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-tabs] { flex-basis: 100%; max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; }
  .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-tabs] button { flex: 1 0 auto; white-space: nowrap; }
  .agent-plugin-source-modal { --agent-plugin-tree-pane: 11rem; }
  .agent-plugin-source-browser { grid-template-columns: 1fr; grid-template-rows: var(--agent-plugin-tree-pane) minmax(0, 1fr); }
  .agent-plugin-source-files { border-right: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
  /* The stacked tree now owns the stage's top-right corner, where the fullscreen toggle floated over
     the first tree row (owner screenshot, 2026-10-06). Drop it into the file header bar under the
     tree, beside "Wrap", in the slot that bar already reserves — the desktop placement. A fixed
     tree height (not a percentage) is what lets `top` line up with that bar. `:has` keeps the
     toggle in the corner on the Memory tab and when no file is selected, where there is no bar. */
  .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-frame]:has(.agent-plugin-source-content-header) > [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] {
    top: calc(var(--agent-plugin-tree-pane) + var(--space-3));
  }
  /* The tree sizes to its rows, capped at that same 11rem (then it scrolls), and the file viewer
     takes every pixel left (owner, 2026-10-07: with three to five files the fixed 11rem pane left a
     block of empty tree above the viewer). With the bar no longer at a fixed height, the fullscreen
     toggle is anchored to the file header bar instead and centred on it. Browsers without anchor
     positioning keep the fixed-height layout above, where the `top` arithmetic still holds. */
  @supports (anchor-name: --a) {
    .agent-plugin-source-browser { grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr); }
    .agent-plugin-source-files { max-height: var(--agent-plugin-tree-pane); }
    .agent-plugin-source-content-header { anchor-name: --agent-plugin-file-bar; }
    .agent-plugin-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-frame]:has(.agent-plugin-source-content-header) > [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] {
      position-anchor: --agent-plugin-file-bar;
      top: anchor(center);
      translate: 0 -50%;
    }
  }
}
 
/* "View Template" (2026-08-10, `TemplateSourceModal.tsx`, shared by both editors since 2026-09-24) — same `PreviewModalShell` host chrome as
   `.agent-plugin-source-modal` above, but a single stage pane rather than a file-browser grid: this
   modal has exactly one file (the chosen template), never a list to pick from. `.code-viewer` reuses
   the identical gutter/line styling `CodeWithLines` renders into, scoped under this modal's own
   ancestor since `.agent-plugin-source-content .code-viewer` above only matches inside that OTHER
   modal's markup. */
.template-source-modal {
  z-index: 80;
  padding: var(--space-4);
  background: var(--jini-overlay-bg-source);
  backdrop-filter: var(--tovu-admin-scrim-backdrop, none);
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal] {
  max-width: 60rem;
  max-height: min(44rem, calc(100vh - 2rem));
  overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-bg);
  color: var(--fg);
  border: var(--jini-border-width, 1px) solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--tovu-admin-elevated-shadow);
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-header] {
  min-height: 4rem;
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-title] { font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); font-family: var(--font-mono); }
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-subtitle] { margin-top: 2px; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-close],
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  min-width: 2rem; min-height: 2rem; padding: 0.4rem;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-fullscreen] { position: absolute; z-index: 1; top: var(--space-3); right: var(--space-3); }
/* The code box is its OWN scroller (owner screenshot, 2026-10-10). When the padded stage scrolled
   instead, the box's `max-content` grid ran past its own border, and the sticky gutter stuck to the
   stage's padding edge, so code slid by to the LEFT of the line numbers. */
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] {
  width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 0; overflow: hidden; padding: var(--space-4);
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto minmax(max-content, 1fr);
  flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow: auto;
  margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface); font: var(--text-xs)/1.6 var(--font-mono);
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
}
/* Wrap mode: the same one-row-per-line grid the plugin viewer uses (see `CodeView.tsx`). */
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer--wrap {
  grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr); align-content: start; padding: var(--space-3) 0;
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer--wrap .line-number {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none; padding: 0 var(--space-3);
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer--wrap .line-content {
  padding: 0 var(--space-4); white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer code { display: block; padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); white-space: pre; }
.template-source-modal [data-preview-modal-stage-custom] .code-viewer .gutter {
  position: sticky; left: 0; text-align: right; user-select: none;
  color: var(--faint); background: var(--surface-2); border-right: 1px solid var(--border);
}
 
/* The theme card's screenshot thumbnail, made clickable (2026-08-10 owner feedback: too small to
   read, needs a click-to-expand). A real `<button>` wrapping the `<img>`, not a bare clickable
   `<img>` — keyboard-operable and properly announced, unlike an image with only an onClick.
   Resets the global `button` rule's filled-primary chrome to transparent so it reads as "the image
   is clickable", not "there's a button over the image". */
.theme-card-preview-trigger { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; padding: 0; border: none; background: none; cursor: zoom-in; }
.theme-card-preview-trigger:hover { opacity: 1; }
.theme-card-preview-trigger img { width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; display: block; }
 
/* ============================================================
   Deployment panel (`/admin/deployment`)
   ------------------------------------------------------------
   Rewritten 2026-08-15 (second owner UI/UX pass). The first pass fixed structure — a 0px row gap,
   six stacked cards collapsed to a row list, a `.tab-bar` that clipped its last tab at 390px — but
   was written without this file's own primitives in view, so it reproduced the exact defect
   `.card-title` (~L744) was added to fix: a bare `<h2>` inside a `.card` renders at the UA default
   24px against a 26.4px `.page-title`, which that rule's own comment calls "not a hierarchy step,
   it is a near-tie". Every card heading on all five tabs was one of those. The screen therefore
   read as a stack of equally-loud boxes, each holding one sentence.
 
   The vocabulary below is borrowed, not invented — it is what the Dashboard (this admin's
   best-looking screen) already does and what Deployment was not doing: a card head with a title
   and its actions on one line, a hairline rule, then dense rows whose values sit in a predictable
   right-hand column. `--space-*`, `--text-*`, `--r-*` and the semantic color tokens throughout;
   no literals except where noted.
 
   DEPENDENCY, recorded because it crosses an authorship boundary: `.card-title` and `.card-lead`
   (~L730) were added to this file by a CONCURRENT agent during the same session as this block, and
   were still uncommitted in the working tree when this was written — `git show HEAD:…/styles.css |
   grep -c '^\.card-title'` returned 0. They are used on all five Deployment tabs and are not
   duplicated here, because a second definition of a shared primitive is how this file ended up with
   the two rival `.link-button` rules its own comment describes merging. If that block is ever
   dropped instead of committed, these tabs' headings fall back to the UA `<h2>` they had before —
   a return to the previous appearance, not a broken layout.
   ============================================================ */
 
/* Card head — title on the left, actions/status on the right, hairline below. Generic (no
   `deployment-` prefix) because it is the missing half of the `.card`/`.card-title` pair: today a
   card with a title AND a right-hand action has no primitive, which is why `DockerfileTab.tsx` was
   reaching for `.deployment-provider-row` (a Full Site row class) to lay out its Copy/Download
   buttons. Additive and opt-in, like `.card-title` itself — nothing existing takes this class.
   The negative margins pull the hairline out to the card's own edges so it reads as a divider
   between head and body rather than a short line floating inside the padding box; they are exactly
   `.card`'s own `padding` values, so they cancel rather than approximate. */
.card-head {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-4);
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  margin: calc(var(--space-5) * -1) calc(var(--space-6) * -1) var(--space-4);
  padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-6);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.card-head .card-title { margin: 0; }
/* The right-hand group. `margin-left: auto` rather than relying on `justify-content` alone so it
   still sits hard right after the row wraps at a narrow width. */
.card-head-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); margin-left: auto; }
 
/* Vertical rhythm between a tab's top-level blocks. The five tab components render a flat list of
   cards and section groups; without this each pair of siblings has whatever margin the last child
   happened to leave, which is what produced the uneven column gaps on the first pass. */
.deployment-tab { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-5); }
/* The same rhythm one level down, inside a card whose body is more than a single paragraph. Every
   spacing value on these five tabs comes from either this rule or `.deployment-tab` above, so the
   whole panel is on one scale rather than on whatever margin each element brought with it. */
.deployment-card-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4); }
/* Two related groups side by side inside one card, collapsing to a stack when there is no room —
   the same `auto-fit`/`minmax` responsive intent as `.deployment-path-grid`, at the narrower
   `minmax` a within-card column can afford. */
.deployment-split { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(18rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); }
.deployment-split > div { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); min-width: 0; }
/* A flex column stretches its children to full width by default, which is how Full Site's "View the
   Dockerfile" link rendered as a ~700px-wide button — the same defect class as the stretched status
   pill, on a different element. A button's width should come from its label. */
.deployment-split .btn-secondary { align-self: flex-start; }
 
/* ---- The two-path choice (Overview) -------------------------------------------------------- */
/* `auto-fit`/`minmax` rather than a hard `1fr 1fr`: at the narrow end the two cards stack
   full-width instead of squeezing to an unreadable column, same responsive intent `.field-row`
   already has. Grid's default `align-items: stretch` keeps both cards the same height when one
   path's copy runs longer than the other's. */
.deployment-path-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(19rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-4); }
.deployment-path-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
/* Icon + title + status pill. The icon sits in a soft rounded square (`--surface-2`, not a fill of
   `--primary`) so it reads as a quiet identifying mark rather than a second call to action — the
   two paths are peers here, and tinting one of them would be the screen picking a side it has no
   basis to pick. */
.deployment-path-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); }
.deployment-path-icon {
  display: grid; place-items: center; flex-shrink: 0;
  width: 2.25rem; height: 2.25rem; border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--fg-2);
}
.deployment-path-card .card-title { margin: 0; flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
/* Pushes the footer (link + note) to the card's bottom edge so both cards' links align on the same
   baseline even when one path's capability list is a row longer. */
.deployment-path-foot { margin-top: auto; padding-top: var(--space-2); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); align-items: flex-start; }
 
/* ---- Import & Export (Operations) ----------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Same auto-fit grid as the deployment path cards: three across on a wide screen, stacked on a
   phone. The link sits at each card's bottom so all three line up when one lead wraps longer. */
.import-export-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-4); }
.import-export-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.import-export-card .card-title { margin: 0; }
.import-export-card .card-lead { margin: 0; }
.import-export-card .btn-secondary { margin-top: auto; align-self: flex-start; }
/* Git backup: the one Import & Export card with its own flow, so it sits full-width under the grid
   (inside it, a full-row card would keep an empty fourth track beside the three link cards). */
/* `.page`'s own 24px gap already separates it from the grid; pulling back the difference leaves the
   grid's 16px row gap, so the card reads as the grid's next row rather than a 40px-away section. */
.import-export-card-wide { margin-top: calc(var(--space-4) - var(--space-6)); }
.git-backup-note { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: var(--text-sm); }
.git-backup-facts { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-1); color: var(--fg-2); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.git-backup-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2); }
.import-export-card .git-backup-actions .btn-secondary { margin-top: 0; }
 
/* ---- Capability list ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* The "what works / what doesn't" rows. Shared by the Overview comparison and the Static Site tab
   so the same fact is stated in the same shape in both places. Meaning is carried by the glyph AND
   the row's own text, never by color alone (`frontend-accessibility`): the ✓/✗ marks are distinct
   shapes with an `aria-label`, and the color is a reinforcement on top of that. */
.deployment-caps { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.deployment-caps li { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-2); font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); }
.deployment-caps-mark { flex-shrink: 0; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 1.05rem; height: 1.05rem; margin-top: 0.05rem; }
.deployment-caps-yes { color: var(--ok); }
.deployment-caps-no { color: var(--faint); }
/* An unsupported capability is stated, not struck through — the row still has to be readable, and
   `line-through` on a whole label is harder to read for exactly the users least able to spare the
   effort. The muted foreground plus the ✗ glyph is the whole signal. */
.deployment-caps li.is-off { color: var(--muted); }
 
/* ---- Fact rows (Overview diagnostics, env vars) --------------------------------------------- */
/* Label above value, hairline-separated, in an auto-fitting grid. Replaces the `.field`/`.field-row`
   pairing the first pass used: `.field` is `display: flex; flex-direction: column`, so a `.status`
   pill placed directly inside one STRETCHES to the full column width — a 4-character pill rendered
   ~400px wide, measured live at 1440px. Pills here hug their text because the row is a grid whose
   value cell contains an inline-flex pill with `justify-self` left. */
/* Separated by rhythm, not by rules. A hairline between grid cells cannot be drawn correctly here:
   `auto-fit` decides the column count from the available width, so no static `nth-child` rule knows
   which cells begin a row, and every version of "border-top except the first row" is wrong at some
   viewport width. Spacing does the grouping instead — which is also what the Dashboard's own stat
   tiles do, and they are the closest existing thing to these. */
.deployment-facts {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(15rem, 1fr));
  gap: var(--space-5) var(--space-6);
}
.deployment-fact { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); min-width: 0; }
.deployment-fact-label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
.deployment-fact-value { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg); min-width: 0; }
/* A filesystem path or other verbatim value. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` rather than a scroller: an
   absolute path has no spaces to break at, and at 390px an un-breakable one is what pushes the
   whole page into horizontal scroll. */
.deployment-fact-value code,
.deployment-code-inline {
  display: block; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs); line-height: 1.5;
  color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-sm); padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3);
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
/* `.status` is a bare `padding`/`border-radius` rule with no display of its own, so it inherits
   whatever its parent's layout gives it. Forcing `inline-flex` here is what actually makes a pill
   hug its label inside these flex/grid parents. */
.deployment-fact .status, .deployment-env-row .status, .deployment-path-head .status,
.deployment-provider-name .status, .card-head .status {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; align-self: flex-start; width: fit-content;
}
.deployment-fact .status {
  max-width: 100%;
  white-space: normal;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
 
/* A completed export/publish run's own failure detail (`failedRoutes`/`failedAssets`) — the ONE
   path in this file, the counts in `.deployment-facts` above only say how many failed. Sits below
   those counts, same `.deployment-fact-label` heading style, but a plain list rather than a grid:
   an unbounded number of rows (one per failed route/asset) would break `.deployment-facts`'s
   `auto-fit` column layout, which assumes a small, fixed set of facts. */
.deployment-failure-list { margin-top: var(--space-4); display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.deployment-failure-list ul { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-1); }
.deployment-failure-list li { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--danger); }
.deployment-failure-list li code { color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm); padding: 0 var(--space-1); }
 
/* ---- Environment variables (Overview) ------------------------------------------------------- */
/* One row per variable: monospace name and its Set/Not set pill on the first line, the consequence
   of it being unset underneath. Hairline-separated rows, the Dashboard's `.dash-activity-row`
   idiom, rather than the first pass's 4-column grid — those four notes are different lengths, so
   the grid rendered four ragged-bottomed columns with the tallest one setting a row height the
   other three left empty. */
.deployment-env-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.deployment-env-row { padding: var(--space-3) 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.deployment-env-row:first-child { border-top: none; padding-top: 0; }
.deployment-env-row:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; }
.deployment-env-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.deployment-env-name { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 500; color: var(--fg); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.deployment-env-note { margin: var(--space-1) 0 0; font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); max-width: 70ch; }
 
/* ---- Command block (Static Site) ------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* The terminal command, as something you can actually copy rather than a sentence with a command
   embedded in the prose (which is what the first pass shipped — "Run tovu export <dir> and Tovu
   writes…", unselectable as a unit and unstyled). `$` is a `::before` on the code element so it is
   NOT part of the copied text. */
/* `max-width` so the Copy button stays beside the command instead of being flung to the far edge of
   a ~1250px card — the same proximity failure the Full Site rows had, and there is no reason for a
   one-line command to occupy the full width of a desktop card. */
/* `flex-wrap` plus a flex-basis on the text: once the line wraps to several rows there is no
   sensible place for a vertically-centred button beside it — at 390px the assistant request runs
   four lines and Copy ended up floating against the middle one. Below the basis the button drops
   onto its own row, left-aligned under the text it copies. */
.deployment-command {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); max-width: 42rem; flex-wrap: wrap;
