  background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-3) var(--space-3) var(--space-4);
}
.deployment-command code { flex: 1 1 16rem; min-width: 0; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.deployment-command code::before { content: "$ "; color: var(--faint); user-select: none; }
/* The prose variant — a sentence to SAY to the assistant, not a command to run in a shell. Same
   box and same Copy control so the two read as one family, but it drops the `$` prompt and the
   monospace face, both of which would be lying about what the text is: a shell prompt in front of
   an English sentence tells the reader to type it into a terminal, where it does nothing. Kept as a
   modifier rather than a second component so the copy affordance stays identical between them. */
.deployment-command-prose code { font-family: var(--font-ui); font-size: var(--text-base); line-height: 1.5; color: var(--fg); }
.deployment-command-prose code::before { content: none; }
 
/* ---- Recommended route (Static Site) --------------------------------------------------------- */
/* The "ask the assistant" block. Borrows `.notice`'s emphasized-surface idiom (a tinted body plus a
   colored border, ~L1188) rather than inventing a second way to mark an emphasized block, but takes
   `--primary` for the accent — this is a recommendation, not a warning, and `.notice`'s own variants
   are all severity states. The word "Recommended" sits in the label above, so the accent colour is
   reinforcement and never the only thing carrying the meaning.
   FULL border, not a left-only accent rail (2026-08-31, owner's explicit call — see `.notice`'s own
   comment above for the fuller reasoning): recoloring all four sides of the already-present
   `1px solid var(--border)` to `--primary` reads as a deliberately highlighted card (the way a
   "recommended plan" is often framed with a colored outline), the same shape `.card-danger` now
   uses for its own accent, just in `--primary` rather than `--danger`. */
.deployment-route {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3);
  background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--primary); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  padding: var(--space-4);
}
.deployment-route-label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); color: var(--fg-2); }
.deployment-route-label .deployment-fact-label { color: var(--fg-2); }
/* The command block sits inside an already-tinted route block, so it flips to `--surface` to stay
   distinguishable from its parent instead of disappearing into it. `max-width` is raised rather
   than removed: the prose line is longer than a shell command, but dropping the cap entirely puts
   Copy about 1000px from the sentence it copies — the same proximity failure already fixed twice
   on this screen. */
.deployment-route .deployment-command { background: var(--surface); max-width: 48rem; }
.deployment-route .deployment-provider-list-item { padding: var(--space-3) 0; }
.deployment-route .deployment-provider-list-item:first-child { padding-top: 0; }
.deployment-route .deployment-provider-list-item > p { margin-top: var(--space-1); }
/* Quiet modifier (2026-08-16) — the CLI recommendation and the "no CLI path" note both used the base
   `.deployment-route` treatment above, the SAME strong `--primary`-accent box "Where this publish
   goes" uses for the tab's actual Preview/Publish action. Three different-weight blocks reading as
   one weight was a real cause of the owner's "it looks just awful" (`StaticSiteTab.tsx`'s own
   "Seventh pass" doc), not just the four-credential-row wall — nothing on the card stood out as more
   important than anything else. This keeps the same structure (icon+label row, tinted body,
   rounded corners) so the three blocks still read as one family, but drops the accent border and the
   tint down to a plain hairline-bordered surface, so only the block that ends in a live publish
   action keeps the strong visual claim on the reader's attention. Still a full border, not a rail
   (2026-08-31) — `border-color` recolors all four sides `.deployment-route`'s base rule already
   draws, same as that rule's own full-primary-border update just above. */
.deployment-route-quiet { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: var(--surface); }
/* The "we can't actually check this" line. It needs a rule above it: without one it sits at the
   same indent and nearly the same size as a tool row's own description, so it reads as a third
   sentence about the last tool's CLI rather than as a statement about the whole list. */
.deployment-route-note { margin: 0; padding-top: var(--space-3); border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
/* The tool's binary name, shown beside its human name — e.g. `gh`. Sized down from the row
   name so the pair reads as one label with a parenthetical, not two competing titles. */
.deployment-tool-command { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 400; color: var(--muted); }
 
/* ---- Numbered step flow (Static Site — "Getting it online") ---------------------------------
   Two steps: connect a credential, then say where this publish goes (`StaticPublishForm`'s own
   `.deployment-route`, marker "2" added inline there). Replaces THREE earlier shapes of the
   credential half in one session: an add/edit/delete list of named connections (pre-2026-08-15),
   then one always-visible row per provider (2026-08-15), then all four rows collapsed to the
   selected provider's row alone, still hidden behind an "Advanced" disclosure regardless of state
   (2026-08-16 morning). The owner's own direct read of THAT result: "Advanced" is backwards for a
   mandatory first step — a new user cannot publish anything through this form until a token is
   saved, so hiding it behind a word that means "optional, skip this" was exactly backwards. This is
   the fix: `.deployment-step` for the open, prominent not-yet-connected state (no box-within-a-box —
   a single bordered surface, not `.deployment-route`'s tinted/accented treatment, since this state
   is a real primary action rather than a recommendation or a settled fact) and
   `.deployment-step-done` for the collapsed, quiet connected state, disclosure now driven by
   `row.saved` (has this actually been done), never by `executionMode` — see
   `PublishCredentialsSection`'s own header in `StaticSiteTab.tsx` for the full story. */
.deployment-step {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4);
  padding: var(--space-4); background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-md);
}
.deployment-step-head { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-3); }
/* The number/checkmark badge — a soft rounded circle rather than `.deployment-path-icon`'s square,
   so a step marker never gets mistaken for that OTHER "icon in a quiet box" idiom this tab already
   uses for the Static/Full Site path cards. Sized to sit on the same baseline as an `<h3>`, not body
   text — it is the size of the thing it is labeling, same reasoning `kole-jain-uiux-concepts`
   gives for sizing an icon to its related text line height. */
.deployment-step-marker {
  display: grid; place-items: center; flex-shrink: 0;
  width: 1.75rem; height: 1.75rem; border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); color: var(--fg-2);
  font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 700;
}
/* The done state's marker — filled green, not just a color swap on the outline: swapping to a solid
   fill AND a checkmark glyph is a second, independent signal (shape, not just color) that this step
   is finished, matching `CapabilityMark`'s own "distinct shapes, not one shape recolored" rule.
   `--ok-solid`/`--ok-solid-ink` (falling back to `--ok`/a literal near-white) rather than plain
   `--ok`: dark mode's own `--ok` (~L74%, tuned to read as TEXT on a dark background, same family
   `.status-ok` uses) is too light to hold a white glyph on top of it, which is exactly why dark mode
   already carries a separate `--ok-solid`/`--ok-solid-ink` pair for a FILLED shape with something
   drawn on it — light mode has no such split because its `--ok` (~L48%) already works as a solid
   fill, so the fallback resolves to the right color there too. */
.deployment-step-marker-done {
  background: var(--ok-solid, var(--ok)); border-color: var(--ok-solid, var(--ok));
  color: var(--ok-solid-ink, var(--jini-status-complete-ink-fallback));
}
/* Step 2's marker sits inline in `.deployment-route-label` beside the existing text, at the smaller
   scale that row already uses — it is not its own step block, just a label prefix, so it drops the
   size/weight the standalone Step 1 marker above needs to hold its own next to an `<h3>`. */
.deployment-step-marker-inline { width: 1.375rem; height: 1.375rem; font-size: var(--text-xs); flex-shrink: 0; }
.deployment-step-headings { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-1); min-width: 0; }
.deployment-step-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.deployment-step-subtitle { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); max-width: 60ch; }
/* The done state's `<summary>` — same marker-plus-text shape as `.deployment-step-head` above, but
   as a single clickable row (native `<summary>`, cursor already signals it) rather than a
   heading-plus-subtitle pair, since a settled fact needs one line, not two. `list-style: none` +
   the `::-webkit-details-marker` reset strip the browser's own disclosure triangle — a second,
   unstyled triangle competing with the step marker at the START of the row would be the same "which
   glyph means what" confusion this whole redesign exists to remove. That triangle is not simply
   gone, though (owner-reported, 2026-08-15: the row was clickable with nothing on screen saying so)
   — `.deployment-step-summary-action` below restores a real expand affordance at the row's OTHER
   end instead, where it cannot compete with the step marker. */
.deployment-step-summary {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-3); cursor: pointer; list-style: none;
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2);
}
.deployment-step-summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
/* `flex: 1` so `.deployment-step-summary-action` is pushed to the row's far edge instead of
   trailing the timestamp mid-row. */
.deployment-step-summary-text { min-width: 0; flex: 1; }
/* The restored expand affordance — a text label plus a chevron, together, at the END of the summary
   row. A label alone doesn't say WHERE the toggle is; a chevron alone (especially unstyled) repeats
   the "mystery glyph" problem the details-marker reset exists to avoid — paired, they read as one
   unambiguous "click here to expand" the way the step marker at the start does not compete with. */
/* The "Verify" control on an already-connected row (2026-08-16 — see `CredentialStepDone`'s own doc
   for the gap this closes) — sits BETWEEN `.deployment-step-summary-text` and
   `.deployment-step-summary-action` so it never competes with either end of the row, and lives
   inside `<summary>` itself (not the `<details>` content revealed on expand) precisely because it
   has to stay reachable while the row is COLLAPSED, the row's normal resting state. `flex-shrink: 0`
   matches `.deployment-step-summary-action`'s own reasoning: this is a fixed-purpose control, not
   text that should be squeezed before the truncatable summary text gives way. `flex-wrap: wrap` lets
   the button and its inline status (Verifying…/the result/an error) drop to a second line on a
   narrow viewport instead of forcing the whole summary row wider than its card. */
.deployment-step-verify {
  display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2); flex-shrink: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-xs);
}
.deployment-step-summary-action {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-1); flex-shrink: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-xs); font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted);
}
/* Down-chevron at rest (collapsed = "more below"), rotated to point up once `<details open>` — one
   glyph rotated rather than swapped for a second icon, same approach `.cms-group-chevron` already
   uses elsewhere in this admin. */
.deployment-step-summary-action svg { transition: transform 0.16s ease; }
.deployment-step-done[open] .deployment-step-summary-action svg { transform: rotate(180deg); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .deployment-step-summary-action svg { transition: none; }
}
/* Collapsed by default (no `open` attribute — the mirror image of the not-yet-connected state,
   which renders with no `<details>` at all so it can never be collapsed). Quieter surface than the
   not-yet-connected `.deployment-step` above: `--surface-2` rather than `--surface`, and the fields
   revealed on expand sit flush with no nested border — the same "no box inside a box" flattening
   the credential row itself already had, still true now that the outer box is `.deployment-step`
   instead of the old Advanced disclosure. */
.deployment-step-done { background: var(--surface-2); }
.deployment-step-done[open] .deployment-step-summary { margin-bottom: var(--space-1); }
.deployment-step-done .deployment-credential-fields,
.deployment-step-done .deployment-action { padding-left: calc(1.75rem + var(--space-3)); }
/* Phones (2026-10-06 mobile catalog DE-1): one row left the status text a ~65px column between the
   check and the Verify / Replace token controls, wrapping one word (even a lone "·") per line. The
   text takes the whole row beside the marker; the controls wrap under it, aligned with the text.
   Container (2026-10-11): the same squeeze happens on desktop with the nav + dock open. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .deployment-step-summary { flex-wrap: wrap; row-gap: var(--space-2); }
  .deployment-step-summary-text { flex-basis: calc(100% - 1.75rem - var(--space-3)); }
  .deployment-step-summary > .deployment-step-verify { margin-left: calc(1.75rem + var(--space-3)); }
  .deployment-step-summary-action { margin-left: auto; }
}
 
/* A row's own fields, stacked — deliberately NOT `.field-row` (the shared two-up `auto-fit` grid
   every target-config field set on this tab otherwise uses). `.field-row` puts both columns of a
   grid ROW at the SAME height, which broke the one row that ever had two fields (a host's
   access token carries two hint lines and a link, its account ID one short hint) — the account ID's
   cell matched the row's full height and floated near the top of it, with the shared Save button
   below reading disconnected from a field it visually had nothing to do with. A single column can't
   have this problem regardless of field count or hint length, which is also why this is the layout
   the coming ~5-field Custom/S3 provider row will use rather than a wider grid tuned for two fields.
   `max-width` matches `.integrations-form label`'s own single-column form width elsewhere in this
   app, so an Access Token input does not stretch to the full width of its card. */
.deployment-credential-fields { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4); max-width: 28rem; }
 
/* The "or" seam between the CLI recommendation and Step 1 (`GettingItOnlineCard`'s own doc) —
   centered, quiet, and unboxed on purpose: it is punctuation between two real blocks, not a third
   block of its own. */
.deployment-route-divider { margin: 0; text-align: center; font-size: var(--text-xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--faint); }
 
/* ---- Host chips (Static Site) ---------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Four proper nouns. A bulleted `<ul>` gave each its own line and a disc marker for no reason —
   these are peers with nothing to rank, so they read better as one wrapped row of chips. Still a
   real `<ul>`/`<li>`, so it is still a list to a screen reader. */
.deployment-chips { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2); }
.deployment-chips li {
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); background: var(--surface-2);
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-pill); padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-3);
}
 
/* ---- Provider rows (Full Site) --------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* One `.card` holding six rows. Deliberately not `.settings-row`/`.settings-row-list` — those bake
   in `cursor: pointer`, hover, `:focus-visible` and `.is-selected` for a SELECTABLE list
   (`Taxonomy.tsx`'s terms), and these rows are fixed and non-interactive; carrying that affordance
   over would promise a click that does nothing.
 
   The status pill sits next to the provider's NAME, not flung to the far edge of a 1440px row by
   `justify-content: space-between` (the first pass), where it lost any visible connection to the
   thing it describes. The right-hand column is the cost instead — a value, which is what a reader
   scanning a column of rows is actually looking for, and what makes six rows differ from each
   other at a glance. */
.deployment-provider-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
.deployment-provider-list-item { padding: var(--space-4) 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.deployment-provider-list-item:first-child { padding-top: 0; border-top: none; }
.deployment-provider-list-item:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; }
.deployment-provider-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-4); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.deployment-provider-name { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: var(--space-3); min-width: 0; font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg); }
/* `tabular-nums` so the "$2–9" / "$5" / "$7" figures line up down the column instead of jittering
   with each glyph's own advance width. */
.deployment-provider-cost { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; }
.deployment-provider-list-item > p { margin: var(--space-2) 0 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); max-width: 78ch; }
 
/* ---- Dockerfile viewer ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Same font-mono treatment `.editor-body .tiptap pre` uses for a code block, bounded to a
   scrollable pane (a multi-stage Dockerfile is much taller than one screen) rather than growing the
   page. `--surface-2` + a border rather than the borderless `--surface-3` slab the first pass used:
   inside a card that is itself `--surface`, the darker fill with no edge read as a hole punched in
   the card, and it is the only element on the five tabs that did not have a border. */
.deployment-dockerfile-viewer {
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-4); max-height: 32rem; overflow: auto;
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs);
  line-height: 1.6; border-radius: var(--r-md); white-space: pre; tab-size: 2;
}
 
/* Same box as `.deployment-dockerfile-viewer` above, as a `<textarea>` instead of a `<pre><code>`
   (2026-08-15 — the tab became editable). `min-height` rather than that block's fixed `max-height`:
   a `<pre>` grows with its content up to a cap and then scrolls, but a `<textarea>` needs an
   explicit starting height to not collapse to ~2 lines, so this keeps the same 32rem the read-only
   viewer settled on as a floor and lets the operator drag it taller via `resize: vertical` — a
   fixed-height-only textarea for a file that can genuinely run to hundreds of lines would make
   editing near the bottom of a long Dockerfile a scroll-fight inside a small box. `outline` is kept
   (not suppressed) — this is real interactive editable content, and a focus ring here is exactly the
   affordance a keyboard user needs to confirm they're typing into it. */
.deployment-dockerfile-editor {
  display: block; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box;
  margin: 0; padding: var(--space-4); min-height: 32rem; resize: vertical;
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--fg); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xs);
  line-height: 1.6; border-radius: var(--r-md); tab-size: 2;
}
.deployment-dockerfile-editor:focus-visible { border-color: var(--accent); }
 
/* ---- Empty / unavailable states -------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* History has no backend at all, and Static Site's build button has no route to call. Both are
   permanent-for-now states rather than "still loading", so both get a composed block — a mark, a
   title, one sentence of what would appear here, and a real next step — instead of the two
   centered grey sentences `.empty-state` gives by default. The point is that a truthful "this
   does not exist yet" should still look deliberate. */
.deployment-empty { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center; gap: var(--space-3); padding: var(--space-8) var(--space-4); }
.deployment-empty-mark {
  display: grid; place-items: center; width: 3rem; height: 3rem; border-radius: var(--r-pill);
  background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--muted);
}
.deployment-empty-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.deployment-empty-body { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); max-width: 46ch; line-height: 1.6; }
 
/* A disabled action plus the reason it is disabled, as one unit. Without the explicit `:disabled`
   override the global `button:disabled` rule (~L243) color-mixes 30% `--primary` behind ANY
   disabled button — on `.btn-secondary` that produced a pink/mauve fill with a near-invisible
   label, which is what the Static Site tab shipped. Same specificity problem `.tab-bar-item
   :disabled` documents at ~L1934. */
.deployment-action { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-2); }
/* `--muted` (53% L, ~5.5:1 on `--surface-2`), not `--faint`. A truly `disabled` control is exempt
   from the contrast minimum; this one is `aria-disabled` and therefore still focusable and still
   something a sighted keyboard user will land on, so it is not exempt and should not look like it
   is. It still reads as inactive next to an enabled `.btn-secondary`, which is `--fg-2`. */
.deployment-action .btn-secondary[aria-disabled="true"] {
  background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--muted); border-color: var(--border);
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
.deployment-action .btn-secondary[aria-disabled="true"]:hover { background: var(--surface-2); opacity: 1; }
 
/* --- Media providers tab: neutralize Jini's warm "paper" tokens --------------
 *
 * `Media.tsx` mounts `@jini-ai/ui`'s `MediaProvidersTab` directly into this page (no
 * `TabbedDialog`/`.jini-tabbed-dialog` shell in between — unlike `AiAssistant.tsx`'s
 * `--page-flow` variant above, there is no modal chrome here to flatten). `--jini-bg-panel`
 * (`#fdfcfa`) and `--jini-bg-elevated` (`#fffefc`) are Jini's intentionally warm "paper" tokens —
 * both R>G>B, a deliberate cream — right for a dialog card floating over its own dimmed backdrop
 * (see `tabbed-dialog.css`'s own header comment). `.jini-media-provider-card`, every `.jini-input`
 * inside it, and the non-ghost `.jini-button`s (`Reload`/`Save changes` use the ghost variant and
 * are unaffected) all read `--jini-bg-panel` directly, so sitting straight on this admin's own
 * neutral white page (`--surface`, hue-powerless — see the `:root` comment atop this file) they
 * read as a faint peach/cream panel floating on a plain white one. Confirmed live: owner report,
 * "the whole thing" — not just the "Clear" button's disabled-state fix already applied in
 * `settings-dialog.css`.
 *
 * Fixed the same way that file's own header names as the override mechanism — every value there
 * resolves through a custom property, so redefining the token downstream re-skins every consumer
 * without forking a single rule — re-pointed at this admin's own `--surface`/`--surface-2`
 * (already the established neutral this admin's own `.card`/`input` use) rather than inventing a
 * new color.
 *
 * `.media-providers-panel[data-theme="light"]` (0,2,0) rather than relying on stylesheet load
 * order to beat Jini's own bare `[data-theme="light"]` (0,1,0): the class guarantees this wins
 * regardless of which stylesheet the bundler happens to inject first — the same reasoning
 * `.jini-button-ghost:disabled` used in `settings-dialog.css` for the sibling "Clear" button fix.
 * `--jini-bg-subtle` is deliberately left alone: `#f4f5f7` is already a cool/neutral grey (B>=G>R),
 * not part of the cream the owner flagged, so overriding it would be an unrequested extra change.
 * Keep this legacy pin on Classic only: Glass derives `--surface` from `--jini-bg-panel` on
 * its local scheme boundary, so the reverse alias here would create a token cycle. */
:where(:root:not([data-admin-theme]), :root[data-admin-theme="classic"]) .media-providers-panel[data-theme="light"] {
  --jini-bg-panel: var(--surface);
  --jini-bg-elevated: var(--surface);
}
/* The panel's heading and each provider card's name are bare Jini `<h4>`/`<strong>` that rendered
   16px/700 — a size above every other card title. Same 14px/600 as `.card-title` and Settings'
   `.settings-ui-section h4`. */
.media-providers-panel :is(.jini-section-head h4, .jini-media-provider-card-head > strong) {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3;
}
.deployment-action-reason { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); max-width: 60ch; }
 
/* Sites — card grid redesign (2026-09-05, owner verdict comparing this screen against Tovu
 * Runner's Projects screen: "Tovu Runner uses space better ... it shows all the sites we have up
 * front"). Replaces the previous single-column stack (a large "Now serving" panel with two
 * full-width disabled-input-styled fields, a "Create a site" panel, then a table far down the
 * page) with a compact one-line status ({@link .sites-now-serving} family below) and a responsive
 * grid of site tiles with Create as the grid's own first tile.
 *
 * `.sites-grid` uses `auto-fill`, NOT `auto-fit` — the exact choice `.theme-grid` above already
 * makes and documents: a lone site (this admin's common case, per the owner) must not have its
 * one card balloon to the grid's full width the way `auto-fit` would (it collapses unused tracks
 * into the occupied ones); `auto-fill` reserves the phantom tracks instead, so a lone card sizes
 * the same as it would in a fully populated row. */
.sites-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-4); }
 
.site-card {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  border-radius: var(--r-lg); padding: 0; overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--jini-panel-bg); border: 1.5px solid var(--jini-panel-border); box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow);
  transition: transform 0.14s, box-shadow 0.14s;
  background-image: var(--jini-panel-texture, none); backdrop-filter: var(--jini-panel-backdrop, none);
}
.site-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); }
 
/* The tinted header carries the folder name — the technical identifier every write on this screen
 * takes (Activate, the create form's own field) — as the card's dominant element, the same role
 * Tovu Runner's port number plays on its own project card. */
.site-card-head { padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5); background: var(--surface-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
.site-card-name { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); word-break: break-all; }
 
/* The one purely visual signal this redesign adds: a tint on whichever card is genuinely the live
 * binding, so it reads at a glance in a grid of several — never a substitute for the `status`
 * badge below, which states the same `siteRowState`-derived fact in words
 * ({@link resolveSiteCardClassName} in `Sites.hooks.tsx`). */
.site-card-serving .site-card-head { background: var(--primary-dim); }
 
.site-card-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-2); padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5) var(--space-5); flex: 1; }
.site-card-display-name { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-md); color: var(--fg-2); }
.site-card-meta { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-xs); color: var(--muted); }
.site-card-actions { margin-top: auto; padding-top: var(--space-2); align-self: stretch; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2); justify-content: flex-end; }
.site-card-actions [role="status"] { flex-basis: 100%; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); }
 
/* The Create tile — dashed outline, no tint, sits first in the grid (`Sites.tsx`'s own render
 * order) so creating a site reads as one more card rather than a form bolted above the list. The
 * form itself stays inline rather than opening on click, unlike Runner's own "+" tile — see
 * `CreateSiteCard`'s own doc comment in `Sites.tsx` for why. */
.site-card-create { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--border-strong); background: transparent; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat); }
.site-card-create:hover { transform: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat); border-color: var(--faint); }
.site-card-create .site-card-head { background: transparent; border-bottom: none; padding-bottom: 0; }
.site-card-create-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; }
.site-card-create-plus {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1.4rem; height: 1.4rem;
  border-radius: var(--r-pill); border: 1.5px dashed var(--border-strong); font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1; color: var(--muted);
}
.site-card-create .site-card-body { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; }
.site-card-create .field { width: 100%; }
 
/* The compact "Now serving" line (`NowServingCard` in `Sites.tsx`) — plain label/value text
 * instead of the two `.field-readonly` boxes the previous layout used, which rendered as
 * disabled-looking text inputs for a fact that is never actually editable here. `title` on the
 * value carries the untruncated string; `text-overflow: ellipsis` only clips the display at
 * narrow widths, the full text stays in the DOM. */
.sites-now-serving { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-6); }
.sites-now-serving-fact { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: var(--space-2); min-width: 0; max-width: 100%; }
.sites-now-serving-fact-label { font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); flex-shrink: 0; }
.sites-now-serving-fact-value { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--fg-2); overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; max-width: 26rem; }
.sites-now-serving-fact-value.mono { font-family: var(--font-mono); }
.sites-now-serving-notices { flex-basis: 100%; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.sites-now-serving-notices:empty { display: none; }
 
/* Sites — tab redesign (2026-09-05, owner: "the new site should be a button that says new site
 * that takes you to maybe, like, an onboarding screen ... maybe we actually need a tab system").
 * Replaces the create-form-as-a-grid-tile the previous pass shipped ("This is just awful"): the
 * grid keeps its `.sites-grid`/`.site-card` rules above unchanged, minus the `.site-card-create`
 * tile, and creating a site moves to its own tab styled below. The `.site-card-create*` rules
 * above are left in place rather than deleted — nothing else claims those class names, and the
 * card idiom they describe is the one an eventual "duplicate this site" tile would reuse. */
 
/* ---- All sites: the empty state ------------------------------------------------------------- */
/* Hit on the REAL install, not a theoretical edge: this repo's dev site folder predates the
 * `.site-meta.json` commit marker `listSites` requires, so the grid is legitimately empty while a
 * site is plainly being served. Dashed, low-contrast, and narrow — it is an invitation, not an
 * error, and the `.notice` treatments are already spoken for by things that ARE warnings. */
.sites-empty {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-3);
  max-width: 34rem; padding: var(--space-8) var(--space-6);
  border: 1.5px dashed var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-lg);
}
.sites-empty-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.sites-empty-lead { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-md); color: var(--muted); }
.sites-empty-action { margin-top: var(--space-2); }
 
/* ---- Create a site: the onboarding screen (Tovu Runner port) --------------------------------- */
/* Ported from Runner's `onboarding`/`onboarding-card`/`onboarding-section` shape at the owner's
 * direction — one card running Site details -> Database -> actions, reached from a header button
 * and titled as its own screen. Runner's CSS itself is NOT ported: every value below is one of this
 * admin's own tokens, so the screen inherits Tovu's palette, radii, and type ramp rather than
 * carrying Runner's in alongside them.
 *
 * A narrow measure, deliberately. The rejected first pass squeezed this form into a grid cell; the
 * opposite failure — a short form stretched across a 1440px admin — reads just as badly. 40rem is
 * wide enough for the database cards' two-line hints without letting any line run past a
 * comfortable measure. */
.back-link {
  /* `gap`, not a trailing space in the arrow's own span — HTML collapses that space away, which
     rendered the link as "←All sites" with the two run together. */
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; align-self: flex-start; gap: var(--space-1);
  margin-bottom: var(--space-3); padding: 0;
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); text-decoration: none; background: none; border: none;
}
.back-link:hover { color: var(--fg); }
 
.onboarding { max-width: 40rem; }
.onboarding-card {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  background: var(--surface); border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); overflow: hidden;
}
/* Hairline-separated bands rather than separate cards: Runner's sections read as one continuous
   setup sheet, and three floating cards would compete with the site grid's own card idiom on the
   view right next door. */
.onboarding-section { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-4); padding: var(--space-6); }
.onboarding-section + .onboarding-section { border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.onboarding-section-head { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-1); }
.onboarding-section-title { margin: 0; font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-lg); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.onboarding-section-lead { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
/* A folder name is a path segment, not prose — the same monospace `.site-card-name` already uses
   for the identical string, so a name looks the same while being typed as it will once it is a
   card. */
.site-name-input { font-family: var(--font-mono); }
 
/* The footer carries the restart truth beside the buttons, Runner's own `onboarding__actions`
   arrangement. Tinted rather than hairline-separated so the commit point reads as the end of the
   sheet rather than a fourth question. */
.onboarding-actions {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3);
  padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-6); background: var(--surface-2); border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.onboarding-actions-note { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
.onboarding-actions-buttons { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: var(--space-3); }
 
/* ---- Create a site: the database picker ------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Three options, exactly one of which this product can deliver. The two it cannot are SHOWN — the
 * owner asked for Runner's picker, and hiding an unbuilt option teaches nothing — with their
 * unavailability stated in words inside the card, because a control that is merely greyed out
 * reads as a bug or a permissions problem. Nothing here is load-bearing for the guarantee itself:
 * the hook refuses unavailable selections and `createSite()` takes no dialect, so styling is never the
 * thing standing between a choice and a lie (see `CreateSiteOnboarding.tsx`'s own header). */
.site-db-options { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
.site-db-option {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; gap: var(--space-3); align-items: start;
  padding: var(--space-4); border: 1.5px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--surface);
}
.site-db-option input[type="radio"] { margin-top: 0.15rem; }
.site-db-option.is-selected { border-color: var(--selected-ring); background: var(--primary-dim); }
/* Dashed, flat, and not-allowed — the visual vocabulary this stylesheet already used for "a
   placeholder, not a thing yet", carried over to the two options that genuinely are ones. */
.site-db-option.is-unavailable { border-style: dashed; background: transparent; cursor: not-allowed; }
.site-db-option.is-unavailable .site-db-option-name { color: var(--muted); }
.site-db-option-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); min-width: 0; }
.site-db-option-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); flex-wrap: wrap; }
.site-db-option-name { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: var(--text-base); font-weight: 700; color: var(--fg); }
.site-db-option-note { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
/* A vendor's credential fields, present so the shape of the eventual flow is visible and inert so
   they cannot collect a credential this product has nowhere to put. Indented under their own option
   with a top rule, so they read as belonging to that vendor rather than to the question. */
.site-db-vendor {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3);
  margin-top: var(--space-1); padding-top: var(--space-3); border-top: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.site-db-vendor .field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-2); }
.site-db-vendor .field-label { display: block; }
.site-db-vendor input { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; }
.site-db-vendor .field-hint { display: block; }
/* An optional service the new site can connect with a pasted token: no radio, so one column. */
.site-db-option.is-token { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
 
/* Container (2026-10-11): keyed on the pane, not the viewport. 30.5rem ≈ the old 32rem viewport
   minus a phone's 2 × 12px page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 30.5rem) {
  .onboarding-section { padding: var(--space-5) var(--space-4); }
  .onboarding-actions { padding: var(--space-4); }
  .onboarding-actions-buttons { flex-direction: column-reverse; }
  .onboarding-actions-buttons > button { width: 100%; }
  .sites-empty { padding: var(--space-6) var(--space-5); }
}
 
/* Sites — compact square cards (2026-09-05). The owner removed the page-level "Now serving" panel
 * and asked for the space back: "It should just be a card in all sites with a green active button.
 * So we save some space. And then we also have the folder, just a regular square card with a hover
 * tooltip for the actual folder directory."
 *
 * Three changes, all overriding the `.sites-grid`/`.site-card` block far above rather than editing
 * it (this stylesheet is append-only for concurrent work):
 *
 * 1. Narrower tracks. 16rem -> 12rem, so a typical admin width fits four cards where it fit two.
 * 2. `aspect-ratio: 1`. A grid item's `min-height` still resolves to `auto`, so the square is a
 *    FLOOR, not a clamp: a long folder name or a pending badge grows the card instead of clipping.
 *    That is why the aspect goes here and not on a fixed `height`.
 * 3. The state badge moves into the card head, alone. The head used to carry the folder name; the
 *    name is now the body's first line, which lets the green `Serving now` pill read as the card's
 *    own status strip — the "green active button" of the brief — without a second row of chrome.
 *
 * The absolute path is a `title` on `.site-card` itself (`resolveSiteCardTitle`), so hovering
 * anywhere on the card reveals the directory. `title` is this screen's established idiom for that
 * exact value — the panel this replaced already used one on its own truncated path. */
.sites-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(12rem, 1fr)); }
 
/* Lifecycle controls and Trash selection must stay visible when a square cannot fit them. */
.site-card { aspect-ratio: 1; min-height: min-content; }
.site-card-head { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: var(--space-3) var(--space-4); }
.site-card-body { gap: var(--space-1); padding: var(--space-4); }
.site-card-name { font-size: var(--text-md); line-height: 1.3; }
 
/* `word-break: break-all` (inherited from the rule above) is right for a long unbroken folder name
 * but would also break a two-word display name mid-word, so the subtitle opts out. */
.site-card-display-name { font-size: var(--text-sm); word-break: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
 
/* The "this folder is not a real site directory" badge. Deliberately a quiet warning pill rather
 * than the full-width amber banner it replaced — the fact has to survive (`tovu serve` would refuse
 * this folder), but it is a footnote on one card, not a page-level alarm. */
.site-card-flag { margin-top: var(--space-1); cursor: help; }
 
/* Page-level facts about the PROCESS — the TOVU_SITE_DIR override and any pending choice. Collapses
 * completely when there is nothing to say, so the grid sits directly under the page header on the
 * normal path rather than behind a permanently-reserved gap. */
.sites-process-notices { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-3); }
.sites-process-notices:empty { display: none; }
.sites-process-notices > * { align-self: stretch; }
.sites-process-notices > .status { align-self: flex-start; }
 
/* Below roughly a phone's width the square becomes a liability: a 1-column grid would render one
 * enormous square. Two narrow tracks, aspect released. Container (2026-10-11): the pane's width,
 * not the viewport's; 28.5rem ≈ the old 30rem viewport minus a phone's page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 28.5rem) {
  .sites-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(9rem, 1fr)); }
  .site-card { aspect-ratio: auto; }
}
 
/* The square is a floor, so on a short card (one badge, no display name) the content sat at the top
 * with the action pinned to the bottom and a band of dead space between them. Two `auto` margins
 * split that free space evenly instead — above the name and below the badges — which centers the
 * identity block in the card and leaves the action on the baseline. */
.site-card-name { margin-top: auto; }
 
/* Sites — the card's status strip (2026-09-06, owner, from a screenshot of `/admin/sites?tab=all`:
 * a pink/blush header band holding a "Serving now" pill, then the name, a "Not initialized" pill,
 * and a disabled "Serve after restart" button crammed into a narrow box — "two status pills saying
 * different things stacked above each other is the core confusion").
 *
 * Measured before changing anything: the band was `--primary-dim` — this admin's burnt orange at
 * 10% over white, which is the blush she is seeing — under a GREEN `.status-ok` pill: two colors
 * making one statement, and disagreeing about it. The second pill is `.site-card-flag`, the
 * registration footnote (`resolveSiteRegistrationBadge`): a warning-toned `.status` in the same
 * pill chrome as the state badge two lines above it, so a reader sees two peers ("Serving now",
 * "Not initialized") and has to work out which one is the card's state. The button is painted by
 * the global `button:disabled` peach tint — the same rule `.btn-danger:disabled` and
 * `.settings-ui-section button:disabled` each already carry an override for.
 *
 * Three changes, all overriding the `.site-card*` blocks above rather than editing them (this
 * stylesheet is append-only for concurrent work). No markup fact moves: the same two facts render,
 * in the same order, from the same functions.
 *
 * 1. The HEAD IS the status strip. The state badge keeps its tone class (so `siteRowStateToneClass`
 *    still decides the color) but drops the pill chrome — no fill, no padding — and gains a dot in
 *    `currentColor`; the BAND takes the tone instead: `--ok-bg` for the serving card (the "green
 *    active" strip the owner asked for on 2026-09-05), `--warning-bg` for a pending restart,
 *    `--surface-2` otherwise. One statement, one color (`kole-jain`: color for purpose, and derive
 *    the background from the semantic color rather than adding an unrelated one). The dot is
 *    `aria-hidden` by construction — a `::before` with no text — so the accessible name is still
 *    the words.
 * 2. The FLAG is a footnote, not a peer. `.site-card-flag` loses the pill fill and becomes a small
 *    warning-colored line with a glyph (`SiteFlagIcon`, `sites-visuals.tsx`) — the shape says
 *    "note about this folder", the pill above it says "state". Same words, same `title` tooltip;
 *    the glyph plus the text keeps the meaning off color alone (`frontend-accessibility`).
 * 3. The disabled Activate button goes quiet. Transparent, faint text, hairline border — the
 *    treatment `.deployment-action .btn-secondary[aria-disabled="true"]` already uses for the
 *    identical "this action does not apply to this card" case. (0,3,1) beats the global (0,1,1). */
.site-card-head .status {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2);
  padding: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent;
  font-size: var(--text-xs); letter-spacing: 0.01em;
}
.site-card-head .status::before {
  content: ""; width: 0.5rem; height: 0.5rem; border-radius: 50%;
  background: currentColor; flex-shrink: 0;
}
.site-card-serving .site-card-head { background: var(--ok-bg); border-bottom-color: transparent; }
.site-card-head:has(.status-warning) { background: var(--warning-bg); border-bottom-color: transparent; }
 
.site-card-flag {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-1);
  padding: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent;
  font-size: var(--text-xs); font-weight: 600; color: var(--warning);
  white-space: normal; text-align: left;
}
.site-card-flag svg { width: 0.875rem; height: 0.875rem; flex-shrink: 0; }
 
/* Sites — card polish (2026-10-08, owner: "make sure it looks good UI-wise", from a screenshot of
 * four equal-weight buttons wrapping into a ragged right-aligned pile, the fourth clipped by the
 * square card, and Delete sitting beside Start).
 *
 * Overrides the `.site-card*` blocks above (this stylesheet is append-only for concurrent work):
 *
 * 1. The square goes. `aspect-ratio: 1` plus `overflow: hidden` is what clipped "Make default"; a
 *    card now sizes to its content with a shared floor, and grid rows stretch, so every card in a
 *    row has the same height. Wider tracks (15rem) give a name and two buttons room; one column on
 *    a phone.
 * 2. Top-down reading order: pill, name, muted meta, then the action row pinned to the bottom. The
 *    old `margin-top: auto` on the name (which centered a short card's identity) is undone — with
 *    equal-height rows it made names float at different heights across a row.
 * 3. The action row is left-aligned: the one primary action first, the "⋯" overflow trigger
 *    pushed to the far edge. The trigger gets a hairline border so it reads as a control beside a
 *    bordered button, and the same 34px height as the buttons so the row shares a baseline.
 * 4. A crashed process tints the strip red, the same `:has()` pattern the warning strip uses.
 * 5. No hover lift. The card itself is not clickable — its buttons are — so lifting it on hover
 *    promised an action that does not exist, and moved the "⋯" trigger under the pointer. */
.sites-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15rem, 1fr)); gap: var(--space-4); }
.site-card { aspect-ratio: auto; min-height: 10.5rem; }
.site-card:hover { transform: none; box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow); }
.site-card-name { margin-top: 0; }
.site-card-body { gap: var(--space-1); padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5); }
.site-card-meta { font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); }
.site-card-actions {
  margin-top: auto; padding-top: var(--space-4);
  display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-start; gap: var(--space-2);
}
.site-card-actions > :is(button, a) { height: 37px; padding: 0 0.9rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }
.site-card-open { gap: 0.35em; text-decoration: none; }
.site-card-menu { margin-left: auto; display: inline-flex; }
.site-card-menu .row-menu-trigger { width: 37px; height: 37px; border-color: var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-sm); }
.site-card-head:has(.status-error) { background: var(--danger-bg); border-bottom-color: transparent; }
.site-card-select {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); margin-top: var(--space-2);
  font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--muted); cursor: pointer;
}
.site-card-trashed .site-card-name { color: var(--fg-2); }
/* Container, same threshold and reason as the two-track rule above (2026-10-11). */
@container admin-content (max-width: 28.5rem) {
  .sites-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  .site-card { min-height: 0; }
}
 
/* Sites — card preview (2026-10-08, owner: "the desktop app shows a picture of each site").
 * A fixed 16:10 band on top of every card — the capture's own 1280×800 shape — so cards keep equal
 * heights whether or not a capture exists yet. `object-fit: cover` anchored top-left: a site's
 * header and hero are what identify it. The placeholder is a quiet surface with the folder's
 * initial, never a broken-image glyph (`useSiteCardPreview` swaps a failed load for it). */
.site-card-preview {
  position: relative; aspect-ratio: 16 / 10; flex: none; overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--surface-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
}
.site-card-preview img {
  display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: top left;
}
.site-card-preview-placeholder {
  position: absolute; inset: 0; display: grid; place-items: center;
  font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--text-xl); font-weight: 700; color: var(--faint);
}
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Plugins screen (Plugins.tsx) — the `.tovu-plugin` runtime family's row list,
   independent of `.agent-plugin-row*` above (that block belongs to the sibling
   Agent Plugins screen). Same row shape, different tokens: this screen stays a
   plain `.page`, so it uses Tovu's own `--surface`/`--fg`/`--border` set rather
   than Jini's `--jini-*` tokens, which only redefine inside a `data-theme`-
   pinned Jini island this screen never opts into.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.plugin-rows {
  container-type: inline-size; container-name: plugin-list;
  margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none;
  border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-md);
  background: var(--surface);
  overflow: hidden;
}
.plugin-row + .plugin-row { border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
/* The row `?plugin=` names (a linked agent plugin's padlock opened this page): an inset ring, so it
   never shifts the list. */
.plugin-row[data-focused="true"] { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--primary); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 6%, transparent); }
/* `flex-wrap` + the summary's `--row-text-min` basis are what decide whether the actions fit
   beside the text (owner, 2026-10-07): while the summary keeps at least that much width the actions
   stay on its line, right-aligned and vertically centred; once they don't fit they wrap under the
   text, still right-aligned (`margin-left: auto`). Wide lists never reach the wrap point. */
.plugin-row-main { --row-text-min: 10rem; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0 12px; padding: 0 14px 0 0; }
 
.plugin-row-summary {
  flex: 1 1 var(--row-text-min); min-width: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
  padding: 13px 8px 13px 17px;
  border: 0; background: transparent; text-align: left; font: inherit; color: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
  border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.plugin-row-summary:hover { background: var(--surface-2); }
.plugin-row-summary:focus-visible,
.plugin-icon-btn:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid var(--accent-text); outline-offset: 2px;
}
 
.plugin-row-glyph {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 34px; height: 34px;
  color: var(--muted);
  background: var(--surface-3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-sm);
}
.plugin-row[data-enabled="true"] .plugin-row-glyph {
  color: var(--accent-text);
  border-color: var(--accent-text);
}
 
.plugin-row-text { min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.plugin-row-heading { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; min-width: 0; }
.plugin-row-name {
  font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 650; color: var(--fg);
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.plugin-row-version {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  font-size: 11px; font-family: var(--font-mono, monospace); color: var(--muted);
  background: var(--surface-3); border: 1px solid var(--border);
  border-radius: var(--r-pill); padding: 1px 7px;
}
.plugin-row-subline {
  font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--muted);
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
 
.plugin-row-chevron { flex: 0 0 auto; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; color: var(--faint); }
.plugin-chevron-glyph { transition: transform 160ms ease; }
.plugin-row-summary[aria-expanded="true"] .plugin-chevron-glyph { transform: rotate(90deg); }
 
/* The hairline between the summary zone and the action zone — same reasoning
   `.agent-plugin-row-actions` documents: without it the chevron reads as floating between the
   subline and the action, belonging to neither. */
.plugin-row-actions {
  flex: 0 0 auto; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
  margin-left: auto; padding-left: 14px;
  border-left: 1px solid var(--border);
  align-self: stretch;
}
 
.plugin-icon-btn {
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 28px; height: 28px; padding: 0;
  color: var(--fg-2);
  background: transparent;
  border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--r-sm);
  cursor: pointer;
}
.plugin-icon-btn:hover:not(:disabled) {
  color: var(--danger); background: var(--danger-bg); border-color: var(--danger);
}
/* Honest-disabled — built-in plugins have no on-disk artifact for this route to remove. Must LOOK
   unavailable rather than merely fail on click; the reason lives in `aria-describedby` and the
   section-wide note above the list. */
.plugin-icon-btn:disabled { color: var(--faint); cursor: default; }
 
/* Downloaded's two Remove notes, as compact helper text between the tabs and the list (owner,
   2026-10-07). Under the list they read as page body copy, each with a full paragraph margin. The
   negative margins trim `.page`'s 24px flex gap so the notes sit with the tabs and the list. */
.plugins-remove-notes { display: grid; gap: 2px; margin: calc(-1 * var(--space-2)) 0 calc(-1 * var(--space-3)); }
.plugins-remove-notes > p { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-sm); line-height: 1.45; color: var(--muted); }
 
/* Detail panel — quarantine + `errors[]`, moved here from the pre-split table's own always-visible
   columns. `[hidden]` needs its own rule for the reason every other `[hidden]` panel in this file
   documents: the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` loses to any `display` declared on
   the element itself — this panel has none, so this is defensive, matching the sibling screen's
   identical rule. Indented to the row's own text column (17px summary padding + 34px glyph + 12px
   gap), so it visibly belongs to the row above it. */
.plugin-row-detail { display: grid; gap: 10px; padding: 2px 17px 16px 63px; }
.plugin-row-detail[hidden] { display: none; }
/* The always-present facts (PL-2): a compact two-column label/value list, labels in the muted
   small-caps-free style the subline uses so the panel reads as reference, not as a form. */
.plugin-row-facts { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 4px 14px; margin: 0; font-size: 12.5px; line-height: 1.45; }
.plugin-row-fact { display: contents; }
.plugin-row-fact dt { color: var(--muted); }
.plugin-row-fact dd { margin: 0; color: var(--fg-2); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
 
/* A chat dock can make this list narrow on a wide viewport. Respond to the list's own width so
   names, versions and actions retain separate space when the dock or sidebar is open. */
@container plugin-list (max-width: 700px) {
  /* The row's bottom inset lives on `.plugin-row-main` and the summary keeps only the rest of its
     12px, so a row whose actions sit inline is 12px top and bottom as before, while actions that
     wrapped get the row inset under them instead of sitting flush on the card edge. The 2px
     `row-gap` only exists between wrapped lines. */
  .plugin-row-main { gap: 2px 8px; padding: 0 12px 10px 0; }
  .plugin-row-summary { padding: 12px 12px 2px; gap: 10px; }
  .plugin-row-text { flex: 1; }
  .plugin-row-heading { flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .plugin-row-name { white-space: normal; overflow: visible; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .plugin-row-subline { white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .plugin-row-version { max-width: 100%; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .plugin-row-detail { padding-left: 12px; padding-right: 12px; }
  /* No divider here: the actions either sit beside the text or wrap under it, and a left border
     would cut through the wrapped line. */
  .plugin-row-actions { flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-end; padding: 0; border-left: none; gap: 8px; align-self: center; }
}
/* At phone width the decorative package glyph is what truncated the name ("Word Co…"); the row's
   own action ("Disable"/"Enable") already states on/off, so the glyph's border tint is redundant. */
@container plugin-list (max-width: 480px) {
  .plugin-row-glyph { display: none; }
  /* Downloaded's three actions (view, Enable, remove) still fit beside a 10rem summary at 390px,
     which squeezed "Content Analyzer" onto two lines with its version and subline stacked under it
     (owner 2026-10-16). Sized to its own one-line text instead, the summary keeps the actions beside
     it only when name, version and subline fit unbroken; otherwise the actions wrap under it. */
  .plugin-row-summary { flex-basis: auto; }
}
 
.site-card-actions .btn-secondary:disabled {
  background: transparent; color: var(--faint); border-color: var(--border);
}
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Observability screen (Observability.tsx) — scoped to `.observability-section`
   so none of these touch any other `.settings-ui-section`/`.jini-*` consumer.
   Same reasoning as the Agent Plugins block above: this screen pins
   `data-theme="light"` on its own wrapper and uses Jini's own `--jini-*`
   tokens throughout, never Tovu's `--muted`/`--fg`/`--surface`. ------------ */
 
.observability-section .jini-tabbed-dialog-content { max-width: 46rem; }
 
.observability-section .jini-tabbed-dialog {
  background: transparent;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 0;
  box-shadow: var(--jini-panel-shadow-flat);
}
 
.observability-lede {
  margin: 0 0 14px; max-width: 44rem;
  font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--jini-text-muted);
}
 
.observability-alert {
  margin: 0 0 14px; padding: 9px 12px;
  font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--jini-danger);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 6%, transparent);
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--jini-danger) 22%, transparent);
  border-radius: var(--jini-radius-sm);
}
 
/* The current-status card — one glance answers "is anything being recorded right now". The dot is
   the ONLY color-only signal, backed by the headline's own words (`Observability.tsx`), same
   "color plus text, never color alone" rule the Sites screen's own status dot documents. */
.observability-status-card {
  display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 10px;
  margin: 14px 0; padding: 12px 14px;
  border: 1px solid var(--jini-border); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-md);
  background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.observability-status-dot {
  flex-shrink: 0; margin-top: 5px;
  width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 50%;
}
.observability-status-card--on .observability-status-dot { background: var(--jini-success); }
.observability-status-card--off .observability-status-dot { background: var(--jini-text-disabled); }
.observability-status-headline { margin: 0 0 2px; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--jini-text-strong); }
 
/* Providers empty state — a designed nothing, not a mocked connection form. Same treatment as
   `.agent-plugins-marketplace-empty` above, for the identical reason: centered and generously
   spaced so the panel reads as "deliberately empty" rather than "failed to load". */
.observability-providers-empty {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center;
  gap: 10px;
  max-width: 30rem; margin: 8px auto;
  padding: 34px 26px;
  border: 1px dashed var(--jini-border-strong); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-md);
  background: var(--jini-bg-panel);
}
.observability-providers-glyph {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 54px; height: 54px; margin-bottom: 2px;
  color: var(--jini-text-disabled);
  background: var(--jini-bg-subtle); border-radius: var(--jini-radius-pill);
}
.observability-providers-empty h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 650; color: var(--jini-text-strong); }
.observability-providers-empty p { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.55; color: var(--jini-text-muted); }
 
/* Recent errors tab: its rules (and their "why") moved to `features/observability/recent-errors.css`,
   imported by `recent-errors-panel.tsx`. */
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Phone card rows for every `.list-table` (mobile catalog P-4, 2026-10-06).
   At 375px the desktop tables sat in a 351px `.table-scroll` holding 400-770px of columns: the
   right-hand cells — usually the row actions, "More", or the only link into a record — were
   off-screen with no hint, and narrow columns wrapped one word per line. Below 640px each row
   becomes a card instead, with no per-screen markup: the primary cell (the first one, or the one
   after a lone select-checkbox) is the title; a trailing cell holding a control (button, link,
   select) is the actions slot, pinned beside the title; every other cell flows underneath as a
   labelled meta line. `useListTableCellLabels` (App shell) supplies each cell's `data-label` from
   its header. The header row itself shrinks to whatever is still useful on a phone — sort buttons
   and a select-all checkbox — and disappears when it has none of those.
   `table.list-table` (0,1,1) so this outranks per-table desktop rules like `.form-fields-table`'s
   `min-width: 720px` regardless of which stylesheet loads last.
   Container, not viewport (2026-10-11): a desktop pane squeezed to ~590px by the expanded nav and
   the open dock had the same off-screen actions column, so the cards follow the pane's width.
   `useListTableCellLabels` sets `data-label` at every width, so nothing JS-side is phone-gated.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  .table-scroll:has(> table.list-table) { overflow-x: visible; }
  table.list-table { display: block; min-width: 0; table-layout: auto; }
  table.list-table > colgroup { display: none; }
  table.list-table > thead,
  table.list-table > tbody { display: block; }
 
  table.list-table > thead:not(:has(button, input)) { display: none; }
  table.list-table > thead > tr { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 0 4px; padding: 2px 6px; background: var(--surface-2); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
  table.list-table > thead > tr > th { display: block; border: 0; padding: 8px; background: transparent; }
  table.list-table > thead > tr > th:not(:has(button, input)) { display: none; }
  /* A select-all checkbox alone read as an empty grey bar (owner, Trash, 2026-10-07). Its label
     already carries the translated screen-reader text ("Select every item shown"); on a phone that
     text is shown beside the box, and the whole label is the tap target. */
  table.list-table > thead > tr > th label:has(> input[type="checkbox"]) { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 44px; cursor: pointer; }
  table.list-table > thead > tr > th label:has(> input[type="checkbox"]) > .visually-hidden {
    position: static; width: auto; height: auto; margin: 0; overflow: visible; clip: auto; white-space: normal;
    font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: normal; text-transform: none; color: var(--muted);
  }
 
  table.list-table > tbody > tr { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px 12px; padding: 12px 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
  /* Forces the meta cells onto their own line(s) under the title + actions. A flex item via its
     own `order`: it lands after the actions slot (also order 1, earlier in source). */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr::after { content: ""; order: 1; flex: 0 0 100%; height: 0; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td { display: block; order: 2; min-width: 0; padding: 0; border: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:empty { display: none; }
 
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child,
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) + td {
    order: 0; flex: 1 1 0; font-weight: 600; color: var(--fg);
  }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) { flex: 0 0 auto; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:last-child:not(:first-child):has(button, a, select) {
    order: 1; margin-left: auto; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 6px;
  }
 
  /* Meta line: "LABEL value". Not on the title, the actions slot or a lone checkbox. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td[data-label]::before {
    content: attr(data-label); margin-right: 6px;
    font-size: var(--text-2xs); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted);
  }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child::before,
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) + td::before,
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:last-child:not(:first-child):has(button, a, select)::before { content: none; }
 
  /* Each meta cell is its own "LABEL | value" line, labels in one fixed-width column (owner,
     2026-10-07). As inline "LABEL value" runs side by side, the pairs wrapped wherever the line
     ran out: a label at the end of one line and its value at the start of the next, and a
     multi-line value (Forms' "Created / Updated") pushing its neighbours out of line. The label
     is a float pulled into the cell's own left padding (a hanging indent), not a grid column:
     the value's children stay in ordinary flow however many there are, every value line keeps
     the indent, and `flow-root` grows the cell when a long label wraps to two lines. Excluded:
     the title, the actions slot, editable cells (label above, below) and colspan detail rows. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td[data-label]:not(:first-child, :first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) + td, :last-child:has(button, a, select), :has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select), [colspan]) {
    --list-meta-label-w: 7.5rem;
    flex: 0 0 100%; display: flow-root; padding-left: calc(var(--list-meta-label-w) + 12px); line-height: 20px;
  }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td[data-label]:not(:first-child, :first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) + td, :last-child:has(button, a, select), :has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select), [colspan])::before {
    float: left; width: var(--list-meta-label-w); margin: 0 0 0 calc(-1 * (var(--list-meta-label-w) + 12px)); line-height: 20px;
  }
  /* A button value (Collections' "Copy embed code") is 44px tall on phones: centre the label on it. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td[data-label]:not(:first-child, :first-child:has(input[type="checkbox"]) + td, :last-child:has(button, a, select), :has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select), [colspan]):has(> button)::before { line-height: 44px; }
 
  /* Editable rows (the form builder's field table, FO-3): a cell holding a text control gets its
     label ABOVE the control and a share of the line, so a field reads as a small labelled form —
     including the primary cell, whose control is otherwise anonymous. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select) { flex: 1 1 140px; font-weight: inherit; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select)::before { display: block; margin: 0 0 4px; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child:has(> input:not([type="checkbox"]), > select)::before { content: attr(data-label); }
  /* An inline detail row (Users' expanded panel spans every column) now gets the card's width,
     not the old table's — its own controls must not keep a desktop min-width past it. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td[colspan] :is(select, input) { max-width: 100%; }
}
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Phone tap targets (mobile catalog P-3, 2026-10-06). Measured at 375px: checkboxes 16x16, sort
   headers 13px tall, row ⋮ triggers 30x30, menu-item ↑/↓/× and chip buttons 24-26px, "Remove"
   26px tall — all well under the ~40px a fingertip needs. One floor for every button-like control
   in the page body instead of per-screen patches. Raised to 44px (2026-10-14): at 40 this floor
   out-ranked the 44px touch targets (Media's action buttons) it was meant to back up. Modal
   dialogs render in <body>, outside `.admin-content`, so `.jini-dialog` is named too: their
   fields and Cancel/Save buttons measured 35-37px. Not on `[role="switch"]`: the pill switches
   draw their own fixed-size track.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  :is(.admin-content, .jini-dialog) :is(button, select, summary, [role="button"], a.btn-primary, a.btn-secondary, a.btn-ghost):not([role="switch"]) {
    min-height: 44px;
  }
  :is(.admin-content, .jini-dialog) :is(button, [role="button"]):not([role="switch"]) { min-width: 44px; }
  :is(.admin-content, .jini-dialog) :is(input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"]) { width: 20px; height: 20px; }
 
  /* OB-1 (also Settings Privacy): a touch-synthesized hover must not leave an inactive tab
     looking pressed. The active underline and keyboard focus outline still convey state. */
  .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item,
  .settings-ui-section .jini-tabbed-dialog--inline .jini-tabbed-dialog-nav-item:hover {
    background: transparent;
  }
 
  /* TR-2, DB-1/AI-4/FO-4, PO-3, DE-3 and the dashboard activity row moved to the
     `@container admin-content` block right after this one (2026-10-11) — they are "the pane is
     narrow" layout rules, not touch rules. */
 
  /* AP-3 (the page owns scrolling on Agent Plugins) now applies at every width; see that screen's
     block ("AP-3, all widths"). */
 
  /* The drawer's active indicator belongs inside its gutter, not against the screen edge. */
  .cms-nav .cms-item.active::before { left: -6px; border-radius: var(--r-pill); }
 
  /* US-2 (card rows open from anywhere) moved to the container block below with the card layout
     itself, which is now container-based too (2026-10-11). */
 
  /* Mobile sweep 2026-10-07 (P-3 follow-up), measured at a real 375px viewport. Text inputs were
     37px against the floor buttons and selects already get; one floor for every field, the same
     44px so a field and the button beside it stay one height. */
  :is(.admin-content, .jini-dialog) input:not([type="checkbox"], [type="radio"], [type="range"], [type="color"], [type="file"], [type="hidden"]) {
    min-height: 44px;
  }
  /* Standalone links that sit beside 44px buttons (a panel head's "All posts"/"Change", a
     toolbar's "View site ↗" or "Regions →", an editor's "view ↗") were 15-19px tall. Padding that
     a matching negative margin cancels grows the hit area to ~44px without moving anything. */
  .admin-content :is(.page-toolbar, .page-actions, .themes-header-side, .dash-panel-head, .editor-slug) > a:not([class*="btn"]) {
    display: inline-block; padding-block: 13px; margin-block: -13px;
  }
  /* The pill switches keep their drawn 38x22 / 34x20 track; an invisible ring around it takes
     the tap (P-3 deliberately left `[role="switch"]` out of the min-height floor). The ring is
     measured from the padding box (36x20 inside the agent / AI Assistant switch's 1px border), so
     -12px -5px makes it 46x44 / 44x44; -10px -4px left both short of 44 tall. The AI Assistant
     switch is an `appearance: none` checkbox whose `::after` is the knob, so `::before` is free. */
  :is(.agent-plugin-switch, .theme-explore-switch, .assistant-toggle--switch input[role="switch"])::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -12px -5px; }
 
}
 
/* The layout half of the phone block above, keyed on the PANE (2026-10-11): the same rows were
   squeezed just as hard on desktop with the nav expanded and the dock open (~590px at 1280). The
   touch half (44px floors, hit-area padding, switch rings) stays viewport-only above. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  /* TR-2: bulk actions only take space once there is a selection; busy selected actions stay
     visible and disabled, so their progress does not cause the toolbar to jump. */
  .trash-toolbar[data-selection-empty="true"] .trash-bulk-action { display: none; }
 
  /* DB-1/AI-4/FO-4: short desktop rows become labelled, full-width fields on phones. */
  .database-filter-bar { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); width: 100%; }
  .database-filter-bar .field { min-width: 0; width: 100%; }
  .database-filter-bar :is(input, select) { width: 100%; min-width: 0; }
  .database-filter-bar > button { justify-self: start; }
  .settings-ui-section .jini-byok-model-row { flex-direction: column; align-items: stretch; }
  .settings-ui-section .jini-byok-model-row > .jini-field { flex: 0 1 auto; width: 100%; }
  .settings-ui-section .jini-byok-model-row > .jini-byok-test-btn { align-self: flex-start; }
 
  /* PO-3: labels start their own line; featured-image controls can still sit beside each other. */
  .page > .editor-publishing-fields { justify-content: flex-start; align-items: stretch; }
  .editor-publishing-fields > .editor-publishing-field { flex: 1 1 100%; flex-wrap: wrap; min-width: 0; }
  .editor-publishing-fields .field-label { flex-basis: 100%; text-align: left; }
  .editor-publishing-fields input { width: 100%; min-width: 0; }
 
  /* DE-3: keep the overview title intact, with the explanatory badge on the next line. */
  .deployment-path-head { flex-wrap: wrap; }
  .deployment-path-head > .status {
    flex-basis: auto;
    margin-left: calc(2.25rem + var(--space-3));
    max-width: calc(100% - 2.25rem - var(--space-3));
    white-space: normal;
  }
  .deployment-path-head > .card-title { flex-basis: calc(100% - 2.25rem - var(--space-3)); }
 
  /* A card row opens its record from anywhere on the card, not only from the ~16px-tall title
     link (US-2): the title link's `::after` stretches over the whole row, and the row's own
     controls sit above it so they still get their taps. Follows the card layout, which is
     container-based too. */
  table.list-table > tbody > tr:has(> td:first-child > a[href]) { position: relative; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:first-child > a[href]::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; }
  table.list-table > tbody > tr > td:not(:first-child) :is(a, button, select, input, label) { position: relative; z-index: 1; }
 
  /* Dashboard "Recently updated": the title took whatever the kind chip and the 16-character
     timestamp left (~125px), so most titles ended in "…", and the 16px link was the only tap
     target. The title gets its own full-width line (wrapping, never clipped), chip and time sit
     under it, and the title link's `::after` covers the row, the same idiom as US-2 above. */
  .dash-activity-row { grid-template-columns: auto minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 4px var(--space-2); position: relative; }
  .dash-activity-title { grid-column: 1 / -1; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
  .dash-activity-title::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; }
}
 
/* Container (2026-10-11): one column once the PANE is phone-narrow, whatever squeezed it.
   456px ≈ the old 480px viewport minus a phone's page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 456px) {
  .sites-grid { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
  .form-editor-panel .field-row:has(#form-name) { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
}
 
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Phone editor chrome (mobile catalog P-6/PG-3/PG-5, 2026-10-06), Page and Post editors. The
   header itself is the `.page-header-split` container rule above; this is the toolbar and the
   Save row under it.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* The toolbar row follows the PANE (2026-10-11): a desktop pane squeezed by the nav + dock needs
   the same one-row arrangement. The sticky Save row below stays phone-only: its `top` offset is
   tied to the phone's own page padding. */
@container admin-content (max-width: 620px) {
  /* Device toggle and template picker share one row (they took two, plus the view tabs' own). The
     "390px" readout goes — the pressed device icon already says which width is showing. Prefixed
     with `.page-editor-toolbar` to outrank `styles/pages.css`'s own wrap/width rules for these
     same classes whichever stylesheet loads last. */
  .page-editor-toolbar .page-editor-toolbar-end { flex-wrap: nowrap; width: 100%; justify-content: space-between; }
  .page-editor-toolbar .page-editor-toolbar-end .page-editor-width { display: none; }
  .page-editor-toolbar .page-editor-toolbar-end .editor-template-picker { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; flex-wrap: nowrap; justify-content: flex-end; }
  .page-editor-toolbar .page-editor-toolbar-end .editor-template-picker select { flex: 1 1 auto; width: auto; min-width: 0; max-width: none; }
}
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  /* Save stays in reach while scrolling a long body: the row pins under the top bar. `top` is minus
     `.admin-content`'s own phone padding-top, because sticky offsets count from the scroller's
     padding edge — at `top: 0` the body scrolled visibly through a 16px strip above the row. */
  .editor-action-row { position: sticky; top: calc(-1 * var(--space-4)); z-index: 6; background: var(--bg); padding-block: 6px; }
  /* Delete moves to the row's far left, away from Save on the right (PG-5: side by side at equal
     size they were one slip apart on a phone). */
  .editor-action-row .btn-danger { order: -2; margin-left: 0; }
}
 
/* Native fieldset/legend keeps the radio group named without adding browser-default framing.
   Float the legend into the section's content flow so it shares the existing title spacing. */
.onboarding-section.site-db-fieldset { margin: 0; min-width: 0; border: 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); }
.site-db-fieldset > legend { float: left; width: 100%; padding: 0; }
 
/* Native checklist wraps its labels and links at phone width; focus uses existing form styles. */
.assistant-permanent-deletes fieldset { min-width: 0; border: 0; padding: 0; margin: 1rem 0; }
.assistant-permanent-deletes legend { font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: .5rem; }
.assistant-permanent-deletes .permanent-delete-actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem; }
.assistant-permanent-deletes .permanent-delete-option { display: grid; gap: .25rem; margin: .75rem 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.assistant-permanent-deletes .permanent-delete-option label { display: flex; align-items: start; gap: .5rem; }
.assistant-permanent-deletes input { flex-shrink: 0; }
